  gxp_obligation_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.gxp_obligation.   primary_patent_claim_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent_claim. Business justification: Specific patent claims cover target modulation methods; claim-level tracking required for FTO clearance, licensing negotiations, and assessing blocking IP in target validation stage gates.']
  competitive_landscape_summary varchar [note: 'Summary of known competitive programs targeting this molecular target, including approved drugs, clinical-stage compounds, and disclosed research programs from competitor organizations. Business-confidential intelligence used for portfolio strategy.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this molecular target record was first created in the discovery data product. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.']
  discovery_program_code varchar [note: 'Internal program or project code under which this target is being investigated. Links the target to the broader drug discovery program for portfolio management, resource allocation, and P&L tracking.']
  disease_association varchar [note: 'Specific disease or condition(s) associated with this molecular target, as supported by published literature or internal research data. May reference ICD-10/ICD-11 disease codes or MeSH disease terms.']
  druggability_assessment varchar [note: 'Scientific assessment of the target\'s amenability to small molecule or biologic modulation based on structural, biochemical, and computational analyses. Key input to portfolio prioritization and NCE/NBE strategy decisions.']
  eln_notebook_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier to the primary Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment record in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics that documents the original target identification and characterization data. Provides full scientific audit trail.']
  ensembl_gene_code varchar [note: 'Ensembl stable gene identifier (e.g., ENSG00000146648) for the gene encoding the molecular target. Used for genomic cross-referencing, variant analysis, and bioinformatics pipelines.']
  expression_tissue varchar [note: 'Primary tissue(s) or cell type(s) where this molecular target is expressed at therapeutically relevant levels, as determined by transcriptomic or proteomic profiling (e.g., liver, lung epithelium, T-cells). Informs tissue selectivity and delivery strategy.']

  genetic_association_score decimal(5,4) [note: 'Quantitative score (0.0000–1.0000) representing the strength of genetic evidence linking this target to the associated disease, derived from GWAS, Mendelian randomization, or Open Targets Platform data. Higher scores indicate stronger genetic validation.']
  indication_code varchar [note: 'ICD-11 (International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision) code for the primary indication associated with this target. Enables standardized cross-referencing with regulatory submissions and clinical trial registries.']
  last_reviewed_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent scientific or portfolio review of this target record. Ensures data currency and supports periodic target triage processes.']
  moa_description varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the molecular mechanism by which modulation of this target is expected to produce a therapeutic effect. Captures agonism, antagonism, inhibition, activation, or allosteric modulation details as documented in ELN.']
  moa_type varchar [note: 'Categorical classification of the pharmacological mechanism of action for compounds acting on this target. Used to group targets by intervention strategy in SAR analysis and portfolio reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: agonist|antagonist|inhibitor|activator|allosteric_modulator|degrader|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  modality varchar [note: 'Preferred drug modality for targeting this molecular target based on its structural and biochemical properties. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: small_molecule|biologic|antibody|peptide|oligonucleotide|cell_therapy|gene_therapy|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  novelty_status varchar [note: 'Classification of the target\'s novelty relative to the competitive landscape. Novel targets represent first-in-class opportunities; established targets have existing approved drugs; repurposed targets are being explored in new indications.']
  organism varchar [note: 'Biological organism in which the molecular target is expressed and studied. Typically Homo sapiens for human targets, but may include model organisms used in preclinical validation studies.']
  patent_landscape_summary varchar [note: 'High-level summary of the patent landscape around this molecular target, including freedom-to-operate (FTO) considerations and known composition-of-matter or method-of-use patents. Supports IP strategy decisions.']
  pathway_name varchar [note: 'Name of the primary biological signaling or metabolic pathway in which this target participates (e.g., PI3K/AKT/mTOR, RAS/MAPK, JAK/STAT). Supports pathway-based target clustering and polypharmacology analysis.']
  pdb_code varchar [note: 'RCSB Protein Data Bank accession code for the primary 3D structure of this molecular target. Used by computational chemistry and structure-based drug design (SBDD) teams for molecular docking and virtual screening.']
  prioritization_tier varchar [note: 'Portfolio prioritization tier assigned to this target by the Target Selection Committee, reflecting strategic importance, scientific confidence, and commercial potential. Tier 1 targets receive maximum resource allocation.']
  protein_structure_available boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a resolved 3D protein structure (X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM, or NMR) is available for this target in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) or internal structural biology repository. Directly impacts structure-based drug design (SBDD) feasibility.']
  safety_concern_description varchar [note: 'Narrative description of identified safety liabilities associated with modulation of this target (e.g., hERG channel activity, hepatotoxicity risk, immunosuppression). Populated only when safety_concern_flag is True.']
  safety_concern_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether known safety liabilities or toxicological concerns have been identified for this target based on literature, genetic association studies, or internal preclinical data. Triggers mandatory safety review before progression.']
  selectivity_profile varchar [note: 'Assessment of the target\'s selectivity relative to related family members or off-target proteins. Informs compound design strategy to minimize off-target toxicity and maximize therapeutic index.']
  target_class varchar [note: 'Pharmacological class of the molecular target based on its biochemical function and structural family. Drives druggability assessment strategy and compound screening cascade design. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GPCR|kinase|nuclear_receptor|ion_channel|protease|phosphatase|epigenetic_regulator|transcription_factor|transporter|other — promote to reference product]']
  target_code varchar [note: 'Internally assigned alphanumeric business identifier for the molecular target, used as the externally-known unique code across systems (ELN, LIMS, CTMS). Distinct from the surrogate PK and from external database accession numbers.']
  target_engagement_assay varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the primary biochemical or biophysical assay used to measure compound engagement with this target (e.g., HTRF binding assay, SPR, ITC, NanoBRET). Registered in LIMS (LabWare/SampleManager) and ELN.']
  target_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable scientific name of the molecular target (e.g., EGFR, BRAF, PD-L1, CDK4/6). Serves as the primary identity label used by research scientists and in ELN records within IDBS/Dotmatics.']
  target_owner varchar [note: 'Name or employee identifier of the principal scientist or research team lead responsible for this molecular target within the discovery organization. Accountable for target validation decisions and data quality.']
  target_type varchar [note: 'Biological molecule type of the target (e.g., protein, enzyme, receptor, ion channel, nucleic acid). Determines the modality of drug intervention and screening assay design. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: protein|enzyme|receptor|ion_channel|nucleic_acid|lipid|carbohydrate|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Primary therapeutic area or disease domain for which this target is being investigated (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular). Aligns with the company\'s portfolio strategy and pipeline reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_disease|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_disease|metabolic|respiratory|other — promote to reference product]']
  uniprot_accession varchar [note: 'Universal Protein Resource (UniProt) accession number uniquely identifying the protein target in the global UniProtKB database. Enables cross-referencing with external biological databases and regulatory submissions.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this molecular target record. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change detection, and audit trail maintenance per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  validation_completion_date date [note: 'Date on which target validation studies were completed and the target was formally declared validated (in vitro or in vivo). Marks the transition from target identification to hit-to-lead progression stage.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle stage of target validation, reflecting the level of scientific evidence supporting the target\'s role in disease. Drives go/no-go decisions for hit-to-lead progression. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: identified|hypothetical|validated_in_vitro|validated_in_vivo|clinically_validated|deprioritized — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Master record for biological molecular targets identified during drug discovery, including proteins, enzymes, receptors, ion channels, and nucleic acids. Captures target class, gene name, UniProt/Ensembl identifiers, mechanism of action (MOA), therapeutic area relevance, target validation status, druggability assessment, and disease association. Authoritative SSOT for all target identification data entering the discovery pipeline from IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.'
}

  logp decimal(8,4) [note: 'Logarithm of the octanol-water partition coefficient (LogP), a measure of the compound\'s lipophilicity. Critical SAR and ADME parameter used to predict membrane permeability, oral bioavailability, and CNS penetration. Lipinski Rule of Five threshold: LogP ≤ 5.']

  molecular_formula varchar [note: 'Empirical molecular formula of the compound expressed using Hill notation (e.g., C21H30N2O5). Represents the elemental composition and is used in regulatory submissions, analytical method development, and structural verification.']
  molecular_weight decimal(12,4) [note: 'Average molecular weight of the compound expressed in grams per mole (g/mol). Critical physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, ADME profiling, formulation development, and Lipinski Rule of Five drug-likeness assessment.']

  primary_target varchar [note: 'Primary biological molecular target of the compound (e.g., gene name, protein name, receptor, enzyme — such as \'EGFR\', \'PD-1\', \'BCL-2\'). Used in target identification, SAR analysis, and cross-compound target coverage analysis within the discovery portfolio.']
  purity_percent decimal(5,2) [note: 'Measured chemical purity of the compound expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00%). Determined by analytical methods such as HPLC or NMR.   solubility_aqueous_um decimal(12,4) [note: 'Measured or predicted aqueous solubility of the compound expressed in micromolar (µM). Key ADME physicochemical property used in SAR analysis, formulation feasibility assessment, and drug-likeness profiling (Lipinski, Veber rules).']

  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Primary therapeutic area or disease indication for which the compound is being developed (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular).   molecular_target_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to discovery.molecular_target. Business justification: Assays are designed to screen against specific molecular targets.   responsible_scientist_employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: GxP compliance and regulatory inspections require traceable accountability for assay validation and execution. Responsible scientist must link to qualified employee record for training verification, e']
  assay_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable unique code assigned to the assay within the ELN or LIMS (e.g., ASY-HTS0042). Serves as the BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for cross-system referencing between IDBS/Dotmatics, LabWare LIMS, and SAP QM.']
  assay_name varchar [note: 'Full descriptive name of the assay as registered in the ELN (e.g., \'EGFR Kinase Inhibition HTRF Assay\'). Serves as the IDENTITY_LABEL category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used in scientific reports, regulatory submissions, and compound screening dashboards.']
  assay_type varchar [note: 'Primary scientific classification of the assay based on its biological or chemical mode of measurement. Serves as the CLASSIFICATION_OR_TYPE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Drives downstream SAR analysis workflows and compound triage decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: biochemical|cell_based|phenotypic|ADME|toxicity|binding|functional — promote to reference product]']
  automation_compatible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the assay has been adapted and validated for automated liquid handling platforms (e.g., Hamilton, Tecan, Beckman Coulter). Determines eligibility for inclusion in HTS screening campaigns and impacts throughput capacity planning.']
  cell_line varchar [note: 'Name of the cell line used in cell-based assays (e.g., HEK293, HeLa, Jurkat, A549, MCF-7). Null for biochemical or cell-free assays. Required for assay reproducibility and cross-site comparability. Cell line authentication records are maintained in the ELN.']
  coefficient_of_variation_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'Percentage coefficient of variation (%CV) of the assay signal across replicate measurements, representing assay precision and reproducibility. Typically required to be ≤ 15% for HTS assays and ≤ 20% for bioanalytical assays per ICH Q2(R1). Stored from the assay validation run.']
  concentration_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measurement for compound concentrations used in the assay (e.g., nM, µM, mM). Standardizes concentration reporting across compound screening results and SAR analysis. Required for dose-response curve fitting and IC50/EC50 calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: nM|uM|mM|mg_mL|ug_mL|ng_mL|pM — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  cost_per_well_usd decimal(10,4) [note: 'Estimated reagent and consumable cost per assay well in US dollars. Used for screening campaign cost modeling, budget planning, and make-vs-buy decisions for outsourcing to CROs. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA MM procurement data and lab supply records.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the assay master record was first created in the ELN or data platform. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance and data lineage tracking.']
  cro_vendor_name varchar [note: 'Name of the external Contract Research Organization (CRO) executing this assay when outsourced_to_cro is true. Null for in-house assays. Used for vendor performance tracking, contract management, and regulatory audit trail documentation.']
  detection_method varchar [note: 'Physical or chemical detection principle used to measure the assay signal (e.g., fluorescence, luminescence, radioactivity, mass spectrometry). Distinct from technology_platform — platform is the instrument system, detection_method is the underlying measurement principle. Used for assay validation documentation and GLP compliance records. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fluorescence|luminescence|absorbance|radioactivity|mass_spectrometry|NMR|SPR|calorimetry — promote to reference product]']
  eln_notebook_reference varchar [note: 'Identifier of the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) experiment or notebook entry in IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics where the assay development and validation data are recorded. Provides direct traceability from the data product to the source scientific record.']
  first_used_date date [note: 'Date when the assay was first deployed for compound screening or profiling activities. Marks the operational start of the assay lifecycle. Used for assay age tracking, periodic revalidation scheduling, and portfolio lifecycle management.']
  format varchar [note: 'Operational format describing how the assay is run in the screening workflow (e.g., High-Throughput Screening (HTS) primary screen, dose-response, selectivity panel). Determines throughput capacity planning and compound consumption requirements.']
  glp_compliant boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the assay is conducted under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations as required for regulatory submissions (IND/NDA/BLA). GLP-compliant assays require full audit trails, validated equipment, and certified personnel. Critical for preclinical safety study data submitted to FDA/EMA.']
  hit_threshold_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measurement for the hit_threshold_value (e.g., percent inhibition, nM IC50). Ensures unambiguous interpretation of the hit-calling criterion across different assay types and readout formats.']
  hit_threshold_value decimal(12,4) [note: 'Numerical threshold used to classify a compound as a \'hit\' in primary screening (e.g., ≥ 50% inhibition at 10 µM). Defined during assay validation and used by automated hit-calling algorithms in the HTS data analysis pipeline. Critical for hit-to-lead progression decisions.']
  incubation_time_hours decimal(8,2) [note: 'Standard incubation duration in hours for the assay reaction or cell treatment step. Critical for assay reproducibility and scheduling of automated liquid handling workflows. Stored from the validated assay protocol.']
  last_validated_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent formal validation or requalification of the assay per ICH Q2(R1) or fit-for-purpose qualification criteria. Used to trigger periodic revalidation workflows and to assess whether assay data is current for regulatory submissions.']
  lims_assay_code varchar [note: 'Cross-reference identifier for this assay in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) — LabWare or Thermo Fisher SampleManager. Enables bidirectional traceability between the discovery data product and the LIMS assay execution records.']
  multiplexed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the assay measures multiple analytes or endpoints simultaneously in a single well or reaction (multiplexed assay). Multiplexed assays increase data density per compound and reduce reagent consumption. Relevant for assay cost modeling and data analysis pipeline configuration.']
  outsourced_to_cro boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this assay is currently outsourced to an external Contract Research Organization (CRO) for execution. When true, the cro_vendor_name field captures the CRO identity. Impacts data governance, IP ownership, and regulatory audit trail requirements.']
  owning_department varchar [note: 'Name of the research department or functional group that owns and maintains the assay (e.g., \'HTS Group\', \'In Vitro Pharmacology\', \'ADME Sciences\', \'Toxicology\'). Used for resource allocation, cost center attribution, and assay portfolio governance.']
  plate_format varchar [note: 'Microplate format used in the assay (e.g., 96-well, 384-well, 1536-well). Determines reagent volumes, automation compatibility, and throughput capacity. Critical for liquid handling robot programming and compound dispensing protocols.']
  protocol_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier or URL reference to the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) or assay protocol document stored in the ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) or document management system (Veeva Vault QualityDocs). Ensures traceability from assay execution to the governing protocol version.']
  protocol_version varchar [note: 'Version number of the assay protocol document in effect at the time of assay execution (e.g., v1.0, v2.3). Required for GLP audit trails and regulatory submission traceability. Distinct from protocol_reference which is the document identifier.']
  readout_type varchar [note: 'Primary quantitative output metric reported by the assay (e.g., IC50, EC50, Ki, Kd, percent inhibition, percent activation). Determines how compound activity data is interpreted in SAR analysis and hit-to-lead progression decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IC50|EC50|Ki|Kd|percent_inhibition|percent_activation|ratio|count|viability_pct — promote to reference product]']
  regulatory_submission_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether assay results generated using this assay are eligible for inclusion in regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA). Eligibility requires full validation per ICH Q2(R1) and GLP compliance where applicable. Governs data governance workflows for regulatory data packages.']
  retirement_date date [note: 'Date when the assay was formally retired and removed from active use. Null for active assays. Retirement is triggered by target deprioritization, supersession by a superior assay, or platform decommissioning. Required for data governance and historical data archival.']
  signal_window decimal(10,4) [note: 'Ratio of the maximum signal (positive control) to the minimum signal (negative control), quantifying the dynamic range of the assay. A signal window ≥ 2 is typically required for HTS qualification. Used in assay validation reports and Z-factor calculations.']
  species_origin varchar [note: 'Biological species from which the assay target, cells, or biological material is derived (e.g., human, mouse, rat, recombinant). Critical for translational relevance assessment and cross-species selectivity profiling. Impacts regulatory acceptability of preclinical data for IND submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: human|mouse|rat|rabbit|dog|monkey|in_vitro_recombinant — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  technology_platform varchar [note: 'Detection technology or instrument platform used to execute the assay (e.g., HTRF, AlphaScreen, Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR), NMR, FRET, TR-FRET, Luminescence, Flow Cytometry). Critical for assay reproducibility assessment and equipment scheduling. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: HTRF|AlphaScreen|SPR|NMR|FRET|TR-FRET|luminescence|flow_cytometry|mass_spectrometry|fluorescence_polarization — promote to reference product]']
  temperature_celsius decimal(6,2) [note: 'Standard incubation or reaction temperature in degrees Celsius for the assay. Critical for assay reproducibility across sites and instruments. Deviations from this value are flagged as out-of-specification (OOS) events in the LIMS.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Disease or therapeutic area that the assay supports (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience, Cardiovascular). Links assay activity to the business portfolio and pipeline planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_diseases|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_diseases|metabolic — promote to reference product]']
  throughput_capacity varchar [note: 'Maximum number of compounds or samples that can be processed per day using this assay under standard HTS conditions. Serves as the MEASUREMENT_OR_VALUE category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. Used for compound library screening campaign planning and resource scheduling in the discovery lab.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the assay with respect to its scientific and regulatory validation. Serves as the LIFECYCLE_STATUS category for MASTER_RESOURCE role. \'validated\' indicates full ICH Q2(R1) compliance; \'qualified\' indicates fit-for-purpose qualification; \'development\' indicates the assay is still being optimized. Governs whether assay results can be used in regulatory submissions.']
  z_prime_factor decimal(6,4) [note: 'Statistical measure of assay quality (Z\') calculated from positive and negative control variability. Values ≥ 0.5 indicate an excellent assay suitable for HTS. Stored as the validated Z\' from the assay qualification run. Used to gate assay deployment for compound screening campaigns.']

  Note: 'Master record for biological and biochemical assays used in drug discovery screening and profiling. Captures assay name, assay type (biochemical, cell-based, phenotypic, ADME, toxicity), assay format (HTS, dose-response, selectivity), target association, assay technology platform (HTRF, AlphaScreen, SPR, NMR), assay validation status, GLP compliance flag, detection method, assay protocol reference, throughput capacity, and responsible scientist. Sourced from IDBS/Dotmatics ELN.'
}

Aligns the campaign to the company\'s R&D portfolio strategy and pipeline reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_disease|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_disease|metabolic|respiratory — promote to reference product]']

Table discovery.screening_result {
  screening_result_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each individual screening result record in the HTS or dose-response assay campaign. Primary key for the screening_result data product in the discovery domain.']
  assay_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the assay definition used to generate this screening result, including assay type, target, and protocol version.']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the scientist or analyst responsible for executing or approving this assay run. Required for GLP audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature compliance.']
  hts_campaign_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the High-Throughput Screening (HTS) campaign or screening project under which this result was generated. Enables grouping of results by campaign for SAR analysis.']
  molecular_target_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the biological molecular target (e.g., protein, enzyme, receptor) against which the compound was screened. Central to target identification and MOA studies.']
  primary_screening_compound_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the compound (NCE or NBE) that was screened in this assay run. Links to the compound master record in the compound library.']
  coefficient_of_variation_pct decimal(10,4) [note: 'Coefficient of variation (CV%) for replicate measurements of this compound in the assay run. Measures intra-assay reproducibility; high CV% triggers data quality review.']
  compound_concentration_um decimal(18,6) [note: 'Concentration of the compound tested in the assay well, expressed in micromolar (µM). Critical for dose-response curve fitting and potency determination.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this screening result record was first created in the system. Required for GLP audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record compliance.']
  curve_fit_r_squared decimal(10,6) [note: 'Coefficient of determination (R²) from the dose-response curve fitting model. Values close to 1.0 indicate a high-quality fit. Used as a data quality gate for potency value acceptance.']
  data_quality_flag varchar [note: 'Data quality status assigned to this screening result based on automated QC rules and manual review. \'flagged\' indicates a potential issue requiring review; \'rejected\' excludes the result from downstream analysis.']
  ec50_nm decimal(18,6) [note: 'Half-maximal effective concentration (EC50) derived from dose-response curve fitting, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Key potency metric for agonist/activator compounds.']
  eln_notebook_ref varchar [note: 'Reference identifier linking this screening result to the corresponding experiment entry in the Electronic Lab Notebook (ELN) system (IDBS E-WorkBook or Dotmatics). Provides traceability to the original experimental record.']
  hill_slope decimal(10,4) [note: 'Hill slope (cooperativity coefficient) from the four-parameter logistic (4PL) dose-response curve fit. Values near 1 indicate simple binding; values significantly different from 1 may indicate cooperativity, aggregation, or assay artifacts.']
  ic50_nm decimal(18,6) [note: 'Half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) derived from dose-response curve fitting, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Key potency metric for inhibitory compounds in SAR analysis and hit-to-lead progression.']
  instrument_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the laboratory instrument (e.g., plate reader, liquid handler, mass spectrometer) used to generate the raw signal. Supports instrument qualification tracking and systematic error investigation per GLP.']
  is_hit_to_lead_eligible boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this compound result meets the predefined criteria for progression into the hit-to-lead (H2L) phase, based on potency, selectivity, and data quality thresholds.']
  ki_nm decimal(18,6) [note: 'Inhibition constant (Ki) representing the binding affinity of the compound to the target, expressed in nanomolar (nM). Derived from competitive binding or enzyme kinetics assays. Used in mechanistic SAR studies.']
  lims_result_ref varchar [note: 'Reference identifier from the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) for this screening result record. Enables bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational LIMS source system.']
  max_response_percent decimal(10,4) [note: 'Maximum observed response (top asymptote) from the dose-response curve, expressed as a percentage of control. Indicates the efficacy ceiling of the compound at the target.']
  min_response_percent decimal(10,4) [note: 'Minimum observed response (bottom asymptote) from the dose-response curve, expressed as a percentage of control. Used to assess baseline signal and curve quality.']
  pan_assay_interference_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the compound has been identified as a Pan-Assay Interference Compound (PAINS) — a compound that produces artifactual activity signals across multiple assays due to non-specific mechanisms. PAINS compounds are deprioritized in hit-to-lead.']
  percent_activation decimal(10,4) [note: 'Calculated percentage activation of the target relative to controls. Primary activity metric for agonist/activator HTS campaigns. Null for inhibition assays.']
  percent_inhibition decimal(10,4) [note: 'Calculated percentage inhibition of the target activity relative to positive and negative controls on the same plate. Primary activity metric for inhibitory HTS campaigns. Null for activation assays.']
  plate_barcode varchar [note: 'Unique barcode identifier of the physical assay plate on which the compound was tested. Used for traceability back to the physical plate in the LIMS and for QC investigations.']
  plate_column varchar [note: 'Numeric column designation (1–24) of the well on the assay plate. Used for spatial analysis of plate effects and systematic error detection.']
  plate_row varchar [note: 'Row designation (A–P) of the well on the assay plate. Used for spatial analysis of plate effects and edge-effect QC.']
  quality_flag_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason explaining why a data quality flag was applied (e.g., \'edge well effect\', \'reagent lot failure\', \'instrument malfunction\', \'outlier replicate\'). Required when data_quality_flag is \'flagged\' or \'rejected\'.']
  raw_signal_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Unprocessed instrument signal reading from the assay detector (e.g., fluorescence units, luminescence counts, absorbance). Preserved as the primary measurement for audit and reanalysis.']
  reagent_lot_number varchar [note: 'Lot identifier of the key assay reagent (e.g., enzyme, antibody, cell line passage) used in this assay run. Enables reagent lot correlation analysis for systematic variability investigation.']
  replicate_number varchar [note: 'Sequential replicate index for this compound-assay combination within the same run (e.g., 1, 2, 3). Enables statistical aggregation across replicates and assessment of intra-assay variability.']
  result_classification varchar [note: 'Scientific classification of the screening result based on activity thresholds and confirmatory data. Drives hit-to-lead progression decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: active|inactive|inconclusive|toxic|hit|confirmed_hit|false_positive|pan_assay_interference — promote to reference product]']
  run_date date [note: 'Calendar date on which the assay run was executed. Used for temporal trending, reagent lot correlation, and GLP audit trail compliance.']
  run_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time when the assay instrument reading was captured. Supports intra-day sequencing, instrument log correlation, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic record compliance.']
  selectivity_score decimal(10,4) [note: 'Quantitative selectivity score measuring the compound\'s specificity for the primary target versus off-target activities in a selectivity panel. Higher scores indicate greater selectivity. Used in SAR-driven lead optimization.']
  signal_to_background_ratio decimal(10,4) [note: 'Ratio of the positive control signal to the background (negative control) signal on the assay plate. A key plate-level QC metric; low S/B ratios indicate assay degradation or reagent failure.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this screening result record. Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks lakehouse.']
  well_position varchar [note: 'Alphanumeric well position on the assay plate (e.g., A01, H12, P24) indicating the exact location of the compound in the plate layout. Standard SBS/ANSI plate format.']
  z_prime_factor decimal(10,4) [note: 'Z\' factor for the assay plate, a dimensionless statistical metric (range -∞ to 1) measuring assay quality based on signal window and variability. Z\' ≥ 0.5 is the accepted threshold for a valid HTS assay plate.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing individual compound screening results from HTS campaigns, dose-response assays, and selectivity panels. Captures compound, assay, and campaign references, plate/well position, raw signal, percent inhibition/activation, potency values (IC50/EC50/Ki), Hill slope, curve fit quality (R-squared), result classification (active, inactive, inconclusive, toxic, hit, confirmed hit, false positive), selectivity score, replicate number, run date, and data quality flags. Includes hit-to-lead eligibility determination. Distinct from in_vitro_study: screening_result covers primary and confirmatory screening at scale; in_vitro_study covers deeper mechanistic follow-up on selected compounds.'
}

  selectivity_findings varchar [note: 'Summary of selectivity data for the lead compounds against off-target proteins or related family members. Describes selectivity ratios, panel screening results, and any observed off-target liabilities.']
  selectivity_ratio decimal(10,2) [note: 'Quantitative ratio of the compound\'s potency against the primary target versus the most relevant off-target (e.g., 100-fold selective over related kinase). Key metric for candidate progression decisions.']
  start_date date [note: 'Date on which the SAR study was formally initiated, corresponding to the first experimental activity recorded in the ELN. Used for timeline tracking and portfolio planning.']

Used for portfolio segmentation and resource allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oncology|immunology|rare_diseases|neuroscience|cardiovascular|infectious_disease|metabolic — promote to reference product]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this SAR study record. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.']

  Note: 'Master record for Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) studies conducted to understand how structural modifications to a compound affect its biological activity.   notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for ADME scientist observations, anomalies, assay deviations, or contextual notes relevant to interpreting the ADME profile results. Supports GLP documentation requirements.']
  permeability_caco2_nm_s decimal(10,4) [note: 'Apparent permeability coefficient (Papp A→B) measured in Caco-2 cell monolayer assay, expressed in nm/s. Predicts intestinal absorption and oral bioavailability. Key ADME parameter for BCS classification.']
  permeability_pampa_nm_s decimal(10,4) [note: 'Passive transcellular permeability measured by PAMPA assay in nm/s. Complements Caco-2 data by isolating passive diffusion component, informing SAR optimization for membrane permeability.']
  pgp_substrate boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the compound is identified as a P-glycoprotein (P-gp / MDR1) efflux transporter substrate based on Caco-2 bidirectional permeability or dedicated P-gp inhibition assay. Impacts CNS penetration and oral bioavailability predictions.']
  plasma_protein_binding_pct decimal(6,3) [note: 'Percentage of compound bound to plasma proteins (albumin, alpha-1-acid glycoprotein) measured by equilibrium dialysis or ultrafiltration. Determines free fraction available for pharmacological activity and clearance.']
  ppb_method varchar [note: 'Analytical method used to determine plasma protein binding percentage. Rapid equilibrium dialysis (RED) is the industry standard; method choice affects result interpretation and cross-study comparability.']
  profile_code varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this ADME profiling run, used in ELN (IDBS/Dotmatics) and LIMS cross-referencing. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER BUSINESS_IDENTIFIER category.']
  profile_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow state of the ADME profile record from data entry through scientific review and approval. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER LIFECYCLE_STATUS category. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|in_progress|completed|reviewed|approved|invalidated — promote to reference product if additional states are needed]']
  progression_recommendation varchar [note: 'Scientific recommendation for compound progression based on the overall ADME profile assessment. Drives hit-to-lead and lead optimization decisions. Assigned by the ADME scientist upon profile review and approval.']
  rlm_clint_ul_min_mg decimal(10,4) [note: 'Intrinsic metabolic clearance measured in rat liver microsomes (RLM), expressed as µL/min/mg protein. Supports cross-species PK scaling and preclinical-to-clinical translation of metabolic stability data.']
  solubility_method varchar [note: 'Analytical method used to determine aqueous solubility, distinguishing kinetic from thermodynamic measurements which have different interpretive implications for drug development.']
  solubility_um decimal(10,4) [note: 'Measured aqueous solubility of the compound in micromolar (µM), typically from kinetic or thermodynamic solubility assay. Critical for assessing oral bioavailability and formulation feasibility. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category.']
  species varchar [note: 'Biological species from which the biological matrix (microsomes, plasma, cells) was derived for this ADME assay. Enables cross-species PK comparison and allometric scaling for preclinical-to-clinical translation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this ADME profile record. Satisfies TRANSACTION_HEADER RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail requirements.']
  volume_of_distribution_l_kg decimal(8,4) [note: 'Predicted or measured apparent volume of distribution (Vd) in L/kg, reflecting the extent of compound distribution into tissues versus plasma. Informs PK/PD modeling and dose prediction.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing ADME (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion) profiling results for compounds under evaluation. Captures compound identifier, assay panel used, solubility value, permeability (Caco-2/PAMPA), plasma protein binding, microsomal stability (human/rat liver microsomes), CYP inhibition profile, P-glycoprotein substrate flag, blood-brain barrier penetration, half-life, clearance rate, bioavailability estimate, assay date, and ADME scientist. Critical for compound progression decisions.'
}

  owning_team varchar [note: 'Name of the scientific team or department responsible for the model (e.g., \'Computational Chemistry\', \'Pharmacometrics\', \'AI Drug Design\'). Supports organisational accountability and model governance reporting.']
  predicted_property varchar [note: 'The specific biological, physicochemical, or pharmacokinetic property or endpoint the model predicts (e.g., \'pIC50 vs EGFR\', \'aqueous solubility (logS)\', \'human hepatic clearance\', \'hERG inhibition\'). Central to model cataloguing and scientific search.']
  publication_reference varchar [note: 'DOI, PubMed ID, or internal report number of the scientific publication or technical report describing the model methodology and validation. Supports IP management, scientific credibility, and regulatory submission traceability.']
  r_squared decimal(5,4) [note: 'R-squared (coefficient of determination) for regression models, measuring the proportion of variance in the predicted property explained by the model. Reported on the external test set per OECD guidelines.']
  retirement_date date [note: 'Date on which the model was retired or superseded and is no longer authoritative for compound design decisions. Null if the model is still active. Supports lifecycle governance and audit trail.']
  rmse decimal(10,4) [note: 'Root Mean Square Error of prediction on the test set for regression models. Primary accuracy metric for QSAR regression and PK/PD parameter prediction models. Units match the predicted property.']
  software_platform varchar [note: 'Name and version of the computational software or platform used to build and run the model (e.g., \'Schrödinger Suite 2023-3\', \'RDKit 2023.09\', \'MOE 2022.02\', \'KNIME 4.7\', \'Python 3.10 / scikit-learn 1.3\'). Required for CSV (Computer System Validation) and reproducibility.']
  test_set_size varchar [note: 'Number of compounds or data points in the external test/validation dataset used to assess model generalisability. Distinct from training set; required for OECD-compliant QSAR validation.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Therapeutic area or disease indication for which the model was developed (e.g., \'Oncology\', \'Immunology\', \'Rare Diseases\', \'Neuroscience\'). Enables portfolio-level analytics and resource allocation across drug discovery programmes.']
  training_dataset_name varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the dataset used to train the model (e.g., \'ChEMBL34_EGFR_IC50\', \'Internal_HTS_2022_Q3\'). Supports data lineage, model reproducibility, and regulatory traceability per OECD QSAR principles.']
  training_set_size varchar [note: 'Number of compounds or data points in the training dataset. Key model quality indicator; small training sets flag potential overfitting risk during scientific review.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the computational model record. Required for change tracking, audit trail, and data synchronisation with source ELN and model registry systems.']
  validation_method varchar [note: 'Statistical or experimental method used to validate the model\'s predictive performance (e.g., cross_validation, external_test_set, prospective validation). Determines regulatory acceptability of the model for decision-making.']

  Note: 'Master record for computational and in silico models supporting drug discovery decisions. Covers QSAR, molecular docking, virtual screening, pharmacophore models, PK/PD models, ADMET prediction, and AI/ML property prediction. Captures model name, type, target or property predicted, algorithm, training dataset, performance metrics (AUC, RMSE, enrichment factor), PK/PD parameters (Emax, EC50, Hill coefficient, compartment structure) where applicable, validation status, software platform, model owner, and deployment status. Supports computational chemistry, pharmacometrics, and AI-driven compound design.'
}

Table discovery.compound_supply_agreement {
  compound_supply_agreement_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated surrogate key for each compound-vendor supply agreement record']
  compound_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the compound being sourced from this vendor']
  vendor_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the vendor supplying this compound']
  agreement_effective_date date [note: 'Date when the supply agreement for this compound-vendor combination became effective']
  agreement_expiry_date date [note: 'Date when the supply agreement for this compound-vendor combination expires and requires renewal or renegotiation']
  agreement_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this compound-vendor supply agreement. Active: approved for procurement. Inactive: temporarily suspended. Pending: under negotiation. Expired: past expiry date. Terminated: permanently ended.']
  catalog_number varchar [note: 'Vendor-specific catalog number or SKU for this compound in the vendor\'s product catalog. Used for purchase order line item specification.']
  coa_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Certificate of Analysis (CoA) must be provided by the vendor with each shipment of this compound. CoA requirements vary by compound criticality and vendor qualification status.']
  last_purchase_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent purchase order placed for this compound from this vendor. Used to track active supply relationships and vendor performance history.']
  last_quality_issue_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent quality issue reported for this compound from this vendor']
  lead_time_days varchar [note: 'Number of business days from purchase order placement to delivery for this compound from this vendor. Lead time varies by vendor based on synthesis complexity, inventory availability, and shipping logistics.']
  minimum_order_quantity decimal(12,4) [note: 'Minimum quantity (in grams, milligrams, or units) that must be ordered from this vendor for this compound. MOQ varies by vendor based on synthesis batch economics.']
  minimum_order_quantity_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the minimum order quantity (gram, milligram, kilogram, vial, unit)']
  preferred_vendor_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this vendor is designated as the preferred supplier for this specific compound based on quality, price, reliability, and strategic relationship. A compound may have multiple approved vendors but only one preferred vendor.']
  price_currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit price (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP)']
  purity_specification varchar [note: 'Contractually agreed minimum purity specification for this compound from this vendor (e.g., ≥95%, ≥98%, ≥99.5%). Purity requirements may vary by vendor capability and intended use.']
  quality_issue_count varchar [note: 'Number of quality issues (out-of-specification results, failed CoA, contamination) reported for this compound from this vendor. Used for vendor performance tracking and sourcing decisions.']
  unit_price decimal(15,4) [note: 'Negotiated price per unit (gram, milligram, or vial) for this compound from this vendor. Price varies by vendor based on volume commitments, purity specifications, and contract terms.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the supply contract between a discovery compound and a procurement vendor. It captures vendor-specific sourcing terms, pricing, quality specifications, and procurement logistics that exist only in the context of this compound-vendor relationship. Each record links one compound to one vendor with commercial and quality attributes negotiated for that specific supply arrangement.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical operations, a single compound can be sourced from multiple vendors to ensure supply security, optimize costs, and maintain regulatory redundancy (multi-sourcing strategy). Conversely, each vendor supplies multiple compounds across the discovery library. The business actively manages these supply relationships as distinct agreements, each with vendor-specific pricing, lead times, purity specifications, catalog numbers, and preferred vendor designations that cannot be stored on either the compound or vendor entity alone.'
}

Table discovery.compound_exposure {
  compound_exposure_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for compound_exposure']
  compound_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the discovery compound that was administered to the patient. Identifies the specific investigational compound (NCE/NBE) used in this treatment exposure.']
  investigational_product_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the specific investigational product formulation administered (links to clinical.investigational_product). Captures the drug product form, not just the compound.']
  patient_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the patient who received the compound. Identifies the clinical trial participant or patient in the treatment exposure record.']
  trial_id varchar [note: 'Identifier of the clinical trial protocol under which this compound exposure occurred. Links to clinical.trial for trial-level context.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when this exposure record was created. Audit metadata for data lineage and compliance.']
  discontinuation_reason varchar [note: 'Primary reason why the patient discontinued treatment with this compound. Critical for safety analysis, efficacy assessment, and regulatory reporting.']
  dose_level varchar [note: 'Dose level or dosing regimen administered to the patient (e.g., \'100mg QD\', \'5mg/kg Q2W\'). Captures the specific dosing schedule for this compound-patient exposure.']
  enrollment_date date [note: 'Date when the patient was enrolled into the treatment arm and began receiving the investigational compound. Critical for exposure duration calculation and safety reporting windows.']
  exposure_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this compound exposure record (active, completed, discontinued, withdrawn). Tracks whether the patient is currently receiving treatment.']
  response_category varchar [note: 'Overall clinical response of the patient to the compound treatment, typically using standardized response criteria (e.g., RECIST for oncology). Captures efficacy outcome for this exposure.']
  treatment_arm varchar [note: 'Clinical trial treatment arm to which the patient was randomized or assigned (active, placebo, comparator, combination). Determines which compound or regimen the patient received.']
  treatment_duration_days varchar [note: 'Total duration of compound exposure expressed in days. Used for exposure-response analysis, safety signal detection, and pharmacovigilance reporting.']
  treatment_end_date date [note: 'Actual date of last dose administration of the compound to the patient. Used for exposure duration calculation and follow-up period determination.']
  treatment_start_date date [note: 'Actual date of first dose administration of the compound to the patient. Used for exposure window calculation and temporal safety analysis.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when this exposure record was last updated. Audit metadata for change tracking.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the treatment exposure event between a discovery compound and a clinical trial patient. It captures the investigational use of a compound in a patient, including dosing regimen, treatment duration, clinical response, and discontinuation details. Each record links one compound to one patient in the context of a specific treatment episode within a clinical trial. This is the authoritative source for compound-patient exposure history across the discovery-to-clinical continuum.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical development, one compound is tested in many patients across multiple trials and trial phases, and one patient may receive multiple investigational compounds either sequentially (across different trials) or simultaneously (in combination therapy trials). The business actively manages compound-patient exposure records as operational entities with treatment-specific data including dosing regimen, treatment duration, clinical response, and discontinuation reasons. This is a recognized business concept called \'compound exposure\' or \'treatment exposure\' that is critical for pharmacovigilance, efficacy analysis, and regulatory submissions.'
}

  delegation_log_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier pointing to the investigator\'s delegation of authority log stored in Veeva Vault eTMF or site trial master file.   investigator_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the investigator record. \'Active\' indicates the investigator is qualified and currently engaged in trial conduct. \'Disqualified\' reflects FDA or regulatory authority debarment or disqualification actions.']

  license_expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which the investigator\'s medical license expires. Triggers re-qualification workflows to ensure continued GCP-compliant trial conduct. Null if the license has no expiry.']
  license_issuing_authority varchar [note: 'Name of the regulatory or professional body that issued the medical license (e.g., California Medical Board, General Medical Council UK, Ordre des Médecins France). Required for cross-border trial conduct verification.']
  medical_license_number varchar [note: 'State or national medical license number issued by the relevant licensing authority. Required for regulatory submissions and site qualification. Uniquely identifies the investigator\'s right to practice medicine.']
  medical_specialty varchar [note: 'Primary board-certified or recognized medical specialty of the investigator (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Cardiology, Neurology). Used to match investigator expertise to trial therapeutic area and protocol requirements.']
  middle_name varchar [note: 'Middle name or initial of the investigator as recorded on official credentials. Used for disambiguation when first and last names are not unique.']
  npi_number varchar [note: '10-digit National Provider Identifier (NPI) assigned by CMS to US-based healthcare providers. Used for US-specific investigator identification, cross-referencing with HCP databases, and commercial engagement separation.']
  orcid_identifier varchar [note: 'Persistent digital identifier (ORCID iD) assigned to the investigator by the ORCID registry. Used to uniquely identify researchers across publications, grant applications, and clinical trial registries (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov).']
  phone varchar [note: 'Primary professional phone number for the investigator, used for urgent safety communications, protocol queries, and site monitoring contact. Includes country code for international trials.']
  prior_trial_count varchar [note: 'Total number of GCP-regulated clinical trials in which the investigator has previously served as PI or sub-investigator. Key feasibility metric used by sponsors and CROs during site selection.']
  professional_title varchar [note: 'Highest relevant professional or academic degree held by the investigator (e.g., MD, PhD, PharmD). Used in regulatory submissions and delegation logs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: MD|DO|PhD|MD-PhD|PharmD|MBBS|MBChB|DVM|Other — promote to reference product]']
  qualification_verified_date date [note: 'Date on which the sponsor or CRO last verified the investigator\'s qualifications, credentials, and GCP training as part of the site qualification or re-qualification process. Supports audit trail for regulatory inspections.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and GCP-compliant record management per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the principal investigator master record was most recently modified. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP data integrity requirements.']
  regulatory_authority_registration_number varchar [note: 'Identifier assigned by a national regulatory authority for the investigator\'s registration to conduct clinical trials (e.g., FDA investigator registration number, EudraCT investigator ID, MHRA registration). Required for IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.']
  sub_specialty varchar [note: 'Secondary or sub-specialty area of clinical expertise (e.g., Hematologic Oncology, Pediatric Immunology). Provides finer-grained matching for complex or rare disease trials.']
  therapeutic_area_expertise varchar [note: 'Primary therapeutic area(s) in which the investigator has documented clinical trial experience (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neurology). Used for protocol-to-investigator matching and feasibility assessments.']
  years_of_clinical_trial_experience varchar [note: 'Number of years the investigator has been conducting GCP-regulated clinical trials. Used during site feasibility assessments to evaluate investigator experience relative to protocol complexity.']

  Note: 'Master record for each Principal Investigator (PI) and sub-investigator responsible for conducting a clinical trial at a site. Captures investigator name, medical license number, specialty, GCP training certification date, CV reference, financial disclosure status, delegation log reference, and regulatory authority registration. Distinct from the HCP domain (which covers commercial HCP engagement) — this entity is specifically scoped to GCP-regulated trial conduct roles.'

Table clinical.clinical_enrollment {

Business justification: Enrolled subjects are assigned to specific investigational product kits at randomization. While enrollment has treatment_arm_code, linking to investigational_product provides the actual IMP kit assign']

Required for product-specific safety reporting (ICH E2A), efficacy analysis by product, and regulatory queries about subject exposure in multi-pro']
  patient_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) record. Links to the subject master record sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.']
  protocol_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific protocol version under which the subject was enrolled. A trial may have multiple protocol amendments; this captures the version active at enrollment.']

  blinding_status varchar [note: 'Indicates the current blinding state of the subject\'s treatment assignment. \'blinded\' = treatment assignment concealed; \'open_label\' = treatment known from outset; \'unblinded\' = previously blinded assignment has been revealed. Critical for data integrity and regulatory compliance.']
  block_size varchar [note: 'The number of subjects per randomization block used in the blocked randomization scheme. Confidential as knowledge of block size could compromise blinding. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM randomization parameters.']
  completion_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject completed all protocol-required study procedures and follow-up visits. Populated only when enrollment_status = completed. Used for study close-out and final analysis datasets.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this enrollment record was first created in the source system (Medidata Rave RTSM or Oracle CTMS). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) GCP guidelines.']
  ctms_subject_key varchar [note: 'The natural/business key for this subject enrollment record as assigned by Oracle Clinical / Siebel CTMS. Used for cross-system reconciliation between CTMS and Medidata Rave EDC. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.']
  data_lock_flag boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the subject\'s enrollment and randomization data has been locked for analysis (database lock). True = data locked and frozen for statistical analysis; False = data still open for query resolution or updates. Critical for regulatory submission readiness.']

  enrollment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the subject within the enrollment and randomization workflow. Drives Intent-to-Treat (ITT), modified ITT, and Per-Protocol (PP) population definitions. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM and Oracle CTMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screened|screen_failed|enrolled|randomized|withdrawn|completed|discontinued — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]']
  informed_consent_confirmed boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether a valid, signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) has been confirmed for this subject prior to any study procedures. True = ICF confirmed; False = ICF not confirmed or pending. Mandatory GCP compliance check.']
  informed_consent_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject signed the Informed Consent Form (ICF), confirming voluntary participation in the trial. Must precede any study-specific procedures per GCP requirements. Critical for regulatory submissions.']
  itt_population_flag boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population. True = subject is part of the ITT population (all randomized subjects regardless of protocol adherence). Drives primary efficacy analysis per ICH E9.']
  mitt_population_flag boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the modified Intent-to-Treat (mITT) analysis population. Criteria for mITT inclusion are protocol-defined (e.g., received at least one dose). Supports secondary efficacy analyses.']
  pp_population_flag boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether the subject is included in the Per-Protocol (PP) analysis population. True = subject completed the trial per protocol without major deviations. Used for sensitivity analyses in NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.']
  randomization_code varchar [note: 'Unique alphanumeric code assigned by the RTSM system at the point of randomization, linking the subject to their treatment arm assignment within the randomization schedule.   randomization_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject was randomized and assigned to a treatment arm via the RTSM system. May differ from enrollment_date in trials with a run-in period. Null for screen-failed or non-randomized subjects.']
  rave_subject_key varchar [note: 'The natural/business key for this subject enrollment record as assigned by Medidata Rave EDC/RTSM. Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracing back to the authoritative EDC source system.']
  screen_failure_reason varchar [note: 'Coded or free-text reason why a subject failed screening and was not enrolled. Populated only when enrollment_status = screen_failed. Used for protocol feasibility analysis and site performance monitoring. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC screen failure CRF.']
  screening_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject first presented at the investigational site for screening assessments. Marks the start of the eligibility evaluation period. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC.']
  screening_number varchar [note: 'Unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to a subject at the point of screening, prior to eligibility confirmation. Format is site-specific and assigned sequentially by the RTSM system in Medidata Rave. Used to track screen failures and pre-enrollment activity.']
  stratification_factor_1 varchar [note: 'Value of the first stratification factor used to balance treatment arm assignments across key prognostic variables (e.g., disease stage, geographic region, biomarker status). Defined in the trial protocol and captured at randomization in RTSM.']
  stratification_factor_2 varchar [note: 'Value of the second stratification factor used to balance treatment arm assignments (e.g., prior therapy, performance status, age group). Null if the trial uses fewer than two stratification factors. Captured at randomization in RTSM.']
  stratification_factor_3 varchar [note: 'Value of the third stratification factor used to balance treatment arm assignments (e.g., country, mutation status, weight band). Null if the trial uses fewer than three stratification factors. Captured at randomization in RTSM.']
  subject_number varchar [note: 'Unique identifier assigned to a subject upon successful enrollment into the trial. Typically formatted as site-number-sequential-ID (e.g., 001-001). Assigned by Medidata Rave RTSM upon eligibility confirmation and enrollment confirmation.']
  treatment_arm_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the treatment arm (e.g., active drug, placebo, comparator, dose level) to which the subject was assigned at randomization. Confidential in blinded trials. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM randomization schedule.']
  treatment_arm_description varchar [note: 'Human-readable description of the treatment arm assignment (e.g., \'Drug A 100mg QD\', \'Placebo\', \'Drug B 200mg BID\'). Confidential in blinded trials. Complements treatment_arm_code for reporting and analysis.']
  unblinding_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject\'s treatment assignment was unblinded. Populated only when blinding_status = unblinded. Emergency unblinding events must be documented per GCP. Null for blinded or open-label subjects.']
  unblinding_reason varchar [note: 'Coded reason for the unblinding of the subject\'s treatment assignment. Emergency unblinding (e.g., for medical management of a Serious Adverse Event) must be documented and reported per GCP and pharmacovigilance requirements. Null for blinded or open-label subjects.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this enrollment record was last modified in the source system. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2). Used for incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver Layer.']
  withdrawal_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject withdrew from the trial or was discontinued. Populated only when enrollment_status = withdrawn. Used for survival analysis (censoring) and dropout rate reporting.']
  withdrawal_reason varchar [note: 'Coded or free-text reason for subject withdrawal or discontinuation from the trial (e.g., adverse event, consent withdrawal, lost to follow-up, protocol deviation, investigator decision). Null for active or completed subjects. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: adverse_event|consent_withdrawal|lost_to_follow_up|protocol_deviation|investigator_decision|sponsor_decision|death|other — promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing each subject\'s complete enrollment and randomization journey within a clinical trial. Tracks screening number, subject number, enrollment date, informed consent confirmation, eligibility assessment (inclusion/exclusion criteria verification), screen failure reason, randomization date, randomization code, treatment arm assignment, stratification factors, blinding status, allocation ratio, block size reference, unblinding event details (if applicable), and enrollment/randomization status (screened, screen-failed, enrolled, randomized, withdrawn, completed). Supports ITT, modified ITT, and per-protocol population definitions. Authoritative SSOT for all subject-level randomization data including scheme parameters and individual assignments. Sourced from Medidata Rave RTSM (Randomization and Trial Supply Management) and Oracle CTMS.'
}

Table clinical.visit {
  visit_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each patient visit record within the clinical trial data product on the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key.']
  clinical_enrollment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to clinical.enrollment. Business justification: Patient visits occur within the context of a specific enrollment. While visit already has participant_id, trial_id, and site_id, linking to enrollment provides the complete enrollment context includin']
  investigational_site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the investigational site where the visit took place. Links to the site master record in CTMS (Oracle/Siebel).']
  investigator_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the principal investigator or sub-investigator who conducted or supervised this visit. Links to the investigator master record in CTMS (Oracle/Siebel).']
  patient_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical trial subject (patient) who attended this visit. Links to the subject/patient master record in the EDC (Medidata Rave) and CTMS (Oracle/Siebel).']
  protocol_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical trial protocol version that governs the schedule of assessments for this visit. Links to the protocol master record.']
  trial_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical study (trial) under which this visit was conducted. Links to the study master record in CTMS.']
  actual_date date [note: 'The date on which the visit actually occurred as recorded in the EDC (Medidata Rave). Corresponds to the CDISC CDASH VISDAT field. Null if the visit was missed or cancelled.']
  ae_reported_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether one or more Adverse Events (AEs) were reported at or since the previous visit (True) or not (False). Triggers downstream pharmacovigilance workflows in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS.']
  arm_name varchar [note: 'The name of the treatment arm or study arm to which the subject was assigned at the time of this visit (e.g., \'Drug A 100mg\', \'Placebo\', \'Drug A + Drug B Combination\'). Sourced from CTMS and EDC randomization records.']
  blinding_status varchar [note: 'Indicates the blinding status of the subject and/or investigator at the time of this visit. Unblinded records are restricted to authorized personnel only and are critical for data integrity in double-blind trials.']
  completion_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of protocol-required assessments and procedures that were completed at this visit (0.00–100.00). Supports partial visit analysis and data completeness reporting for regulatory submissions.']
  conmed_updated_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject\'s concomitant medication list was reviewed and updated at this visit (True) or not (False). Supports safety and drug-drug interaction analysis.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this visit record was first created in the source EDC system (Medidata Rave). Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.']
  data_entry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the visit data was first entered into the EDC system (Medidata Rave) by the site staff. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2).']
  data_lock_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the visit record was locked in the EDC (Medidata Rave), preventing further data entry or modification without an authorized unlock. Null if the record has not yet been locked.']
  day_from_reference varchar [note: 'The study day number calculated from the subject\'s reference date (typically first dose date or randomization date) to the actual visit date. Corresponds to the CDISC VISITDY variable. Negative values indicate pre-dose visits.']
  deviation_category varchar [note: 'Classification of the protocol deviation severity at this visit: major (could affect subject safety or data integrity), minor (unlikely to affect safety or data integrity), or administrative (procedural/documentation only).']
  deviation_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the protocol deviation(s) noted at this visit, as recorded by the site in the EDC or CTMS. Null when deviation_flag is False.']
  deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether one or more protocol deviations were recorded for this visit (True) or not (False). A True value triggers linkage to the protocol deviation register in the CTMS or eTMF (Veeva Vault).']
  early_termination_reason varchar [note: 'The reason the subject discontinued the study at or before this visit, if applicable. Null for non-termination visits. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: adverse_event|withdrawal_of_consent|lost_to_follow_up|protocol_violation|sponsor_decision|death|other — promote to reference product]']
  edc_visit_oid varchar [note: 'The unique object identifier (OID) assigned to this visit record within the Medidata Rave EDC system. Used for traceability and reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the source EDC system.']
  epoch varchar [note: 'The trial epoch during which this visit occurred, as defined in the CDISC SDTM Trial Design model (e.g., Screening, Run-In, Treatment, Follow-Up, Post-Study). Supports epoch-level analysis.']
  informed_consent_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject\'s current informed consent form (ICF) was verified as valid and current at the time of this visit (True) or not (False). Critical for GCP compliance and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  planned_date date [note: 'The date on which the visit was scheduled to occur per the protocol Schedule of Assessments and the subject\'s randomization or enrollment anchor date.']
  query_open_count varchar [note: 'The number of data queries (discrepancies) currently open against this visit record in the EDC (Medidata Rave). A non-zero value indicates outstanding data cleaning actions required before database lock.']
  randomization_number varchar [note: 'The unique randomization number assigned to the subject at the time of randomization, as recorded in the Interactive Response Technology (IRT) system. Confidential as it may reveal treatment assignment in blinded trials.']
  sae_reported_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether one or more Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) were reported at this visit (True) or not (False). SAEs require expedited reporting to health authorities per ICH E2A and 21 CFR Part 312.32.']
  source_verified_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether Source Data Verification (SDV) has been completed for this visit by the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) or monitor (True) or not (False). Critical for GCP compliance and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this visit record was last modified in the source EDC system (Medidata Rave) or during Silver Layer processing. Supports audit trail and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11.']
  visit_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable label for the visit as defined in the protocol Schedule of Assessments (e.g., \'Screening\', \'Cycle 1 Day 1\', \'Week 12 Follow-Up\', \'End of Study\'). Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC visit folder name.']
  visit_number varchar [note: 'Sequential numeric identifier for the visit as defined in the protocol Schedule of Assessments (SoA). Unscheduled visits may carry a non-integer or supplemental numbering convention captured separately.']
  visit_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the visit record indicating whether the visit was completed, missed, partially completed, cancelled, or rescheduled. Sourced from Medidata Rave EDC and CTMS.']
  visit_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the visit according to its role in the trial timeline. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screening|baseline|treatment|follow_up|end_of_study|unscheduled|early_termination — promote to reference product]']
  window_lower_day varchar [note: 'The number of days before the planned visit date that defines the lower boundary of the acceptable visit window per the protocol. Used to assess visit window compliance.']
  window_upper_day varchar [note: 'The number of days after the planned visit date that defines the upper boundary of the acceptable visit window per the protocol. Used to assess visit window compliance.']
  within_window_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the actual visit date fell within the protocol-defined visit window (True) or outside it (False). Derived at ingestion from planned_date, actual_date, window_lower_day, and window_upper_day; stored for analytical efficiency.']

  Note: 'Transactional record for each scheduled or unscheduled patient visit within a clinical trial, as captured in the EDC (Medidata Rave). Tracks visit number, visit name per protocol schedule of assessments, planned visit date, actual visit date, visit window compliance, visit type (screening, treatment, follow-up, end-of-study), visit status, and deviations noted. Forms the backbone of the clinical data collection timeline.'
}
