  form_oid varchar [note: 'Unique Object Identifier (OID) for the CRF form as defined in Medidata Rave and conforming to CDISC ODM standards. Used for cross-system referencing and SDTM mapping. Example: \'AE_FORM_V2\'.']
  form_order varchar [note: 'Numeric sequence order of this form within its associated visit or study schedule of events. Determines the display order in the EDC and printed CRF booklet.']
  form_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the CRF form by its data collection pattern in Medidata Rave. \'scheduled\' forms appear at predefined visits; \'unscheduled\' are event-driven; \'common\' appear across all visits; \'log\' forms capture repeating events (e.g., AE log); \'repeating\' forms allow multiple instances per visit.']
  form_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the CRF form definition, following semantic versioning (e.g., \'1.0\', \'2.1\', \'3.0.1\'). Tracks design changes over the trial lifecycle and supports audit trail requirements.']
  is_blinded boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this CRF form contains blinded data (e.g., treatment assignment, randomization code) that must be restricted from unblinded personnel during the trial. Supports GCP-compliant blinding controls.']
  is_repeating boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this CRF form allows multiple instances per subject per visit (e.g., an Adverse Event log form where each AE is a separate instance). Drives EDC configuration in Medidata Rave.']
  is_sdv_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether Source Data Verification (SDV) is required for data entered on this CRF form. Critical forms (e.g., primary endpoints, safety data) typically require 100% SDV; others may be risk-based.']
  is_signature_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an electronic signature (e-signature) is required on this CRF form by the investigator or site staff upon completion, as mandated by 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP requirements.']
  itt_population_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this CRF form contributes data to the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population definition. ITT-relevant forms are critical for primary efficacy analysis and regulatory review.']
  modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when this CRF form definition record was last modified. Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail, change control, and GCP compliance.']
  primary_endpoint_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this CRF form captures data for the trial\'s primary efficacy or safety endpoint (e.g., ORR, PFS, OS). Primary endpoint forms receive heightened monitoring, SDV, and data review scrutiny.']
  rave_form_draft_version varchar [note: 'The internal Medidata Rave draft version number for this CRF form, distinct from the business version. Tracks incremental design changes within the Rave study build environment prior to promotion to production.']
  rave_study_name varchar [note: 'The study name as configured in Medidata Rave EDC system, used to identify the parent study context for this CRF form. Supports cross-referencing between the data lakehouse and the source EDC system.']
  regulatory_submission_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether data collected on this CRF form is included in regulatory submissions (NDA/BLA/MAA/IND). Drives SDTM dataset inclusion and eCTD packaging requirements.']
  safety_form_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this CRF form is designated as a safety-critical form (e.g., Adverse Event, Serious Adverse Event, SUSAR reporting). Safety forms trigger expedited review workflows and pharmacovigilance data feeds.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'Two-letter CDISC SDTM domain code to which this CRF form maps for regulatory submission (e.g., \'AE\' for Adverse Events, \'VS\' for Vital Signs, \'CM\' for Concomitant Medications, \'LB\' for Laboratory). Drives SDTM dataset generation for NDA/BLA/MAA submissions.']
  sdv_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The percentage of data points on this CRF form subject to Source Data Verification (SDV) under the risk-based monitoring plan. Ranges from 0.00 (no SDV) to 100.00 (full SDV). Supports risk-based monitoring strategy.']
  source_system_form_code varchar [note: 'Native identifier of this CRF form record in the source EDC system (Medidata Rave). Enables lineage tracing from the Silver Layer back to the operational system of record.']
  validation_rule_set varchar [note: 'Identifier or name of the edit check / validation rule set applied to this CRF form in Medidata Rave. References the programmed edit checks that enforce data quality, range checks, and cross-form consistency rules.']
  visit_oid varchar [note: 'CDISC ODM-compliant OID of the study visit to which this form is assigned, as defined in Medidata Rave. Supports cross-system visit-form linkage without requiring a resolved FK at this stage.']

  Note: 'Master record for each Case Report Form (CRF) design used in a trial, representing the electronic data capture instrument definition in Medidata Rave. Captures form name, form OID, associated visit, data domain (SDTM domain mapping), version, validation rules, completion requirements, and approval status. Distinct from CRF data (captured in subject_observation) — this is the instrument definition, not the collected data.'
}

  is_baseline boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this observation represents the baseline measurement for the subject, used as the reference value for change-from-baseline calculations in efficacy endpoint derivation (e.g., tumor size at baseline for ORR). Corresponds to SDTM ABLFL flag in ADaM datasets.']
  is_unscheduled boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this observation was collected during an unscheduled visit (not defined in the protocol schedule of assessments). Unscheduled observations may be excluded from primary efficacy analyses per the statistical analysis plan.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time of the most recent modification to this observation record in the EDC system. Supports audit trail tracking, data change monitoring, and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.']
  normal_range_high decimal(18,6) [note: 'The upper bound of the reference (normal) range for this observation type as defined by the central laboratory or clinical standard. Used for out-of-range flagging, safety signal detection, and SDTM STNRHI derivation.']
  normal_range_low decimal(18,6) [note: 'The lower bound of the reference (normal) range for this observation type as defined by the central laboratory or clinical standard. Used for out-of-range flagging, safety signal detection, and SDTM STNRLO derivation.']
  numeric_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The numeric representation of the observation value after unit standardization, corresponding to the SDTM STRESN variable. Used for quantitative analyses, endpoint derivation (ORR, PFS, OS), and statistical modeling in ADaM datasets.']
  observation_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow status of the observation record within the EDC system lifecycle. Drives data cleaning workflows, lock readiness assessment, and database lock milestones. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: entered|verified|locked|queried|resolved|deleted — promote to reference product if additional statuses are required]']
  out_of_range_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the numeric observation value falls outside the defined normal reference range (low or high). Triggers safety review workflows, potential AE/SAE reporting, and DSMB notification processes.']
  protocol_deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this observation is associated with a protocol deviation (e.g., collected outside the visit window, wrong procedure performed). Flagged observations may be excluded from Per Protocol (PP) analysis populations.']
  query_status varchar [note: 'Status of any data query (discrepancy) raised against this observation in the EDC system. Open queries must be resolved prior to database lock. Supports data cleaning metrics and site performance monitoring.']
  query_text varchar [note: 'The text of the most recent data query raised against this observation, describing the discrepancy or clarification required from the site. Supports data management review and site communication workflows.']
  raw_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The verbatim data value as entered by the site user in the EDC system (Medidata Rave), prior to any derivation or standardization. Stored as STRING to accommodate all data types (numeric, text, coded). Represents the source data for SDV and audit trail purposes.']
  reason_for_change varchar [note: 'The documented reason provided by the site user when modifying a previously entered observation value in the EDC system. Mandatory per 21 CFR Part 11 and GCP requirements for any post-entry data correction. Stored as the most recent change reason.']
  sdtm_domain varchar [note: 'CDISC SDTM domain code to which this observation maps (e.g., VS for Vital Signs, LB for Laboratory, AE for Adverse Events, EX for Exposure). Critical for SDTM dataset generation and regulatory submission packages (NDA/BLA/MAA).']
  sdtm_variable varchar [note: 'The specific CDISC SDTM variable name to which this CRF field maps (e.g., VSSTRESN, LBORRES, AEDECOD). Enables automated SDTM dataset generation and submission-ready data transformation.']
  sdv_date date [note: 'The date on which Source Data Verification (SDV) was completed for this observation. Used for monitoring visit planning, SDV coverage reporting, and GCP audit trail documentation.']
  sdv_status varchar [note: 'Status of Source Data Verification (SDV) for this observation, indicating whether the EDC-entered value has been verified against the original source document (e.g., medical record, lab report) by the CRA or site monitor. Critical for GCP compliance and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  standard_unit varchar [note: 'The standardized unit of measure after conversion to the study-defined reference unit (SDTM STRESU). Enables cross-site and cross-study comparability for endpoint derivation and pooled analyses.']
  toxicity_grade varchar [note: 'The NCI CTCAE toxicity grade assigned to this observation when it represents an adverse finding (Grade 1=Mild, Grade 2=Moderate, Grade 3=Severe, Grade 4=Life-threatening, Grade 5=Death). Critical for safety endpoint reporting, dose modification decisions, and regulatory safety narratives.']
  unit varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for the observation value as collected (e.g., mmHg, mg/dL, kg, beats/min). Corresponds to SDTM ORRESU variable. Required for clinical interpretation and cross-site data harmonization.']
  verified_by varchar [note: 'The username or identifier of the Clinical Research Associate (CRA) or monitor who performed Source Data Verification (SDV) for this observation. Supports GCP compliance documentation and monitoring visit reports.']

  Note: 'Core transactional table capturing all clinical data collected per subject per visit per CRF form in the EDC (Medidata Rave). Stores data point value, unit, SDTM variable mapping, collection date, data entry date, query status, source data verification (SDV) status, and audit trail reference. Represents the atomic unit of clinical trial data — the foundation for efficacy and safety endpoint derivation (ORR, PFS, OS, QoL) and CDISC SDTM/ADaM dataset generation.'
}

  etmf_document_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in the Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) system (e.g., Veeva Vault) for the scanned or electronically captured consent form. Enables direct linkage between the consent record and the regulatory-compliant document archive.']
  investigator_signed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the Principal Investigator (PI) or delegated sub-investigator has signed the informed consent form, confirming the consent discussion was conducted per GCP requirements.']
  irb_iec_approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the IRB or IEC approved the ICF version referenced in this consent event. Consent must not be obtained prior to this date to maintain GCP compliance.']
  irb_iec_approval_number varchar [note: 'Reference number of the IRB or IEC approval that authorized the specific ICF version used in this consent event. Ensures GCP-compliant traceability between the consent form version and its ethics committee approval.']
  itt_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject is included in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT) analysis population. Subjects who consented and received at least one dose of investigational product are typically included in the ITT population.']
  lar_name varchar [note: 'Full legal name of the Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) who provided consent on behalf of the subject. Populated only when lar_required is True.']
  lar_relationship varchar [note: 'Relationship of the Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) to the trial subject (e.g., parent, legal guardian, spouse). Required when lar_required is True to establish legal authority to consent.']
  lar_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) was required to provide consent on behalf of the subject, applicable for minors, cognitively impaired subjects, or other legally incapacitated individuals.']
  lar_signed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) has signed and dated the informed consent form. Applicable only when lar_required is True.']
  optional_consent_biobank boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject provided optional consent for long-term storage and future use of biological samples in a biobank. This is a separate optional consent element from the main trial consent.']
  optional_consent_genetic boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject provided optional consent for genetic or genomic research using their biological samples. Separate from the main trial consent and biobank consent.']
  reconsent_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject provided re-consent following a protocol amendment or updated ICF version. Null if no re-consent has been required for this subject.']
  reconsent_reason varchar [note: 'Reason that triggered the re-consent requirement, such as a protocol amendment, new safety information identified during the trial, or a regulatory authority request. Null if no re-consent was required.']
  source_document_location varchar [note: 'Location reference for the original signed consent form source document, such as the eTMF folder path in Veeva Vault or physical file location at the investigational site. Supports GCP source data verification (SDV) and audit trail requirements.']
  subject_signed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the subject has personally signed and dated the informed consent form. False if consent was provided solely by a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) without subject co-signature.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this consent record in the system. Supports audit trail requirements and data integrity monitoring per 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.']
  withdrawal_date date [note: 'Date on which the subject formally withdrew consent to participate in the trial. Null if consent has not been withdrawn. Triggers subject discontinuation workflow in the CTMS.']
  withdrawal_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text or coded reason provided by the subject or investigator for withdrawal of consent. Captured for regulatory reporting and subject safety follow-up purposes.']
  witness_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an impartial witness was required to be present during the consent process, applicable when the subject or LAR is unable to read or when a short-form consent is used.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing each informed consent event for a trial subject, including consent form version, consent date, re-consent date (if protocol amended), subject signature confirmation, legally authorized representative details (if applicable), consent withdrawal date, and IRB/IEC approval reference for the consent version used. Ensures GCP-compliant documentation of subject autonomy and regulatory traceability.'
}

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this endpoint assessment record was most recently modified. Required for GCP audit trail compliance and data integrity monitoring under 21 CFR Part 11.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing the formal assessment of primary and secondary clinical endpoints for each subject at defined timepoints.   entered_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the laboratory result was entered or imported into the Medidata Rave EDC system. Used for audit trail compliance per 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) to demonstrate timely data entry and GCP compliance.']
  fasting_status varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the subject was fasting at the time of specimen collection. Relevant for metabolic panels (glucose, lipids) where fasting status affects reference ranges and result interpretation. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBFAST.']
  lab_accreditation_number varchar [note: 'Accreditation or certification number of the central or local laboratory that performed the analysis (e.g., CAP accreditation number, ISO 15189 certification reference, CLIA certificate number). Required for GCP compliance documentation and regulatory submissions to confirm laboratory qualification.']
  lab_name varchar [note: 'Name of the central or local laboratory that performed the laboratory analysis (e.g., \'Covance Central Laboratory\', \'Q2 Solutions\', \'Local Site Lab\'). Used for lab-level data quality monitoring, audit trail, and regulatory submission documentation.']
  lab_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the laboratory result was generated by a central laboratory (contracted central lab with standardized methods across all sites) or a local laboratory (site-specific lab). Central lab results are preferred for primary efficacy and safety endpoints due to standardization.']
  loinc_code varchar [note: 'Standardized LOINC code identifying the laboratory test or observation. Enables cross-study, cross-site, and cross-system harmonization of lab test definitions. Required for regulatory submissions and interoperability with central lab data transfers.']
  method_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the analytical method or assay used by the laboratory to generate the result (e.g., spectrophotometry, flow cytometry, PCR, ELISA). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBMETHOD. Important for result comparability and method validation documentation.']
  normal_flag varchar [note: 'Flag indicating whether the result is within, below, or above the laboratory\'s normal reference range. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBNRIND. Values: normal, low, high, critically_low, critically_high. Used in safety data listings and shift tables for regulatory submissions.']
  out_of_range_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the result value falls outside the laboratory\'s defined reference range (either below lower limit or above upper limit). Distinct from clinical significance — a result can be out of range but not clinically significant. Used for automated data quality checks and safety signal detection.']
  panic_value_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether the result meets the laboratory\'s criteria for a panic (critical) value requiring immediate notification to the investigator or site. Supports GCP-compliant safety monitoring and timely SAE/AE reporting obligations.']
  protocol_deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this laboratory result is associated with a protocol deviation (e.g., specimen collected outside the protocol-defined time window, incorrect specimen type collected). Used for ITT/PP population analysis and regulatory submission deviation summaries.']
  query_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether an open data query (discrepancy) exists for this laboratory result record in Medidata Rave EDC. Used by data managers to track unresolved data issues requiring site clarification before database lock.']
  rave_record_reference varchar [note: 'Source system record identifier from Medidata Rave EDC for this laboratory result entry. Used for data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail back to the originating EDC system.']
  reference_range_high decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper bound of the laboratory\'s normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject\'s demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRHI. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.']
  reference_range_low decimal(18,6) [note: 'Lower bound of the laboratory\'s normal reference range for this test, applicable to the subject\'s demographic group (age, sex). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTNRLO. Used for normal/abnormal flagging and shift table generation.']
  reported_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the laboratory result was officially reported and transmitted by the laboratory to the sponsor or EDC system. Used for turnaround time monitoring, GCP compliance (timely reporting of critical values), and data transfer reconciliation.']
  result_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the laboratory result record reflecting its lifecycle in the EDC and central lab workflow. Values: preliminary (initial result), final (verified and released), corrected (amended after initial release), cancelled (result voided), pending (awaiting analysis). Corresponds to HL7 observation status.']
  result_unit_standard varchar [note: 'Standardized unit of measure for the laboratory result after conversion to a common unit for cross-site and cross-study comparability. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESU. Enables pooled analyses and regulatory submission datasets.']
  result_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'The reported result value for the laboratory test as a string to accommodate both numeric and character results (e.g., \'5.4\', \'>100\', \'POSITIVE\', \'NEGATIVE\', \'TRACE\'). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBORRES. Stored as STRING to preserve original reported value including qualifiers.']
  result_value_numeric decimal(18,6) [note: 'Numeric representation of the laboratory result value after standardization and unit conversion. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSTRESN. Used for quantitative statistical analyses, shift tables, and outlier detection. Null for non-numeric results.']
  study_day varchar [note: 'Relative study day of specimen collection calculated from the subject\'s first dose date (Day 1). Negative values indicate pre-dose assessments. Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBDY. Used for time-course analyses, PK/PD modeling, and protocol compliance assessment.']
  test_category varchar [note: 'Broad classification of the laboratory test panel or category (e.g., hematology, chemistry, urinalysis, coagulation). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBCAT variable. Used for grouping and filtering in safety data review and regulatory submissions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: hematology|chemistry|urinalysis|coagulation|immunology|microbiology|pharmacokinetics|other — promote to reference product]']
  test_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable name of the laboratory test performed (e.g., Hemoglobin, Serum Creatinine, ALT, White Blood Cell Count). Sourced from the central lab data transfer file and mapped to the CRF lab panel definition in Medidata Rave.']
  test_subcategory varchar [note: 'More granular sub-classification of the laboratory test within its category (e.g., liver function tests within chemistry, CBC within hematology). Corresponds to CDISC SDTM LBSCAT variable.']
  toxicity_grade varchar [note: 'Toxicity grade assigned to the laboratory abnormality per the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading scale (Grade 1=Mild, Grade 2=Moderate, Grade 3=Severe, Grade 4=Life-threatening, Grade 5=Death). Used for safety signal detection, dose modification decisions, and regulatory safety reporting.']
  verified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the laboratory result was verified (source data verified, SDV) by the clinical monitor or data manager in Medidata Rave. Required for GCP audit trail and trial master file completeness.']

  Note: 'Transactional record for each central or local laboratory test result collected during a clinical trial. Captures lab test name (LOINC coded), specimen type, collection date, result value, unit, reference range, normal/abnormal flag, clinically significant flag, out-of-range flag, and laboratory accreditation reference. Sourced from central lab data transfers into Medidata Rave. Distinct from manufacturing LIMS results — this is trial-specific clinical lab data.'
}

  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp indicating when this monitoring visit record was first created in the data platform. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  critical_findings_count varchar [note: 'Number of critical findings identified during the monitoring visit. Critical findings represent major deviations from GCP, protocol, or regulatory requirements that pose significant risk to subject safety, data integrity, or trial validity.']
  etmf_document_reference varchar [note: 'Unique identifier for the monitoring visit report and related documents in the electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) system, typically Veeva Vault eTMF.']
  findings_summary varchar [note: 'Narrative summary of key findings, observations, and issues identified during the monitoring visit. Provides context for the quantitative finding counts and highlights areas requiring attention.']
  follow_up_letter_date date [note: 'Date on which the formal monitoring visit follow-up letter was issued to the investigational site. The follow-up letter documents findings, required actions, and timelines for resolution.']
  gcp_compliance_status varchar [note: 'Overall assessment of the investigational sites compliance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards based on observations during the monitoring visit. GCP compliance is mandatory for regulatory acceptance of trial data.']
  informed_consent_verified_count varchar [note: 'Number of informed consent forms reviewed and verified for completeness, signatures, and regulatory compliance during the visit.']
  investigator_meeting_held boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a face-to-face meeting was conducted with the principal investigator during the monitoring visit to discuss trial progress, findings, and site performance.']
  ip_accountability_verified boolean [note: 'Indicates whether investigational product (IP) accountability records were reviewed and verified during the visit. IP accountability ensures proper receipt, storage, dispensing, and return/destruction of study drug.']
  major_findings_count varchar [note: 'Number of major findings identified during the monitoring visit. Major findings represent significant deviations that require corrective action but do not immediately threaten subject safety or data integrity.']
  minor_findings_count varchar [note: 'Number of minor findings or observations identified during the monitoring visit. Minor findings represent low-impact deviations or areas for improvement that do not significantly affect trial conduct.']
  monitoring_report_date date [note: 'Date on which the formal monitoring visit report was completed and submitted. The monitoring report is a GCP-required document that summarizes visit activities, findings, and recommendations.']
  monitoring_report_reference varchar [note: 'Document reference or identifier for the formal monitoring visit report stored in the Trial Master File (TMF) or electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) system.']
  prior_capa_resolved_count varchar [note: 'Number of CAPA items from previous monitoring visits that were verified as resolved during this visit. Tracks effectiveness of corrective actions and continuous improvement.']
  protocol_deviations_identified varchar [note: 'Number of protocol deviations identified during the monitoring visit. Protocol deviations represent departures from the approved study protocol that may affect subject safety, data integrity, or trial outcomes.']
  regulatory_binder_reviewed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the site regulatory binder (containing essential documents such as IRB approvals, investigator CVs, licenses, and training records) was reviewed for completeness and currency during the visit.']
  risk_score_change varchar [note: 'Direction of change in the site risk score compared to the previous assessment. Indicates whether site performance and compliance are improving, deteriorating, or stable.']
  scheduled_date date [note: 'Planned date for the monitoring visit as defined in the monitoring plan or risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategy.']
  sdv_completion_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of case report form (CRF) data points verified against source documents during this monitoring visit. SDV is a core GCP requirement to ensure data accuracy and integrity.']
  site_risk_score decimal(5,2) [note: 'Updated risk score for the investigational site following the monitoring visit. Risk scores inform risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategies and determine frequency and intensity of future monitoring activities.']
  subjects_reviewed_count varchar [note: 'Number of enrolled subjects whose records were reviewed during this monitoring visit for protocol compliance, data quality, and safety assessment.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp indicating when this monitoring visit record was last modified in the data platform. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']
  visit_end_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time when the monitoring visit concluded at the investigational site.']
  visit_mode varchar [note: 'Method by which the monitoring visit was conducted. On-site visits involve physical presence at the investigational site, remote visits use electronic systems and telecommunications, and hybrid visits combine both approaches.']
  visit_start_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Precise date and time when the monitoring visit commenced at the investigational site.']

  Note: 'Transactional record for each monitoring visit conducted by a Clinical Research Associate (CRA) at an investigational site. Captures visit type (routine, triggered, close-out), visit date, CRA name, source data verification (SDV) completion percentage, critical findings, follow-up letter date, CAPA items raised, site risk score update, and confirmation of GCP compliance observations. Tracks resolution status of prior visit findings. Core operational record for GCP oversight per ICH E6 R2 section 5.18 and supports risk-based monitoring (RBM) strategies.'
}

Table clinical.imp_administration {
  imp_administration_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each IMP administration event record']
  administered_by_investigator_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the investigator or qualified designee who administered or supervised the IMP administration']
  investigational_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific investigational medicinal product (IMP) batch administered at this visit']
  visit_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the patient visit during which this IMP administration occurred']
  accountability_log_entry varchar [note: 'Reference to the corresponding entry in the IMP accountability log maintained at the investigational site']
  administration_deviation_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a protocol deviation occurred during this IMP administration (wrong dose, wrong time, wrong route, etc.)']
  administration_status varchar [note: 'Status of this administration event: administered (full dose given), partially_administered, not_administered (subject refused or clinically contraindicated), returned (subject returned unused IMP), destroyed (IMP disposed per protocol)']
  administration_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the investigational product was administered to the subject, as recorded in source documents and EDC']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this IMP administration record was first created in the EDC system']
  deviation_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the protocol deviation related to this IMP administration, if deviation_flag is true']
  dose_administered decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of IMP administered to the subject at this visit, expressed in the dose unit']
  dose_number varchar [note: 'The sequential dose number administered to the subject at this visit, as recorded in the EDC (Medidata Rave). Null for non-dosing visits. Supports cumulative exposure and dose-response analysis. [Moved from visit: The dose_number attribute in visit represents the sequential dose count for the subject, which is actually a property of the administration event (the relationship between IMP and visit), not an intrinsic property of the visit itself. Multiple IMPs could be administered at a single visit, each with its own dose sequence.]']
  dose_unit varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the administered dose (mg, mL, tablets, capsules, units, mcg, g)']
  kit_number varchar [note: 'Unique identifier for the IMP dispensation kit from which this dose was taken, linking to the randomization and supply chain']
  lot_number varchar [note: 'Manufacturer batch or lot number of the specific IMP unit administered, required for drug accountability and traceability']
  route_of_administration varchar [note: 'Route by which the IMP was administered (oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical, etc.) per protocol specifications']
  study_drug_administered_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the investigational medicinal product (IMP) or study drug was administered to the subject at this visit (True) or not (False). Supports exposure analysis and Intent-to-Treat (ITT) population derivation. [Moved from visit: This boolean flag in visit is a summary indicator that becomes redundant once the detailed imp_administration association exists. The flag can be derived by checking if any imp_administration records exist for the visit. The detailed administration records in the association provide the complete regulatory-required documentation.]']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this IMP administration record, supporting audit trail requirements']

  Note: 'This association product represents the administration event between investigational_product and visit. It captures each instance of IMP dispensation to a trial subject during a clinical visit, documenting regulatory-required accountability data per ICH E6 R2 and 21 CFR Part 312. Each record links one investigational product (specific batch/lot) to one patient visit with administration-specific attributes including timestamp, dose, route, and deviation tracking that exist only in the context of this administration event.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trials, investigational medicinal product (IMP) administration is a core regulatory-mandated business process. A single IMP batch can be administered across multiple patient visits (different subjects, different timepoints), and a single patient visit can involve administration of multiple IMPs (combination therapies, dose escalation, or comparator plus active treatment). Each administration event is a distinct regulatory record with its own timestamp, dose, route, lot traceability, and deviation tracking per ICH E6 R2 and 21 CFR Part 312.'
}

Table clinical.site_imp_accountability {
  site_imp_accountability_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each site-lot accountability record']
  inventory_lot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific IMP inventory lot shipped to and tracked at the site']
  investigational_site_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the investigational site receiving and managing the IMP lot']
  accountability_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the IMP lot at this site for accountability tracking purposes']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the site IMP accountability record was first created in the clinical supply system']
  destruction_date date [note: 'Date on which unused or expired IMP from this lot was destroyed at the site or returned for destruction, with destruction certificate reference']
  discrepancy_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an accountability discrepancy has been identified for this site-lot combination, requiring CAPA and regulatory reporting']
  discrepancy_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text description of any accountability discrepancy, investigation findings, and corrective actions taken']
  dispensed_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Cumulative quantity of the IMP lot dispensed to subjects enrolled at this site, tracked per subject dispensation record']
  last_reconciliation_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent IMP accountability reconciliation performed by the CRA during a site monitoring visit, confirming physical inventory matches accountability records']
  quarantine_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of the IMP lot placed in quarantine at the site due to temperature excursion, packaging damage, or quality hold pending investigation']
  receipt_date date [note: 'Date on which the IMP lot was received at the investigational site, recorded in the site accountability log']
  received_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of the IMP lot received at the investigational site, documented at goods receipt and verified during site monitoring visits']
  returned_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of the IMP lot returned by subjects or returned to the sponsor/depot at site closure or lot expiry']
  shipment_number varchar [note: 'Reference number of the IMP shipment that delivered this lot to the site, linking to depot shipment records and temperature monitoring data']
  storage_location varchar [note: 'Site-specific storage location identifier where this IMP lot is held (e.g., pharmacy refrigerator ID, secure cabinet number), documented during site initiation and verified during monitoring visits']
  temperature_excursion_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this lot experienced a temperature excursion during storage at this site, requiring quality assessment and potential quarantine']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the site IMP accountability record was most recently modified']

  Note: 'This association product represents the accountability relationship between investigational sites and inventory lots of Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP). It captures the regulatory-mandated tracking of IMP receipt, dispensation, return, and storage at each clinical site. Each record links one investigational site to one inventory lot with attributes that exist only in the context of this site-specific lot accountability. Required under ICH GCP E6 and GDP regulations for clinical trial material traceability.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trials, investigational sites receive multiple IMP lots over the trial duration due to resupply cycles, different batch releases, and enrollment progression. Each IMP lot is distributed to multiple sites based on enrollment forecasts and geographic distribution. Site-level IMP accountability is a regulatory-mandated business process under ICH GCP E6 and GDP, where Clinical Research Associates actively create, monitor, and reconcile site-lot accountability records during monitoring visits.'
}

  admitting_privileges_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the HCP has admitting privileges at this site, which may be required for inpatient trials or protocols requiring hospitalization. Critical for site feasibility assessment.']
  affiliation_end_date date [note: 'Date when the HCP\'s affiliation with this investigational site ended or is planned to end. Used to track investigator turnover, site capacity changes, and delegation of authority updates.']
  affiliation_start_date date [note: 'Date when the HCP\'s affiliation with this investigational site became active for clinical trial purposes. May differ from employment start date; represents trial-specific credentialing completion.']
  affiliation_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the HCP\'s relationship to the investigational site for clinical trial purposes. Determines delegation of authority and protocol responsibilities.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the site affiliation record was first created in the clinical data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  credentialing_completion_date date [note: 'Date when the site credentialing process was completed and the HCP was approved to perform protocol activities at this site. Required for regulatory inspection readiness.']
  credentialing_expiration_date date [note: 'Date when the HCP\'s site-specific credentialing expires and must be renewed. Triggers recredentialing workflows to maintain investigator eligibility.']
  credentialing_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the HCP\'s credentialing process at this investigational site. Must be \'Credentialed\' before HCP can perform protocol procedures or enroll subjects. Tracked per site per HCP.']
  department_name varchar [note: 'Name of the clinical department or service line where the HCP practices at this site (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Internal Medicine). Relevant for patient referral pathways and enrollment feasibility.']
  enrollment_authority_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the HCP is authorized to enroll and randomize subjects at this site. Derived from delegation of authority log and protocol-specific training completion.']
  is_primary_site boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this is the HCP\'s primary investigational site affiliation for enrollment and patient care. Used when HCP has privileges at multiple sites to determine primary contact point.']
  role_title varchar [note: 'Specific job title or departmental role the HCP holds at this site (e.g., Chief of Oncology, Attending Physician, Clinical Research Director). Used for delegation of authority documentation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the site affiliation record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking for credentialing status updates and affiliation changes.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the affiliation relationship between investigational sites and healthcare professionals. It captures the operational reality that HCPs hold privileges, credentials, and roles at multiple clinical sites, and sites maintain rosters of affiliated physicians for trial enrollment capacity planning. Each record links one investigational site to one HCP with attributes that govern the HCP\'s ability to serve as investigator, enroll patients, and perform protocol procedures at that specific site.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trials, investigational sites maintain rosters of multiple affiliated physicians with varying roles (Principal Investigator, Sub-Investigator, site staff), and healthcare professionals hold privileges and credentials at multiple sites simultaneously. Site feasibility assessments require understanding which HCPs can enroll patients at which sites, and HCPs leverage multi-site affiliations for patient referral networks. This is an operational relationship actively managed through credentialing workflows, delegation of authority documentation, and site activation processes.'
}

Table clinical.trial_investigator {
  trial_investigator_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each trial-investigator assignment record. Primary key for the association.']
  master_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the healthcare professional serving as investigator on this trial']
  trial_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the clinical trial for which this HCP serves as investigator']
  assignment_end_date date [note: 'Date when this HCP\'s investigator assignment on this trial ended (site closure, investigator departure, trial completion). Null for active assignments. Used for historical investigator portfolio tracking and conflict-of-interest screening.']
  assignment_start_date date [note: 'Date when this HCP was assigned to this trial as an investigator. Typically corresponds to site activation date or investigator onboarding completion. Used for investigator tenure tracking and workload analysis.']
  cv_on_file_date date [note: 'Date when the investigator\'s current CV was received and filed in the eTMF for this trial. Required regulatory document per ICH-GCP. Must be updated if investigator credentials change during trial.']
  delegation_log_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or document ID for the Delegation of Authority Log entry that authorizes this investigator to perform specific trial activities. Required per ICH-GCP for all trial staff. Links to eTMF document management system (Veeva Vault).']
  enrollment_responsibility boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this investigator has patient enrollment responsibilities for this trial. Principal Investigators typically have enrollment responsibility; some Sub-Investigators and Coordinators may not. Drives enrollment tracking and site performance metrics.']
  financial_disclosure_status varchar [note: 'Status of FDA Form 3454 (Financial Disclosure) submission and review for this investigator on this trial. Required for all covered clinical studies per 21 CFR Part 54. Conflict Identified triggers sponsor review and potential investigator exclusion from trial.']
  financial_disclosure_submission_date date [note: 'Date when the investigator submitted financial disclosure documentation for this trial. Required for regulatory submission timelines.']
  gcp_training_date date [note: 'Date when this HCP completed Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training specific to this trial or valid for this trial period. Required before investigator can perform any trial-related activities per ICH-GCP. Must be renewed periodically (typically every 2-3 years).']
  gcp_training_expiration_date date [note: 'Expiration date of the GCP training certification for this investigator on this trial. Triggers re-training workflows and compliance alerts in CTMS.']
  investigator_role varchar [note: 'Role classification for this HCP on this specific trial. Principal Investigator (PI) has ultimate responsibility for trial conduct at the site; Sub-Investigators and Coordinators have delegated responsibilities. Drives regulatory reporting requirements and delegation log structure.']
  investigator_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this investigator assignment on this trial. Active indicates the HCP is currently authorized to perform trial activities. Suspended/Terminated indicates removal from the trial team. Drives access control in EDC systems (Medidata Rave) and eTMF permissions.']
  irb_approval_date date [note: 'Date when the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) approved this investigator to conduct this trial at this site. Required before any trial activities can begin.']
  medical_license_verified_date date [note: 'Date when the sponsor or CRO verified the investigator\'s medical license status for this trial. Required before site activation. Typically re-verified annually during trial conduct.']
  patients_enrolled_count varchar [note: 'Count of patients enrolled by this investigator on this trial. Used for site performance tracking, investigator workload analysis, and enrollment forecasting. Updated as patients are consented and randomized.']
  protocol_deviation_count varchar [note: 'Count of protocol deviations attributed to this investigator on this trial. Used for quality oversight, investigator performance monitoring, and risk-based monitoring (RBM) triggers.']
  site_assignment varchar [note: 'Site identifier or site name where this investigator is assigned for this trial. Links to the clinical site/investigator site record. An HCP may serve as investigator at multiple sites for the same trial (multi-site PI scenarios).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the investigator assignment relationship between clinical trials and healthcare professionals. It captures the operational assignment of HCPs to trials in investigator roles (Principal Investigator, Sub-Investigator, Study Coordinator), including GCP training compliance, financial disclosure status, site-specific responsibilities, delegation of authority, and enrollment accountability. Each record links one trial to one HCP with role-specific attributes that exist only in the context of this investigator assignment. Authoritative SSOT for investigator rosters required for regulatory submissions (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA) and eTMF documentation in Veeva Vault.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trial operations, a single trial requires multiple investigators across sites (Principal Investigators, Sub-Investigators, Study Coordinators), and a single HCP routinely serves as investigator on multiple concurrent trials. The investigator assignment is an operational business entity actively managed by clinical operations teams: assignments are created during site activation, updated as roles/responsibilities change, and tracked throughout the trial lifecycle. The relationship carries substantial operational data (role, GCP training status, financial disclosures, delegation logs, enrollment counts) that belongs to neither the trial nor the HCP alone, but to the specific assignment.'
}

  Note: 'This association product represents the activation and operational lifecycle of a specific protocol version at a specific investigational site. Each record links one investigational site to one protocol version with attributes tracking activation dates, site-specific enrollment targets, training completion, protocol deviations, and closure dates that belong to neither the site nor the protocol alone but to their operational relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trial operations, investigational sites participate in multiple clinical trials (each with its own protocol), and each protocol is activated at multiple investigational sites globally. Site Protocol Activation is a recognized operational entity in CTMS systems, tracking the regulatory, training, enrollment, and compliance lifecycle of each protocol version at each site. This relationship carries substantial operational data (activation dates, site-specific enrollment targets, training completion, deviation counts, closure dates) that belongs to neither the site nor the protocol alone.'

Table clinical.imp_accountability {
  imp_accountability_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the imp_accountability association']
  inventory_lot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific inventory lot (batch) of investigational medicinal product dispensed to this trial']
  site_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific clinical site (investigator location) where this lot was shipped and dispensed. Critical for site-level accountability reconciliation and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  trial_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the clinical trial that received and used this inventory lot for patient dosing or study procedures']
  accountability_status varchar [note: 'Current reconciliation status of this trial-lot accountability record. Open = active dispensation; Reconciled = all quantities accounted for; Discrepancy = variance requiring investigation; Closed = final reconciliation complete and documented.']
  destruction_certificate_number varchar [note: 'Reference number of the destruction certificate issued by the site or destruction vendor for this lot. Required regulatory documentation for destroyed IMP.']
  destruction_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of this lot destroyed at the site per protocol (expired, damaged, or end-of-study destruction). Requires destruction certificate for regulatory compliance.']
  discrepancy_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text explanation of any accountability discrepancy (quantity variance, missing documentation, temperature excursion during shipment). Triggers CAPA if material.']
  dispensed_date date [note: 'Date on which this lot was first dispensed to a patient in this trial at this site. Critical for expiry compliance verification and audit trail.']
  dispensed_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total quantity of this lot dispensed to patients at the site for this trial. Used for accountability reconciliation: dispensed + returned + destroyed must equal shipped quantity.']
  reconciliation_date date [note: 'Date on which this trial-lot accountability record was formally reconciled and closed by the clinical monitor or site coordinator. Required for database lock and CSR completion.']
  remaining_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of this lot currently remaining at the site (not yet dispensed, returned, or destroyed). Calculated field for real-time accountability tracking.']
  return_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of this lot returned by the site (unused drug product returned to sponsor or depot). Part of the accountability reconciliation equation.']
  shipped_date date [note: 'Date on which this lot was shipped from the depot to the clinical site for use in this trial. Start of the accountability timeline.']
  shipped_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Total quantity of this lot shipped to the site for this trial. Baseline for accountability reconciliation. Must equal dispensed + returned + destroyed + remaining.']
  temperature_monitoring_compliant boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this lot maintained required storage conditions throughout its lifecycle at the site for this trial. False triggers deviation investigation.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the accountability record between clinical trials and inventory lots of investigational medicinal products (IMPs). It captures the dispensation, return, and destruction of specific drug product lots used in clinical trials, ensuring full traceability and regulatory compliance per GCP and 21 CFR Part 312. Each record links one trial to one inventory lot with quantities, dates, and accountability status that exist only in the context of this trial-lot relationship. This is the authoritative SSOT for IMP accountability reconciliation required for regulatory inspections and CSR appendices.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical operations, trials consume multiple inventory lots over their lifecycle due to resupply needs, dose escalation cohorts, and multi-site distribution, while individual lots (especially in Phase I or multi-indication studies) are allocated across multiple concurrent trials. IMP accountability is a regulated operational process where clinical teams actively create, monitor, and reconcile dispensation records for each trial-lot combination, tracking quantities dispensed, returned, and destroyed per GCP requirements.'
}

Each record links one trial to one vendor with contractual terms, service scope, performance metrics, and deliverables that exist only in the context of this engagement relationship. This is the authoritative SSOT for vendor-trial service agreements consumed by procurement, clinical operations, and trial management systems.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trial operations, trials routinely engage multiple vendors simultaneously (CRO for trial management, central lab for sample analysis, CMO for IMP manufacturing, imaging vendor for endpoint assessment, SMO for site recruitment), and vendors serve multiple trials concurrently across the sponsor\'s portfolio. The business actively manages these vendor-trial engagements as distinct operational entities with contractual terms, service scopes, performance metrics, and deliverables tracked per engagement.'

  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this regulatory application record was most recently modified in the data platform. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.']
  vault_document_reference varchar [note: 'The unique document or object identifier assigned to this application record in Veeva Vault RIM, enabling traceability back to the source system of record for the regulatory dossier.']

  Note: 'Master record for a regulatory application (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, ANDA, 510k) representing the formal dossier filed with a health authority for a specific drug product. Tracks application number assigned by the agency, application type, applicant entity, lead product, therapeutic indication, regulatory pathway, orphan designation status, priority review status, PDUFA/action date, and overall approval status. One application may have multiple submissions (original + supplements).'

SSOT for all health authority communications — no separate correspondence product exists. Sourced from Veeva Vault RIM correspondence and meeting modules.'

  pai_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) for the manufacturing site or process covered by this DMF.   updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this DMF record in the regulatory data product. Supports change tracking, audit trail compliance, and data freshness monitoring.']
  veeva_vault_document_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management System) corresponding to this DMF record. Enables traceability between the data product and the source system of record for regulatory document management.']
  withdrawal_date date [note: 'Date on which the DMF was formally withdrawn by the holder or closed by the health authority. Null for active DMFs. Used to manage the lifecycle of supplier relationships and assess impact on referencing applications.']

  Note: 'Drug Master File (DMF) registry tracking all DMFs filed with health authorities for APIs, excipients, packaging materials, and manufacturing sites. Captures DMF number, DMF type (Type I-V), holder name, subject of DMF, filing date, last annual update date, authorization letters issued, and associated products referencing the DMF. Supports CMC regulatory strategy and third-party supplier qualification. Aligns with 21 CFR 314.420 and EMA DMF guidelines.'
}

  post_approval_commitment_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this registration carries outstanding post-approval commitments or conditions imposed by the health authority (e.g., Phase IV studies, risk management measures, label updates). True = open commitments exist.']
  registration_date date [note: 'Date on which the marketing authorization or product registration was officially granted by the health authority. This is the EFFECTIVE_FROM date for the MASTER_AGREEMENT role — the date the registration became binding.']
  registration_holder varchar [note: 'Legal entity name of the Marketing Authorization Holder (MAH) or registration holder responsible for maintaining this registration in the country. May differ from the parent company in cases of local affiliates or licensing partners.']
  registration_number varchar [note: 'Official marketing authorization or product registration number assigned by the health authority in the country of registration (e.g., NDA number, EU MA number, NMPA approval number). This is the externally-known business identifier for the registration.']
  registration_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the product registration in the given country. Active = valid and commercially available; Suspended = temporarily halted by authority or holder; Withdrawn = permanently removed; Expired = lapsed without renewal; Pending Renewal = renewal submitted and under review.']
  rems_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is required for this product registration in the applicable market. Applicable primarily to FDA-regulated products.']
  renewal_approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the health authority granted approval of the renewal application, extending the validity of the marketing authorization.']
  renewal_due_date date [note: 'Calendar date by which the renewal application must be submitted to the health authority to prevent registration lapse. Critical for renewal calendar management and commercial continuity planning.']
  renewal_fee_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Monetary amount of the regulatory renewal fee payable to the health authority for this registration renewal. Expressed in the local currency of the health authority jurisdiction.']
  renewal_fee_currency varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the renewal fee amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CNY).']
  renewal_fee_status varchar [note: 'Payment status of the regulatory renewal fee due to the health authority for this registration renewal cycle. Unpaid or overdue fees can result in registration lapse.']
  renewal_outcome varchar [note: 'Outcome of the most recent renewal application for this registration. Approved = renewal granted; Refused = health authority denied renewal; Withdrawn by Holder = MAH withdrew the renewal application; Pending = renewal submitted and under review; Not Submitted = renewal not yet submitted.']
  renewal_submission_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the renewal application dossier was submitted to the health authority. Used to confirm timely submission and calculate submission lead time against the renewal due date.']
  renewal_type varchar [note: 'Type of renewal cycle applicable to this registration as defined by the health authority. Five-year = standard EU/ICH 5-year renewal; Annual = annual renewal required (e.g., certain PMDA registrations); Sunset Clause = registration lapses if product not marketed within defined period; Indefinite = no renewal required after initial grant; Not Applicable = renewal not applicable in this jurisdiction.']
  route_of_administration varchar [note: 'Approved route of administration for the registered drug product as stated in the marketing authorization (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, topical, inhalation).']
  strength varchar [note: 'Approved strength(s) of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) as stated in the marketing authorization (e.g., 10 mg, 100 mg/mL, 500 mg/5 mL). Multiple strengths may be listed as a delimited string if covered under a single registration number.']
  sunset_clause_date date [note: 'Date by which the product must be placed on the market in the registered country to avoid automatic lapse of the registration under the sunset clause provision. Applicable in EU and certain other jurisdictions where a registration lapses if the product is not marketed within 3 years of grant.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Therapeutic area classification of the registered product (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Used for portfolio analytics and commercial reporting.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this product registration record was most recently updated in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing.']
  veeva_vault_document_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) system corresponding to the registration dossier and supporting documents for this product registration. Enables traceability to the source system of record.']

  Note: 'Single source of truth for country-level product registration master tracking the marketing authorization status, complete renewal lifecycle, and maintenance calendar of each drug product in each country/market. Captures registration number, country, registration holder, registration date, expiry date, approved indication, approved dosage forms and strengths, local brand name, and registration status (active, suspended, withdrawn, expired). Includes complete renewal tracking: renewal type (5-year, annual, sunset clause), renewal due dates, submission dates, approval dates, fee payment status, and renewal outcomes. Manages the renewal calendar across all markets to prevent registration lapse. SSOT for global product registration footprint, renewal compliance, and commercial continuity — no separate renewal product exists.'
}

Lapsed indicates the registration has expired without successful renewal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned|in_preparation|submitted|under_review|approved|rejected|withdrawn|lapsed — promote to reference product]']
  renewal_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the renewal cycle required by the health authority. Five-year renewal is standard in EU/EMA; annual renewal applies in certain markets; sunset clause applies when a product has not been marketed within three years of initial authorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: five_year_renewal|annual_renewal|sunset_clause|conditional_renewal|exceptional_circumstances — promote to reference product]']

  post_approval_commitment_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent post-approval commitment record that this action belongs to. Links the granular action to its higher-level regulatory obligation.']
  responsible_owner_employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Commitment actions require structured employee ownership for execution tracking, milestone management, and accountability. Essential for action-level workload management and performance tracking. Repl']
  action_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the specific task or deliverable required to fulfill this commitment action, as agreed with or imposed by the health authority. Provides operational clarity for the responsible function.']
  action_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for this specific action, often referenced in agency correspondence and commitment tracking systems (e.g., PMC-2024-001-A1). Used for cross-referencing with health authority communications.']
  action_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this commitment action, reflecting its progress toward fulfillment. Drives operational dashboards and health authority reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|in_progress|submitted|completed|overdue|waived|deferred — promote to reference product]']
  action_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the deliverable type required for this action (e.g., protocol submission, interim report, final study report, label update). Determines the nature of the work and the responsible function. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: promote to reference product if values expand beyond 6]']
  agency_imposed_date date [note: 'The date on which the health authority formally imposed or agreed to this commitment action, typically the approval date or the date of the commitment letter. Serves as the BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP for this transaction.']
  agency_reference_number varchar [note: 'The reference number assigned by the health authority to this specific commitment action or the correspondence in which it was imposed (e.g., FDA PMC number, EMA commitment reference). Used for agency correspondence and annual reporting.']
  commitment_category varchar [note: 'Regulatory category of the commitment under which this action falls. PMR (Post-Marketing Requirement) is legally mandated; PMC (Post-Marketing Commitment) is voluntarily agreed. Specific Obligation and Follow-Up Measure are EMA-specific categories.']
  completion_date date [note: 'The actual date on which this commitment action was completed internally (e.g., study completed, report finalized). Distinct from submission date; used to measure internal execution performance against the due date.']
  completion_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text notes documenting the outcome, findings, or any relevant context upon completion of this commitment action. May include summary of study results, reasons for delay, or agency feedback received.']

  deferral_reason varchar [note: 'Documented reason for deferring this commitment action beyond its original due date, including whether the deferral was agency-approved or internally initiated. Supports compliance audit and risk management.']
  deliverable_title varchar [note: 'The formal title of the document or deliverable produced to fulfill this action (e.g., \'Phase 4 Pediatric Safety Study Final Report\', \'Updated Prescribing Information\'). Used for document management and health authority correspondence.']
  due_date date [note: 'The date by which this commitment action must be completed and/or submitted to the health authority, as specified in the approval letter, commitment schedule, or agency agreement. Critical for compliance monitoring.']
  ectd_sequence_number varchar [note: 'The eCTD sequence number of the submission in which the deliverable for this action was filed with the health authority. Enables traceability to the specific regulatory submission dossier.']
