  quantity_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure applicable to quantity_distributed and quantity_recovered fields (e.g., EA=Each, BT=Bottle, VL=Vial, AMP=Ampoule, PKG=Package, KG=Kilogram, L=Liter). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|BT|VL|AMP|PKG|KG|L — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  recall_class varchar [note: 'FDA-defined classification indicating the severity of the health hazard associated with the recalled product. Class I: serious adverse health consequences or death; Class II: temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences; Class III: unlikely to cause adverse health consequences.']
  recall_closure_date date [note: 'The date on which the recall was formally closed or terminated by the regulatory authority or the company after all recall activities, effectiveness checks, and documentation requirements were completed.']
  recall_effectiveness_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of distributed product that has been successfully recovered or accounted for, calculated as (quantity_recovered / quantity_distributed) * 100. Key metric for FDA recall effectiveness checks and regulatory reporting under 21 CFR Part 7.']
  recall_initiated_date date [note: 'The date on which the recall was formally initiated by the company or ordered by the regulatory authority. Represents the principal business event timestamp for the recall lifecycle.']
  recall_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional operational notes, regulatory correspondence summaries, or contextual information relevant to the recall event that is not captured in structured fields.']
  recall_number varchar [note: 'Externally-assigned recall identification number issued by the regulatory authority (e.g., FDA recall number) or internally assigned by the company for voluntary recalls. Serves as the primary business identifier for tracking and referencing the recall event across regulatory submissions and communications.']
  recall_reason_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code categorizing the root cause or reason for the recall (e.g., contamination, labeling error, sub-potency, sterility failure, foreign particulate). Aligns with FDA recall reason taxonomy for regulatory reporting and trend analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Contamination|Labeling Error|Sub-Potency|Super-Potency|Sterility Failure|Foreign Particulate|Stability Failure|Packaging Defect|Microbial Contamination|Other — promote to reference product]']
  recall_reason_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the specific defect, violation, or safety concern that triggered the recall. Provides the full technical and regulatory context beyond the recall reason code, including root cause findings from CAPA investigations.']
  recall_scope varchar [note: 'Geographic scope of the recall indicating whether the recall covers the entire national market, specific regions, international markets, or is limited to a specific manufacturing or distribution site.']
  recall_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the recall event. Pending: recall initiated but not yet active; Active: recall in progress with field corrections underway; Monitoring: recall effectiveness checks ongoing; Terminated: FDA has terminated the recall; Closed: all recall activities completed and documented.']
  recall_strategy varchar [note: 'Description of the recall strategy approved by the regulatory authority or company, including the depth of recall, communication methods, effectiveness check methodology, and disposition instructions for recovered product.']
  recall_type varchar [note: 'Categorization of the recall initiation type. Voluntary recalls are company-initiated; Mandatory recalls are ordered by a regulatory authority; Market Withdrawal involves minor violations not subject to legal action; Stock Recovery involves products not yet distributed to the market.']
  regulatory_notification_date date [note: 'The date on which the company formally notified the relevant regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA) of the recall initiation. Critical compliance milestone tracked under 21 CFR Part 7 and equivalent international regulations.']
  regulatory_submission_ref varchar [note: 'Reference number or identifier for the regulatory submission (e.g., NDA, BLA, MAA) associated with the recalled product. Links the recall event to the product\'s regulatory dossier for compliance tracking in RIMS.']
  sku_code varchar [note: 'The Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) code identifying the specific commercial packaging configuration of the recalled product as used in SAP MM/WM and supply chain systems. Enables traceability at the packaging level across distribution channels.']

  Note: 'Pharmaceutical product recall event record initiated by regulatory authority mandate or voluntary company action. Captures recall number, recall class (Class I, II, III per FDA), affected NDC, affected lot numbers, recall scope (market, distribution level), recall reason, regulatory agency notification date, press release date, customer notification status, quantity recovered, and recall closure date. Supports lot traceability and regulatory reporting obligations under 21 CFR Part 7.'
}

  cold_chain_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this lot requires cold-chain handling and storage conditions (e.g., 2–8°C refrigerated, -20°C frozen, -80°C ultra-cold). Drives GDP-compliant logistics routing, carrier selection, and temperature monitoring requirements.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this traceability record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11 for electronic records.']
  deviation_reference_number varchar [note: 'Reference number of any GMP deviation, OOS (Out of Specification), or OOT (Out of Trend) investigation associated with this lot or transformation step. Links to the Quality Management System (MasterControl/TrackWise) for CAPA tracking.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The expiration date assigned to the child lot, beyond which the material must not be used or distributed. Determined by stability studies and shelf-life specifications. Critical for GDP compliance, inventory management, and recall scope determination.']
  gdp_compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the transformation and handling of this lot was performed in compliance with Good Distribution Practice (GDP) guidelines. FALSE triggers a quality investigation. Required for EU distribution authorization and WHO prequalification.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp of the most recent modification to this traceability record, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Required for audit trail completeness under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11. Supports incremental data loading in the Databricks Silver layer.']
  manufacture_date date [note: 'The official date of manufacture assigned to the child lot, as recorded on the Certificate of Analysis (CoA) and batch record. Used for shelf-life calculation, regulatory reporting, and lot genealogy.']
  material_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the child lot material type within the pharmaceutical supply chain hierarchy. Drives traceability chain logic, regulatory reporting scope, and GDP compliance requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: raw_material|api|excipient|packaging_component|drug_substance|drug_product|finished_goods|clinical_supply — promote to reference product]']
  ndc_code varchar [note: 'The FDA-assigned National Drug Code (NDC) for the child lot material, in the standard 5-4-2 format. Applicable to commercial finished goods. Used for regulatory traceability, serialization compliance, and distribution tracking under DSCSA.']
  process_order_number varchar [note: 'SAP PP process order number or manufacturing work order number that authorized and tracked the transformation operation. Provides the operational link between the traceability record and the ERP production execution.']
  qp_release_status varchar [note: 'The Qualified Person (QP) or Authorized Person (AP) release status of the child lot. \'released\' indicates the lot has been certified by a QP for distribution per EU GMP Annex 16. \'rejected\' indicates the lot failed QP review. Required for EU market distribution and clinical supply.']
  quantity_in decimal(18,4) [note: 'The quantity of the parent lot material consumed or input into the transformation step. Expressed in the unit of measure defined by quantity_uom. Used for yield calculation and GMP batch record reconciliation.']
  quantity_out decimal(18,4) [note: 'The quantity of the child lot material produced or output from the transformation step. Expressed in the unit of measure defined by quantity_uom. Used for yield calculation and GMP batch record reconciliation.']
  quantity_uom varchar [note: 'Unit of measure applicable to both quantity_in and quantity_out fields (e.g., kg for API, units for finished tablets, vials for injectables). Aligns with SAP MM base unit of measure for the material. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: kg|g|mg|L|mL|units|tablets|vials|bottles|capsules — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  recall_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this lot is subject to an active product recall. Set to TRUE when a recall action is initiated by the company or regulatory authority. Enables rapid identification of affected lots across the traceability chain for recall scope determination.']
  recall_reference_number varchar [note: 'The regulatory or internal recall reference number associated with this lot when recall_flag is TRUE. Links the traceability record to the formal recall action for scope tracking, regulatory reporting, and pharmacovigilance investigation.']
  retest_date date [note: 'The date by which the child lot material (typically API or drug substance) must be retested to confirm continued compliance with specifications before use. Applicable to materials with retest periods rather than expiry dates per ICH Q7.']
  serialization_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this lot requires unit-level serialization per DSCSA (US), FMD (EU Falsified Medicines Directive), or other track-and-trace regulations. Drives serialization system integration and aggregation hierarchy management.']
  sku_code varchar [note: 'The internal Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) code for the child lot material as defined in the ERP/WMS system. Used for inventory management, demand planning integration with Kinaxis/Blue Yonder, and commercial distribution tracking.']
  storage_condition varchar [note: 'The required storage condition for the child lot material as specified in the product dossier and CoA. Drives warehouse slotting, GDP compliance, and cold-chain logistics planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ambient|refrigerated|frozen|ultra_cold|controlled_room_temp|protect_from_light|controlled_substance — promote to reference product]']
  supply_chain_segment varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this traceability record belongs to the commercial supply chain, the clinical trial supply chain, or spans both. Clinical supply chain records require additional IND/CTA traceability and blinding controls.']
  theoretical_yield decimal(18,4) [note: 'The maximum expected quantity of output material based on the bill of materials and batch formula, expressed in quantity_uom. Used to calculate actual vs. theoretical yield variance for GMP batch record review and OOS/OOT investigations.']
  traceability_chain_level varchar [note: 'Numeric level in the lot genealogy hierarchy, where level 1 represents the raw material/API input and higher levels represent downstream transformation steps (e.g., level 2 = drug substance, level 3 = drug product, level 4 = finished goods). Enables hierarchical traceability chain traversal for recall scope and genealogy reporting.']
  traceability_chain_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this traceability linkage record. \'active\' indicates a valid, in-use chain link; \'recalled\' flags lots subject to a market recall; \'under_investigation\' indicates a pharmacovigilance or quality investigation is open; \'invalidated\' marks records superseded by corrections.']
  traceability_record_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for this traceability linkage record. Used in regulatory submissions, recall investigations, and GMP batch record cross-references. Typically sourced from SAP MM/WM or MES batch record systems.']
  transformation_date date [note: 'The calendar date on which the manufacturing, packaging, or supply chain transformation operation was performed, converting the parent lot into the child lot. Principal business event date for this traceability record.']
  transformation_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the manufacturing or supply chain operation that converted the parent lot into the child lot. Drives traceability chain logic and GMP batch record linkage. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: manufacturing|packaging|repackaging|blending|filling|labelling|sampling|testing|transfer — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]']
  yield_pct decimal(7,4) [note: 'The process yield expressed as a percentage, calculated as (quantity_out / quantity_in) × 100. Stored as a business-critical GMP metric for batch record review, deviation investigation, and process performance trending. Out-of-specification yield triggers CAPA.']

  Note: 'End-to-end lot/batch traceability record linking raw material lots through drug substance, drug product, and finished goods lots across the pharmaceutical supply chain. Captures parent lot, child lot, material, transformation type (manufacturing, packaging, repackaging), site, transformation date, quantity in, quantity out, yield, and traceability chain status. Supports regulatory recall traceability, pharmacovigilance investigations, and GMP batch record linkage. Critical for 21 CFR Part 211 and EU GMP Annex 11 compliance.'
}

Table supply.fulfillment_event {
  fulfillment_event_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for fulfillment_event']
  reported_by_employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Supply chain excursions require documented reporter for CAPA assignment, deviation management, and regulatory reportability assessment. New attribute needed; removes denormalized reported_by text fiel']
  shipment_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the pharmaceutical shipment record associated with this event. Links the event to the specific shipment leg, delivery document, or transport order in the distribution network.']
  stock_transfer_order_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the stock transfer order associated with this event, linking to the supply.stock_transfer_order product for intra-company or inter-site material movements.']
  storage_location_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the storage or transit location where the supply chain event occurred. Covers manufacturing sites, distribution centers, third-party logistics (3PL) warehouses, customs facilities, and clinical trial depots.']
  affected_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'The quantity of pharmaceutical material directly affected by this supply chain event (e.g., quantity of product in a temperature-excursed shipment, quantity subject to a supply disruption, quantity reallocated in an allocation change event).']
  capa_reference varchar [note: 'The CAPA identifier from the Quality Management System (MasterControl or TrackWise) linked to this supply chain event. Populated when a formal CAPA has been initiated in response to a GDP deviation, temperature excursion, or supply disruption.']
  carrier_name varchar [note: 'The name of the carrier, courier, or third-party logistics (3PL) provider responsible for the shipment at the time of this event. Relevant for GDP qualification tracking and carrier performance management.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this fulfillment event record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GDP Guidelines. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  deviation_reference varchar [note: 'The formal quality deviation or non-conformance report number from the QMS (MasterControl/TrackWise) associated with this event. Distinct from CAPA reference — a deviation may exist without a CAPA if the risk is low.']
  event_description varchar [note: 'Free-text narrative description of the supply chain event, providing operational context, observed conditions, and initial assessment. Captured by the logistics operator, quality team, or automated monitoring system at the time of event detection.']
  event_location_description varchar [note: 'Human-readable description of the location where the event occurred, including site name, warehouse zone, or transit leg description. Complements the location ID for operational reporting and GDP deviation documentation.']
  event_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier for the fulfillment event, used for cross-system referencing and communication with logistics partners, CROs, and CMOs. Sourced from SAP S/4HANA SD/WM or Kinaxis RapidResponse.']
  event_source_system varchar [note: 'The operational system of record that originated or captured this supply chain event. Enables data lineage tracing and source system reconciliation across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis RapidResponse, Blue Yonder, IoT monitoring devices, courier portals, LIMS, and MES platforms. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: SAP_S4HANA|Kinaxis_RapidResponse|Blue_Yonder|manual_entry|IoT_sensor|courier_portal|LIMS|MES — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  event_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the fulfillment event record, tracking whether the event is newly identified, under active investigation, resolved with corrective action, formally closed, or escalated to regulatory or senior management.']
  event_subtype varchar [note: 'Granular classification within the event type. Examples: for shipment_milestone — departed, in_transit, arrived, delivered, customs_hold; for temperature_excursion — cold_chain_breach, freeze_event, heat_event; for gdp_deviation — documentation_gap, unauthorized_access, pest_control, vehicle_hygiene. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: departed|in_transit|arrived|delivered|customs_hold|cold_chain_breach|freeze_event|heat_event|documentation_gap|unauthorized_access|pest_control|vehicle_hygiene — promote to reference product]']
  event_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time at which the supply chain event occurred in the real world (e.g., when a shipment departed, when a temperature excursion was detected, when a GDP deviation was identified). Distinct from record audit timestamps. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  event_type varchar [note: 'Discriminator classifying the nature of the supply chain event. Shipment milestones cover departed/in-transit/arrived/delivered states; temperature excursions cover cold-chain breaches; GDP deviations cover documentation gaps, unauthorized access, pest control; supply disruptions cover material shortages; allocation changes cover demand reallocation; ATP exceptions cover available-to-promise failures.']
  excursion_duration_minutes varchar [note: 'The total duration in minutes of a temperature or humidity excursion event, from first breach detection to return within acceptable limits. Used for mean kinetic temperature (MKT) calculations and product impact assessments. Null for non-excursion events.']
  excursion_severity varchar [note: 'The severity classification of a temperature, humidity, or GDP excursion event. Minor excursions may be within product stability limits; major excursions require quality investigation; critical excursions may necessitate product quarantine, destruction, or regulatory reporting. Null for non-excursion events.']
  gdp_guideline_reference varchar [note: 'The specific GDP guideline clause or section number that is relevant to this event or deviation. Examples: EU GDP 2013/C 343/01 Chapter 6.3 (Temperature Control), WHO GDP TRS 957 Annex 5 Section 8. Supports regulatory inspection readiness and deviation documentation.']
  humidity_reading_pct decimal(5,2) [note: 'The relative humidity percentage recorded at the time of the event. Relevant for moisture-sensitive pharmaceutical products and storage condition compliance monitoring. Null for non-environmental events.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this fulfillment event record was most recently modified. Tracks status changes, resolution updates, and CAPA linkages. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.']
  lot_number varchar [note: 'The manufacturing lot or batch number of the pharmaceutical material affected by this event. Critical for GMP traceability, recall management, and GDP compliance. Aligns with SAP batch management and LIMS batch records.']
  material_number varchar [note: 'SAP material number or equivalent ERP identifier for the pharmaceutical material affected by this event. Covers APIs, excipients, packaging components, drug substances, and finished drug products.']
  monitoring_device_code varchar [note: 'The unique identifier of the temperature/humidity monitoring device (data logger, IoT sensor, or continuous monitoring system) that captured the environmental reading associated with this event. Supports device calibration traceability and GDP audit trails.']
  ndc_code varchar [note: 'The U.S. National Drug Code identifying the specific drug product, dosage form, and package size affected by this event. Used for regulatory traceability and DSCSA compliance for finished pharmaceutical products.']
  product_quarantine_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the affected pharmaceutical material has been placed in quarantine status as a result of this event. When True, the material is blocked from further distribution pending quality investigation and disposition decision.']
  quantity_uom varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for the affected quantity field. Standard pharmaceutical units include each (EA), kilograms (KG), litres (L), millilitres (mL), grams (g), milligrams (mg), vials, bottles, cartons, and pallets. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|KG|L|mL|g|mg|vials|bottles|cartons|pallets — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  regulatory_authority varchar [note: 'The regulatory authority to which this event must be reported, if regulatory_reportable is True. Applicable for events involving product quality failures, GDP deviations, or controlled substance discrepancies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|DEA|other — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  regulatory_reportable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this supply chain event requires regulatory reporting to health authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA). True for events such as critical GDP deviations, product recalls, or significant cold-chain failures affecting product quality and patient safety.']
  resolution_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the actions taken to resolve this supply chain event, including corrective measures, product disposition decisions, and process improvements implemented. Populated when event_status transitions to resolved or closed.']
  resolved_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time at which the supply chain event was formally resolved and closed in the QMS or supply chain system. Used to calculate event resolution cycle time for GDP KPI reporting.']
  sku_code varchar [note: 'The Stock Keeping Unit code identifying the specific commercial or clinical product variant affected by this event, including pack size and configuration. Used for inventory management and commercial distribution tracking.']
  source_system_event_code varchar [note: 'The native identifier of this event in the originating source system (e.g., SAP delivery document number, Kinaxis event ID, IoT platform alert ID). Supports cross-system traceability and deduplication during ETL processing.']
  storage_condition_required varchar [note: 'The required storage condition for the affected pharmaceutical material as per product specification and regulatory labelling. Used to assess the impact of excursion events against the product\'s approved storage requirements.']
  supply_chain_segment varchar [note: 'Identifies whether this event pertains to the commercial supply chain, clinical trial supply chain, product returns/reverse logistics, or sample distribution. Enables segregated reporting and compliance tracking across supply chain segments.']
  temperature_reading_c decimal(6,2) [note: 'The actual temperature reading in degrees Celsius recorded at the time of the event. Critical for cold-chain integrity monitoring of biologics, vaccines, and temperature-sensitive APIs. Null for non-temperature-related events.']
  tracking_number varchar [note: 'The carrier-assigned tracking number or waybill number for the shipment associated with this event. Enables real-time shipment visibility and event correlation with carrier tracking systems.']

  Note: 'Unified event log capturing all supply chain milestones, exceptions, and deviations across the pharmaceutical distribution network. Includes shipment milestones (departed, in-transit, arrived, delivered), temperature and environmental excursions during cold-chain storage/transit (biologics, vaccines, APIs), GDP deviations (documentation gaps, unauthorized access, pest control), supply disruptions, allocation changes, and ATP exceptions. Captures event type, event timestamp, affected material, lot, shipment or storage location reference, temperature/humidity readings, monitoring device ID, excursion severity (minor, major, critical), GDP guideline reference, CAPA reference, regulatory reportability flag, event source system, and resolution status. Supports GDP compliance per EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 343/01, WHO GDP guidelines, and cold-chain integrity assurance. SSOT for all supply chain event and exception tracking.'
}

  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this cold chain monitoring record was most recently modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']
  location_code varchar [note: 'The unique identifier or code for the specific facility, warehouse, or site where the temperature monitoring occurred.']
  location_type varchar [note: 'The category of location where the temperature monitoring occurred, indicating the supply chain segment.']
  monitoring_device_code varchar [note: 'Unique identifier of the temperature monitoring device or data logger used to capture the reading. Required for device calibration traceability.']
  monitoring_event_code varchar [note: 'Business identifier for the temperature monitoring event or data collection session. Used for traceability and audit purposes.']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional comments, observations, or contextual information related to the temperature monitoring event or excursion.']
  reading_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The precise date and time when the temperature or humidity reading was captured by the monitoring device. Critical for excursion analysis.']
  regulatory_report_date date [note: 'The date when the temperature excursion event was reported to the relevant regulatory authority, if reporting was required.']
  regulatory_reportable boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator whether the temperature excursion event requires reporting to regulatory authorities such as FDA, EMA, or other health agencies.']
  serial_number varchar [note: 'Unique serialization identifier for the individual package or pallet being monitored, if serialization is implemented.']
  storage_condition_required varchar [note: 'The required storage condition classification for the pharmaceutical product as defined in the product specification and regulatory approval.']
  storage_zone varchar [note: 'The specific storage zone, room, or area within the facility where the product was located during monitoring.']
  supply_chain_segment varchar [note: 'The segment of the pharmaceutical supply chain where the temperature monitoring occurred, enabling segment-specific analysis.']
  temperature_max_threshold_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'The maximum acceptable temperature in degrees Celsius for the product storage condition. Readings above this trigger an excursion event.']
  temperature_min_threshold_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'The minimum acceptable temperature in degrees Celsius for the product storage condition. Readings below this trigger an excursion event.']
  temperature_reading_c decimal(5,2) [note: 'The actual temperature measurement in degrees Celsius recorded by the monitoring device at the reading timestamp.']
  tracking_number varchar [note: 'The carrier-assigned tracking number for the shipment, enabling correlation with carrier systems and proof of delivery.']

  Note: 'Transactional record capturing temperature monitoring data points and excursion events for cold-chain pharmaceutical products during storage and transit, including sensor readings, excursion duration, and disposition decisions'
}

Table supply.drug_dispensation {
  drug_dispensation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each drug dispensation record linking a lot to a patient']
  employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the clinical site pharmacist or coordinator who performed the dispensation']
  inventory_lot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific inventory lot from which the drug was dispensed to the patient']
  patient_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the clinical trial participant who received the drug from this lot']

  dispense_location varchar [note: 'Clinical site code or pharmacy location where the dispensation occurred']
  dispense_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of drug dispensed from the lot to the patient, measured in the lot\'s unit of measure']
  dispense_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the dispensation record for drug accountability tracking']
  gdp_compliance_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this dispensation met Good Distribution Practice requirements for temperature, handling, and documentation']
  kit_number varchar [note: 'Unique kit identifier for the dispensed investigational product package, used for IRT/IWRS reconciliation']
  return_date date [note: 'Date on which unused drug from this dispensation was returned to the site pharmacy or destroyed']
  return_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'Quantity of drug returned from the patient, used for drug accountability reconciliation']
  return_reason varchar [note: 'Reason code or free-text explanation for why drug was returned (e.g., patient discontinuation, dose adjustment, study completion)']
  temperature_at_dispense decimal(5,2) [note: 'Recorded storage temperature at time of dispensation for cold chain compliance verification']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'System timestamp when the dispensation record was last modified']
  visit_number varchar [note: 'Clinical trial visit or cycle number during which the dispensation occurred, linking to EDC visit schedule']

  Note: 'This association product represents the dispensation event between inventory_lot and patient in clinical trials. It captures the operational record of investigational product or commercial drug being dispensed from a specific lot to a specific trial participant. Each record links one inventory_lot to one patient with attributes that exist only in the context of this dispensation transaction, including dispense date, quantity, location, status, and return information for GDP compliance and clinical trial accountability.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical clinical trials, drug dispensation represents a true operational many-to-many relationship. A single inventory lot is dispensed to multiple patients over the course of a trial (one lot serves many participants across visits), and a single patient receives drug from multiple lots throughout their trial participation (across visits, cycles, or dose adjustments). The dispensation event is actively managed by clinical supply teams and site pharmacists as a distinct business process with its own lifecycle, attributes, and regulatory requirements.'
}

Table supply.distribution_service_agreement {
  distribution_service_agreement_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each distribution service agreement record linking a distribution node to a payer account']
  distribution_network_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the distribution network node providing service under this agreement']
  payer_account_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the payer account receiving distribution service under this agreement']
  agreement_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the distribution service agreement. Active agreements govern current shipments; Suspended agreements are temporarily inactive; Terminated agreements are historical.']
  cold_chain_capability varchar [note: 'Temperature control capability required and committed for shipments from this distribution node to this payer account. Must match or exceed product temperature requirements.']
  cost_allocation_code varchar [note: 'Internal accounting code used to allocate distribution costs for shipments under this agreement. Links to cost center or GL account for financial reporting.']
  delivery_lead_time_days varchar [note: 'Contractual number of calendar days from order placement to delivery for shipments from this distribution node to this payer account. Used for supply planning and order promising.']
  direct_delivery_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether shipments under this agreement are delivered directly from the distribution node to the payer\'s designated location (True) or routed through intermediary wholesalers/distributors (False).']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date on which this distribution service agreement becomes active and governs shipments from the distribution node to the payer account.']
  minimum_order_quantity varchar [note: 'Minimum number of units or pallets required per shipment under this distribution service agreement. Used to optimize logistics efficiency and cost.']
  preferred_carrier varchar [note: 'Name of the logistics carrier designated for shipments under this distribution service agreement (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL, specialty pharma courier). May be mandated by payer or selected by supply chain.']
  serialization_verification_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this payer account requires serialization verification at the distribution node level for DSCSA compliance or payer-specific track-and-trace requirements.']
  service_level_agreement varchar [note: 'Classification of the service level commitment governing this distribution relationship (Standard, Expedited, Critical, Custom). Determines delivery speed, handling priority, and cost structure.']
  termination_date date [note: 'Date on which this distribution service agreement expires or was terminated. Null indicates an active, ongoing agreement.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the contractual service agreement between a distribution network node and a payer account. It captures the operational service level commitments, delivery parameters, and cold-chain capabilities that govern how pharmaceutical products flow from specific distribution nodes to specific payer organizations. Each record links one distribution_network node to one payer_account with service-level attributes that exist only in the context of this distribution relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical supply chain operations, a single distribution network node (e.g., a regional distribution center in Frankfurt) serves multiple payer accounts (commercial insurers, PBMs, specialty pharmacies) with potentially different service level agreements, delivery lead times, and cold-chain requirements for each payer. Conversely, a single payer account (e.g., a national PBM like Express Scripts) receives pharmaceutical products from multiple distribution nodes across different geographic regions to ensure supply redundancy, optimize delivery speed, and source products with different temperature requirements. The business actively manages these distribution service agreements as operational contracts with specific service levels, carriers, and capabilities per node-payer pair.'
}

Table supply.contract_fulfillment_allocation {
  contract_fulfillment_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each lot-to-contract allocation record.']
  inventory_lot_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the specific inventory lot (batch) being allocated to fulfill the payer contract. References the lot with its lot number, NDC, expiry date, and quality status.']
  market_payer_contract_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the payer contract (rebate agreement, formulary contract, or performance-based contract) that this inventory lot allocation is fulfilling.']
  actual_ship_date date [note: 'The actual date on which this allocated lot quantity was shipped. Populated upon shipment execution. Used for rebate accrual timing and contract performance measurement.']
  allocated_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'The quantity from this lot that has been operationally allocated (reserved) for this payer contract in the inventory management system. May differ from contracted_quantity based on actual lot availability and allocation decisions.']
  allocation_date date [note: 'The date on which this inventory lot was allocated to this payer contract in the supply chain planning or inventory management system. Establishes the temporal relationship for allocation tracking.']
  allocation_reason varchar [note: 'Business reason or driver for this specific lot-to-contract allocation. Examples: \'Formulary commitment fulfillment\', \'Shortage mitigation - split allocation\', \'Expiry date optimization\', \'GPO volume commitment\', \'Performance rebate tier achievement\'.']
  allocation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this lot-to-contract allocation. Tracks progression from planning through fulfillment. Values: PLANNED (forecasted allocation), ALLOCATED (inventory reserved), PARTIALLY_SHIPPED (some quantity shipped), FULLY_SHIPPED (allocation complete), CANCELLED (allocation voided).']
  contract_period varchar [note: 'The specific contract performance period (e.g., \'Q1 2024\', \'2024-03\', \'2024\') during which this lot allocation applies. Critical for aligning lot-level shipments with contract rebate periods and performance metric calculations.']
  contracted_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'The quantity from this specific lot that has been contractually committed to this payer contract. Represents the planned allocation amount based on contract terms and demand forecasts.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this allocation record was created in the system. Part of standard audit trail.']
  expected_ship_date date [note: 'The planned or forecasted date by which this allocated lot quantity is expected to ship to fulfill the payer contract. Used for supply chain planning and contract performance monitoring.']
  fulfillment_priority varchar [note: 'The business priority assigned to this lot-contract allocation, determining fulfillment sequencing during inventory shortages or competing contract demands. Values: CRITICAL (formulary-critical contracts, shortage risk), HIGH (tier 1 payer contracts), MEDIUM (standard contracts), LOW (opportunistic allocations).']
  last_modified_by varchar [note: 'User ID or system identifier that last modified this allocation record. Supports audit trail for allocation changes.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this allocation record. Part of standard audit trail.']
  shipped_quantity decimal(18,4) [note: 'The actual quantity from this lot that has been physically shipped to fulfill this payer contract. Used for rebate accrual calculations and gross-to-net revenue reconciliation tied to actual lot-level shipments.']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for all quantity fields in this allocation record (e.g., EA for eaches/units, CS for cases, KG for bulk). Must align with the inventory_lot.unit_of_measure for consistency.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User ID or system identifier that created this allocation record. Supports audit trail and allocation decision accountability.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the operational allocation and fulfillment tracking between inventory lots and payer contracts in pharmaceutical supply chain operations. It captures the business process of allocating specific inventory lots (with their lot numbers, expiry dates, and quality status) to fulfill contracted obligations with payers, PBMs, and GPOs. Each record links one inventory lot to one payer contract with allocation quantities, fulfillment priorities, and contract period tracking that exist only in the context of this lot-to-contract allocation relationship. Critical for gross-to-net revenue management, rebate accrual calculations tied to actual shipped inventory, and GDP-compliant lot traceability to contracted entities.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical supply chain operations, a single inventory lot (batch) can be allocated across multiple payer contracts during shortage scenarios, multi-contract fulfillment strategies, or when optimizing expiry date management across contracted entities. Conversely, a single payer contract is fulfilled by multiple inventory lots over time due to replenishment cycles, batch production schedules, and the need to maintain continuous supply. The business actively manages these lot-to-contract allocations with specific quantities, fulfillment priorities, and contract period tracking.'
}

  Note: 'Individual Case Safety Report — the primary transactional record in pharmacovigilance.   case_narrative varchar [note: 'Free-text medical narrative describing the clinical course of this adverse reaction, including relevant medical history, concomitant medications, treatment, and outcome. Required for regulatory ICSR submissions and medical review. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field H.1.']
  causality_assessment varchar [note: 'Assessment of the causal relationship between the suspect drug and the adverse reaction, using WHO-UMC or company standard causality categories. Drives listedness determination, SUSAR classification, and signal detection weighting.']
  causality_method varchar [note: 'The methodology or algorithm used to perform the causality assessment (e.g., WHO-UMC scale, Naranjo algorithm, company-specific algorithm). Supports audit trail and methodological consistency across cases.']
  coded_by varchar [note: 'User identifier of the medical coder or system process that performed or confirmed the MedDRA coding. Required for audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance. Stores the user login or system account name.']
  coding_date date [note: 'Date on which the MedDRA coding was completed for this adverse reaction. Used for coding turnaround time metrics, audit trail, and compliance with regulatory submission timelines.']
  coding_method varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the MedDRA coding was performed automatically by the safety system (auto-coded), manually by a medical coder (manual review), or auto-coded and subsequently confirmed by manual review. Supports coding quality metrics and audit trail requirements.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this adverse reaction record was first created in the pharmacovigilance safety database. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI. Supports case processing timeline metrics.']
  ctcae_grade varchar [note: 'Severity grade assigned per the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), ranging from 1 (mild) to 5 (death). Applicable primarily for oncology clinical trial adverse events. Null for non-oncology or post-market cases where CTCAE grading is not applicable.']
  dechallenge_result varchar [note: 'Outcome of dechallenge (withdrawal of the suspect drug) on the adverse reaction. Positive dechallenge (reaction improved or resolved after withdrawal) supports causality. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.18.']
  is_serious boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this adverse reaction meets the regulatory definition of a Serious Adverse Event (SAE) per ICH E2A criteria. True if any seriousness criterion is met. Drives expedited reporting timelines (7-day or 15-day) to health authorities.']
  is_susar boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this adverse reaction has been classified as a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR). True when the reaction is serious, unexpected (unlisted), and there is a reasonable causal relationship to the investigational medicinal product. Triggers mandatory expedited reporting to health authorities and ethics committees.']
  last_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this adverse reaction record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11. Used to track follow-up updates and case amendments in the safety database.']
  listedness_determination varchar [note: 'Determination of whether this adverse reaction is listed (expected) or unlisted (unexpected) in the current Reference Safety Information (RSI), such as the Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS) or Investigator Brochure (IB). Unlisted serious reactions in clinical trials constitute Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) requiring expedited reporting.']
  meddra_hlgt_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA High Level Group Term (HLGT) code, one level above HLT in the MedDRA hierarchy. Supports broader therapeutic area grouping for signal detection and regulatory submissions.']
  meddra_hlt_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA High Level Term (HLT) code representing the grouping level above the Preferred Term. Used for aggregate signal detection and periodic safety update report (PSUR) tabulations.']
  meddra_pt_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) numeric code assigned to this adverse reaction after coding. The PT is the primary level used for regulatory reporting, signal detection, and line listing generation. Mandatory for ICSR submissions to FDA and EMA.']
  meddra_pt_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) label corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Stored denormalized for reporting and line listing generation without requiring a join to the MedDRA reference table.']
  meddra_soc_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code representing the highest level of the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for regulatory line listings, PSUR summary tabulations, and risk management plan (RMP) categorization.']
  meddra_version varchar [note: 'Version of the MedDRA dictionary used to code this adverse reaction (e.g., 26.0, 26.1). Critical for regulatory submissions and recoding exercises when MedDRA versions are updated. Required for reproducibility of signal detection analyses.']
  medical_confirmation boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the adverse reaction has been medically confirmed by a healthcare professional (HCP). Medically confirmed cases carry greater weight in signal detection and regulatory reporting. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field A.1.7.']
  onset_date date [note: 'Date on which the adverse reaction first began. Used to calculate time-to-onset from drug exposure, supports causality assessment, and is required for ICSR regulatory submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.4.']
  outcome_code varchar [note: 'Standardized outcome of the adverse reaction at the time of reporting. Values align with ICH E2B(R3) outcome codes: recovered/resolved, recovering/resolving, not recovered/not resolved, fatal, unknown, recovered with sequelae. Mandatory for regulatory submissions.']
  reaction_duration_days varchar [note: 'Duration of the adverse reaction in days, calculated from onset to resolution. Stored as a business attribute when explicitly reported by the reporter or calculated during case processing. Supports time-to-resolution analytics and benefit-risk assessments.']
  reaction_sequence_number varchar [note: 'Sequential line number of this adverse reaction within the parent ICSR, enabling ordering and identification of multiple events within a single case. Corresponds to the reaction/event sequence in ICH E2B(R3) message structure.']
  reaction_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow processing status of this adverse reaction record within the pharmacovigilance case management system: new (received, not yet processed), under review, coded (MedDRA coding complete), medically reviewed, closed (finalized), or deleted (voided). Drives case management workflow in Argus Safety.']
  rechallenge_result varchar [note: 'Outcome of rechallenge (re-administration of the suspect drug after withdrawal) if performed. Positive rechallenge (reaction recurred) strengthens causality. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.4.k.19.']
  regulatory_report_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the regulatory reporting obligation triggered by this adverse reaction: 7-day expedited (unexpected fatal/life-threatening SUSAR), 15-day expedited (other serious unexpected), periodic (PSUR/PBRER), non-expedited, or not reportable. Drives submission workflow and deadline tracking.']
  reporting_source_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the original source from which this adverse reaction was reported: spontaneous (unsolicited), clinical trial, published literature, regulatory authority, or other. Determines applicable reporting timelines and regulatory obligations. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field A.1.4.']
  resolution_date date [note: 'Date on which the adverse reaction resolved or ended. Null if the event is ongoing, fatal, or outcome is unknown. Used to calculate event duration and supports outcome determination. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.6.']
  seriousness_criteria varchar [note: 'Pipe-delimited list of applicable seriousness criteria met by this adverse reaction per ICH E2A: death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability/incapacity, congenital anomaly, medically significant. Supports regulatory reporting classification and expedited reporting decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: death|life_threatening|hospitalization|prolonged_hospitalization|disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]']
  severity_description varchar [note: 'Narrative severity classification of the adverse reaction using standard WHO/ICH terminology: mild, moderate, severe, life-threatening, or fatal. Complements CTCAE grade for non-oncology cases and post-market surveillance where CTCAE grading is not used.']
  signal_detection_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this adverse reaction record has been flagged as contributing to a potential pharmacovigilance signal under review. Set by the signal detection process in the safety database. Supports signal management workflow and regulatory signal reporting obligations.']
  time_to_onset_days varchar [note: 'Number of days from the first dose of the suspect drug to the onset of the adverse reaction. A key pharmacovigilance metric used in signal detection, causality assessment, and benefit-risk evaluation. Derived from drug start date and reaction onset date during case processing.']
  verbatim_term varchar [note: 'The exact adverse event term as reported by the original reporter (patient, healthcare professional, or literature source) before MedDRA coding. Preserved verbatim for coding audit trail and signal detection. Required per ICH E2B(R3) field B.2.i.1.']

  Note: 'Granular adverse event record linked to an ICSR. Captures the specific event term (MedDRA coded at PT, HLT, HLGT, SOC levels with version tracking), verbatim reporter term, onset date, resolution date, outcome (recovered, not recovered, fatal, unknown), seriousness criteria, severity grade (CTCAE where applicable), and listedness determination against reference safety information. Includes coding metadata: auto-coded vs manual review, coding date. One ICSR may contain multiple adverse events. Supports signal detection aggregation by MedDRA term and regulatory line listing generation.'
}

  narrative_text varchar [note: 'The free-text clinical narrative describing the SUSAR, including the sequence of events, medical history, treatment, and outcome. Required for all regulatory submissions per ICH E2B(R3). Classified as confidential due to sensitive clinical content.']
  pmda_submission_date date [note: 'The date on which the SUSAR was submitted to the Japan Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA). Null if not applicable.']
  reaction_meddra_pt_code varchar [note: 'The MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) Preferred Term code representing the primary adverse reaction. Mandatory for regulatory submissions to FDA, EMA, MHRA, and PMDA.']
  reaction_meddra_pt_name varchar [note: 'The human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term name corresponding to the reaction_meddra_pt_code. Stored for reporting clarity and to avoid repeated lookups against the MedDRA dictionary.']
  reaction_meddra_soc_name varchar [note: 'The MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) under which the primary adverse reaction is classified. Used for signal detection, aggregate analysis, and PSUR/PBRER reporting by therapeutic area.']
  reaction_onset_date date [note: 'The date on which the suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction first manifested in the subject. Used for temporal causality assessment and time-to-onset analysis.']
  reaction_outcome varchar [note: 'The outcome of the adverse reaction at the time of reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: recovered|recovering|not_recovered|recovered_with_sequelae|fatal|unknown — promote to reference product]']
  report_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the SUSAR record within the pharmacovigilance workflow. Drives workflow routing in Argus Safety and regulatory submission tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|under_review|submitted|follow_up_pending|closed|invalidated — promote to reference product]']
  reporting_clock_type varchar [note: 'Indicates whether this SUSAR is subject to a 7-day expedited reporting clock (fatal or life-threatening) or a 15-day reporting clock (all other serious unexpected reactions). Drives SLA enforcement and regulatory deadline calculation.']
  reporting_deadline_date date [note: 'The calculated calendar date by which the SUSAR must be submitted to all applicable health authorities, derived from initial_receipt_date plus the applicable reporting clock (7 or 15 calendar days). SLA-critical field with criminal liability for non-compliance.']
  seriousness_criteria varchar [note: 'The ICH E2A seriousness criterion or criteria met by this adverse reaction, which qualifies it as serious. Multiple criteria may apply. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fatal|life_threatening|hospitalization_required|prolonged_hospitalization|persistent_disability|congenital_anomaly|medically_significant — promote to reference product]']
  sponsor_causality varchar [note: 'The sponsor\'s assessment of the causal relationship between the investigational product and the adverse reaction. A causality of \'related\' or \'not assessable\' (where benefit of doubt applies) is required for SUSAR classification.']
  subject_age varchar [note: 'The age of the clinical trial subject in years at the time the adverse reaction occurred. Required for regulatory submissions and demographic analysis. Classified as restricted PHI.']

  unblinding_date date [note: 'The date on which the treatment assignment was unblinded for this SUSAR case, if applicable. Null for open-label trials or cases where unblinding was not performed. Critical for audit trail and trial integrity documentation.']
  worldwide_unique_case_number varchar [note: 'The globally unique case identifier assigned per ICH E2B(R3) standards, formatted as country code + organisation identifier + local case number. Used for regulatory submissions and cross-authority deduplication.']

  Note: 'Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction record for clinical trial expedited reporting. Captures SUSARs identified from clinical trial ICSRs meeting expedited criteria: unexpected (not in IB/RSI), serious, and at least possibly causally related. Stores parent ICSR reference, trial phase, investigational product, expectedness determination against current IB, causality assessment by sponsor and investigator, 7-day (fatal/life-threatening) or 15-day reporting clock, and submission status to authorities (FDA IND safety report, EMA SUSAR, MHRA, PMDA). SLA-critical: 7-day and 15-day expedited reporting deadlines with criminal liability for non-compliance.'

  regulatory_inspection_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection.   rmp_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.rmp. Business justification: Some PV submissions are for RMP reports. Add rmp_id FK (nullable - only populated for RMP submission types). Remove rmp_version as it normalizes to rmp.version_number.']
  sae_report_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.sae_report. Business justification: SAE reports generate regulatory submissions. Add sae_report_id FK (nullable - only populated for SAE submission types). This links the submission transaction to the SAE master record.']

Distinct from the submission_number assigned by the health authority.']
  safety_signal_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the pharmacovigilance safety signal record that prompted or is associated with this submission, where applicable. Links to the signal detection and management record. Null for routine ICSR submissions not linked to a formal signal.']
  submission_country_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Submission target country determines format (E2B R2/R3, CIOMS), gateway (EudraVigilance, FDA ESG, MHRA Yellow Card), and timelines.   susar_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to pharmacovigilance.susar. Business justification: SUSAR records generate regulatory submissions (expedited reporting). Add susar_id FK (nullable - only populated for SUSAR submission types). One SUSAR can have multiple submissions (initial + follow-u']
  acknowledgement_code varchar [note: 'Technical acknowledgement code returned by the health authority gateway per HL7 v2 / E2B messaging standards. AA = Application Accept; AE = Application Error; CA = Commit Accept; CE = Commit Error; TA = Technical Accept; TE = Technical Error. Drives automated error handling and resubmission workflows.']
  acknowledgement_date timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the technical acknowledgement (ACK) message was received from the health authority gateway confirming successful receipt of the submission. Distinct from substantive acceptance. Used for SLA compliance evidence.']
  argus_case_number varchar [note: 'The case number from the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system that is the source of record for this submission. Enables direct traceability from the submission record back to the full safety case in the operational PV system.']
  authority_case_number varchar [note: 'The case or report reference number assigned by the receiving health authority upon acceptance of the submission (e.g., EudraVigilance case number, FDA FAERS case ID). Used for follow-up queries and regulatory correspondence. Populated after authority acceptance.']

  date_of_first_receipt date [note: 'The date the company first received the minimum valid safety information constituting a reportable case (Day 0 for regulatory clock purposes). This is the anchor date from which the 7-day or 15-day expedited reporting deadline is calculated for ICSRs. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.4.']
  days_to_deadline varchar [note: 'Number of calendar days remaining between the current date and the regulatory_deadline at the time of last record update. Negative values indicate overdue submissions. Used for SLA monitoring dashboards and automatic escalation triggers. Note: this is a snapshot value captured at record update time, not a live calculation.']
  error_code varchar [note: 'Structured error code returned by the health authority gateway or E2B validation engine upon rejection or technical failure (e.g., EudraVigilance business rule error code, FAERS conformance error code). Enables automated error categorisation and routing to the appropriate remediation team.']
  gateway_portal varchar [note: 'The specific electronic gateway or web portal used to transmit this submission to the health authority. Determines technical format and protocol requirements. EudraVigilance Gateway and EVWEB are EMA channels; FAERS Gateway is the FDA channel for ICSRs; MHRA Sentinel is the UK post-Brexit channel. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EUDRAVIGILANCE_GATEWAY|EUDRAVIGILANCE_EVWEB|FAERS_GATEWAY|MHRA_SENTINEL|PMDA_GATEWAY|NMPA_GATEWAY|VIGIBASE_WHO|DIRECT_EMAIL|PAPER — promote to reference product]']
  health_authority_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the target regulatory health authority to which this submission is directed. FDA = U.S. Food and Drug Administration; EMA = European Medicines Agency; MHRA = Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK); PMDA = Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (Japan); NMPA = National Medical Products Administration (China). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|ANVISA|TGA|HEALTH_CANADA|SWISSMEDIC|COFEPRIS|KFDA|MEDSAFE — promote to reference product]']
  is_expedited boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this submission is subject to expedited regulatory reporting requirements (7-day or 15-day clock). True = expedited; False = periodic/non-expedited. Drives SLA escalation logic and compliance monitoring.']
  is_on_time boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the submission was transmitted on or before the regulatory_deadline. True = submitted on time; False = submitted late. Key compliance KPI field populated at time of submission. Used for regulatory compliance reporting and CAPA tracking.']
  is_susar boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this submission relates to a Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) from a clinical trial, which carries specific expedited reporting obligations to both health authorities and investigators under ICH E2A and GCP regulations.']
  message_format varchar [note: 'The technical format standard used for the submission message. E2B_R2_XML = ICH E2B(R2) XML format (used by some national authorities); E2B_R3_XML = ICH E2B(R3) XML format (required by EMA EudraVigilance and FDA from 2022); ECTD = Electronic Common Technical Document format (for aggregate reports); PDF = portable document format for ad-hoc communications; PAPER = legacy paper submission.']
  regulatory_deadline date [note: 'The mandatory regulatory deadline date by which this submission must be transmitted to the health authority, calculated from the date of first receipt (Day 0) of the safety information.   report_type_qualifier varchar [note: 'Qualifier indicating whether this is an initial report, a follow-up update to a previously submitted case, or a nullification (withdrawal) of a previously submitted report. Corresponds directly to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2 field.']

  resubmission_count varchar [note: 'Number of times this submission has been resubmitted to the health authority following a rejection or technical error.   sender_organisation varchar [note: 'Name of the pharmaceutical company or Marketing Authorisation Holder (MAH) submitting the report, as declared in the E2B message header (ICH E2B(R3) C.1.3.1). Required field in all E2B transmissions.']
  submission_date timestamp [note: 'The principal real-world timestamp when the pharmacovigilance report was transmitted to the health authority gateway or portal. This is the legally significant submission event time used for regulatory deadline compliance calculations.']
  submission_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this submission, either generated internally or assigned by the receiving health authority gateway (e.g., EudraVigilance transmission ID, FAERS acknowledgement number). Used for tracking and cross-referencing with authority systems.']
  submission_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the pharmacovigilance submission workflow. DRAFT = in preparation; PENDING = queued for transmission; SUBMITTED = transmitted to health authority gateway; ACKNOWLEDGED = technical acknowledgement received from gateway; ACCEPTED = substantively accepted by authority; REJECTED = rejected with errors requiring correction; RESUBMITTED = corrected and resubmitted after rejection; WITHDRAWN = voluntarily withdrawn by the company. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DRAFT|PENDING|SUBMITTED|ACKNOWLEDGED|ACCEPTED|REJECTED|RESUBMITTED|WITHDRAWN — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  submission_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the pharmacovigilance submission by regulatory report type. ICSR_EXPEDITED_7DAY = fatal/life-threatening Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) requiring 7-calendar-day reporting; ICSR_EXPEDITED_15DAY = serious ICSR requiring 15-calendar-day reporting; ICSR_NON_EXPEDITED = non-expedited periodic ICSR; PSUR = Periodic Safety Update Report; PBRER = Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report; PADER = Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report; DSUR = Development Safety Update Report. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ICSR_EXPEDITED_7DAY|ICSR_EXPEDITED_15DAY|ICSR_NON_EXPEDITED|PSUR|PBRER|PADER|DSUR|AD_HOC_SAFETY_COMM|REMS_ASSESSMENT|SUSAR — promote to reference product]']
  submission_version varchar [note: 'Sequential version number of this submission for a given safety case or aggregate report. Version 1 = initial submission; Version 2+ = follow-up or amendment submissions. Corresponds to ICH E2B(R3) C.1.2 (report type: initial/follow-up/nullification).']
  transmission_reference varchar [note: 'Unique message transmission identifier assigned by the health authority gateway at the point of receipt (e.g., EudraVigilance message ID, FAERS transmission reference). Distinct from the authority_case_number; this is the technical envelope identifier used for gateway-level tracing and acknowledgement matching.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this pharmacovigilance submission record was most recently modified in the data platform. Audit trail field for data lineage and 21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11 electronic records compliance.']

  Note: 'Regulatory submission record for all pharmacovigilance reports submitted to health authorities worldwide. Covers expedited individual case reports (7-day fatal/life-threatening, 15-day serious), periodic aggregate reports (PSUR, PBRER, PADER, DSUR), and ad-hoc safety communications. Stores submission type, target authority, submission date, acknowledgement status, error handling, submission format (E2B R2/R3 XML, eCTD), gateway/portal details, submission reference number, resubmission history, and compliance status. Supports all major regulatory gateways including EudraVigilance (EVWEB/gateway), FAERS (FDA), MHRA Sentinel, PMDA gateway, and NMPA. Tracks authority-specific technical requirements (E2B R3 for EMA, E2B R2 for some national authorities). SLA-critical: regulatory deadline compliance with automatic escalation.'
}

Table pharmacovigilance.psur {

Business justification: PSURs inform brand planning as safety profile outcomes impact positioning, target population, and promotional strategy. Brand teams review PSUR benefit-risk conclusions quarterly to adjust market acce']

  mah_legal_entity_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to masterdata.legal_entity. Business justification: PSUR is submitted by specific MAH legal entity. Determines signatory authority, regulatory obligations, and submission routing. Critical for regulatory compliance and multi-entity portfolio management']
  medical_publication_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to medical.medical_publication. Business justification: PSURs cite key medical publications as evidence sources for benefit-risk assessment and safety specification updates. Critical for regulatory submission and scientific justification of safety profile.']
  patent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: PSURs reference patent status for benefit-risk assessment context, especially when evaluating whether formulation changes covered by new patents affect safety profile. Patent expiry impacts market dyn']

  psur_medical_reviewer_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the qualified physician or clinical pharmacologist responsible for the medical review and benefit-risk evaluation section of this PSUR. Required for regulatory compliance.']
  psur_qppv_employee_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the EU Qualified Person for Pharmacovigilance (QPPV) who is responsible for oversight and approval of this PSUR prior to submission to EMA. Mandatory for EU-authorised products.']
  pv_product_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the medicinal product (drug substance or drug product) that is the subject of this periodic safety report.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the QPPV (or designated signatory) formally approved the PSUR for regulatory submission. Represents the final internal milestone before submission and is an auditable event per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  benefit_risk_conclusion varchar [note: 'Overall benefit-risk evaluation conclusion for the product as determined by the medical reviewer for this PSUR period. A finding of unfavourable or inconclusive may trigger regulatory action, label update, or risk management plan revision.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this PSUR record was first created in the pharmacovigilance data lakehouse, providing the audit trail creation event per 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR data governance requirements.']
  cumulative_case_count varchar [note: 'Total number of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) received from the IBD through the data lock point across all reporting intervals, providing the full post-marketing safety case history for the product.']

  cumulative_exposure_patients varchar [note: 'Estimated cumulative number of patients exposed to the product from the IBD through the data lock point, derived from post-marketing surveillance, clinical trials, and sales data. Used as denominator for cumulative incidence rate calculations.']
  data_lock_point date [note: 'The cut-off date up to which all safety data (adverse events, literature, clinical studies) are included in this PSUR. No new data arising after this date is incorporated into the current report period.']
  draft_completion_date date [note: 'Date on which the initial draft of the PSUR was completed by the lead author and made available for internal review. Used to track preparation milestones against the submission deadline.']
  ha_assessment_outcome varchar [note: 'Outcome of the health authority\'s assessment of this PSUR, indicating any regulatory action required. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pending|no_action|label_update|rmp_update|referral|suspension|withdrawal — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]']
  international_birth_date date [note: 'The date of first marketing authorisation for the product in any country worldwide, used as the anchor date for calculating PSUR submission deadlines and reporting intervals per ICH E2C(R2). SLA-critical field.']
  interval_case_count varchar [note: 'Total number of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) received during the current reporting interval (between interval_start_date and data_lock_point), including both spontaneous and solicited reports.']
  interval_end_date date [note: 'End date of the current PSUR reporting interval, which is typically equal to the data lock point. Defines the close of the reporting window for interval case counts and exposure data.']
  interval_sae_count varchar [note: 'Number of Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) reported during the current reporting interval. SAEs include fatal, life-threatening, hospitalisation-requiring, or permanently disabling events per ICH E2A criteria.']
  interval_start_date date [note: 'Start date of the current PSUR reporting interval (the period covered by this report). Together with interval_end_date defines the reporting window for interval case counts and exposure data.']
  interval_susar_count varchar [note: 'Number of Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) identified during the current reporting interval. SUSARs require expedited reporting and are tracked separately for signal detection purposes.']
  label_update_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the safety findings in this PSUR require an update to the product label (SmPC, Package Insert, or Patient Information Leaflet). A True value initiates a label change management workflow.']
  medical_review_date date [note: 'Date on which the medical reviewer completed the clinical and benefit-risk review of the PSUR draft. Milestone in the PSUR preparation workflow tracked against the submission deadline.']
  new_safety_signals_count varchar [note: 'Number of new safety signals identified during the reporting interval through signal detection activities (disproportionality analysis, literature review, spontaneous reports). Drives benefit-risk re-evaluation.']
  psusa_procedure_number varchar [note: 'EMA-assigned procedure number for the PSUR Single Assessment (PSUSA) process applicable to centrally authorised products in the EU. Used to track the PSUSA workflow and outcome in Veeva Vault RIM and RIMS.']
  qc_completion_date date [note: 'Date on which quality control review of the PSUR was completed, verifying accuracy of case counts, exposure data, and regulatory formatting prior to QPPV approval and submission.']
  report_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to this PSUR/PBRER/PADER/DSUR submission, used in regulatory correspondence and tracking systems such as Argus Safety and Veeva Vault RIM.']
  report_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle workflow state of the PSUR record, tracking progression from initial drafting through medical review, QC, approval, and regulatory submission. Drives SLA monitoring and escalation workflows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|in_review|qc_review|approved|submitted|accepted|withdrawn — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  report_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the periodic aggregate safety report: PSUR (Periodic Safety Update Report), PBRER (Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report per ICH E2C R2), PADER (Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report per FDA), DSUR (Development Safety Update Report for investigational products), or PSUSA (PSUR Single Assessment for EU centralised procedure).']
  reporting_frequency varchar [note: 'Regulatory-mandated submission frequency for this PSUR, which varies by product age, risk profile, and authority requirements. Drives automated SLA deadline calculation from the IBD.']
  reporting_period_number varchar [note: 'Sequential ordinal number of this PSUR reporting period for the product (e.g., 1st, 2nd, 3rd PSUR), enabling chronological tracking of the full PSUR history for a product.']
  rmp_update_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the benefit-risk findings in this PSUR necessitate an update to the product\'s Risk Management Plan (RMP). A True value triggers a formal RMP revision workflow in the pharmacovigilance system.']
  source_system_record_code varchar [note: 'Native record identifier from the originating pharmacovigilance system (Argus Safety, Oracle AERS, or Veeva Vault RIM) for this PSUR record, enabling traceability and reconciliation between the lakehouse silver layer and the operational system of record.']
  submission_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the PSUR was submitted to the health authority. Compared against submission_deadline to determine on-time or late submission for regulatory compliance tracking.']
  submission_deadline date [note: 'Mandatory regulatory deadline by which this PSUR must be submitted to the applicable health authority, calculated from the IBD and reporting frequency. SLA-critical field monitored for compliance.']
  submission_format varchar [note: 'Electronic or paper format used for regulatory submission of this PSUR. eCTD (Electronic Common Technical Document) is the standard for FDA and EMA submissions; NeeS is a non-eCTD electronic submission format.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this PSUR record in the data lakehouse, supporting audit trail requirements and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR.']

  Note: 'Periodic aggregate safety report master record covering PSUR, PBRER (ICH E2C R2), PADER (FDA), and DSUR (development phase) for each product-indication combination. Captures data lock point, reporting interval, international birth date (IBD), cumulative exposure data, interval and cumulative case summaries, signal summary, benefit-risk evaluation conclusion, and submission status per applicable authority. Tracks preparation milestones, author assignments, medical review, QC, and approval workflow. Supports EU PSUR single assessment (PSUSA) process, FDA PADER requirements, and ICH DSUR for investigational products. Includes structured benefit-risk assessment sections. SLA-critical: fixed regulatory submission deadlines based on IBD.'
}

  safety_specification_summary varchar [note: 'Narrative summary of the safety specification section of the RMP, covering the epidemiology of the indication, non-clinical safety findings, clinical trial safety data, and post-marketing experience.']

  scope_population varchar [note: 'Description of the target patient population covered by this RMP, including age groups, special populations (pediatric, geriatric, renal/hepatic impairment), and any population restrictions.']

  superseded_date date [note: 'Date on which this RMP version was superseded by a newer version. Null for the currently active version.']
  title varchar [note: 'Full descriptive title of the Risk Management Plan document, typically including the product name, indication, and version.']
  veeva_vault_doc_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) where the RMP document is stored and managed as part of the regulatory dossier.']

  version_number varchar [note: 'Version identifier of the RMP document (e.g., 1.0, 2.3), incremented with each regulatory submission or significant update. Supports version history tracking.']

  Note: 'Risk Management Plan master record. Captures RMP version, scope (product, indication, population), safety specification (important identified risks, important potential risks, missing information), pharmacovigilance plan activities (routine and additional), risk minimization measures (routine and additional including REMS for US), effectiveness evaluation plan, and PASS commitments. Links to resulting PV actions and PASS study commitments.'
