  detection_method varchar [note: 'Methodology used to identify the safety signal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: disproportionality_analysis|clinical_review|machine_learning|literature_review|spontaneous_report|regulatory_authority — promote to reference product]']
  detection_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Date and time when the safety signal was first detected or identified, representing the principal real-world event time. Critical for SLA tracking of PRAC rapporteur notification timelines and regulatory reporting deadlines.']
  ebgm_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Empirical Bayes Geometric Mean (EBGM) — a Bayesian disproportionality metric used in the FDA FAERS database analysis. EBGM ≥2 is a commonly applied threshold for signal detection.']
  fatal_case_count varchar [note: 'Number of fatal outcome cases among the cases contributing to this safety signal. Fatal cases receive highest priority in signal triage and may trigger expedited regulatory notification.']
  ic_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Information Component (IC) — a Bayesian disproportionality metric used by the WHO Uppsala Monitoring Centre (UMC) VigiBase. Positive IC values indicate a drug-event association stronger than expected by chance.']
  label_change_recommended boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the signal assessment has resulted in a formal recommendation to update the product label (SmPC, USPI, or equivalent). Triggers regulatory submission activities.']
  meddra_pt_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) code representing the primary adverse event or medical concept associated with this safety signal. Standardized coding per MedDRA hierarchy for regulatory submissions and signal tracking.']
  meddra_pt_name varchar [note: 'Human-readable MedDRA Preferred Term name corresponding to the meddra_pt_code. Provides the standardized medical terminology label for the safety signal event.']
  meddra_soc_code varchar [note: 'MedDRA System Organ Class (SOC) code for the primary adverse event, providing the highest-level classification in the MedDRA hierarchy. Used for signal clustering and therapeutic area analysis.']
  prac_notification_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the PRAC rapporteur was notified of the safety signal. Compared against prac_notification_due_date to assess SLA compliance.']
  prac_notification_due_date date [note: 'SLA-critical deadline by which the PRAC rapporteur must be notified of the validated safety signal per EMA regulatory requirements. Drives escalation workflows and compliance monitoring.']
  priority_level varchar [note: 'Triage priority assigned to the safety signal based on clinical seriousness, signal strength, and public health impact. Drives SLA timelines for assessment completion and regulatory notification.']
  prr_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR) — a disproportionality analysis metric quantifying the ratio of the proportion of reports for a drug-event combination versus all other drugs. Values >2 with chi-squared >4 and ≥3 cases typically indicate a signal.']
  psur_referral_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this safety signal has been referred for inclusion and evaluation in the next Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER).']
  regulatory_action_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the safety signal assessment has determined that a regulatory action is required (e.g., label update, DHPC, REMS modification, product withdrawal). Drives downstream regulatory affairs workflows.']
  regulatory_action_type varchar [note: 'Type of regulatory action determined to be required based on the signal assessment outcome. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: label_update|rems_modification|dhpc|psur_referral|product_withdrawal|contraindication_addition|none — promote to reference product]']
  rmp_update_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the signal assessment outcome requires an update to the product\'s Risk Management Plan (RMP). Triggers regulatory affairs and pharmacovigilance team coordination.']
  ror_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) — a disproportionality analysis metric representing the odds of a specific adverse event being reported for a drug versus all other drugs. Complements PRR in signal detection.']
  serious_case_count varchar [note: 'Number of Serious Adverse Event (SAE) cases among the total cases contributing to this signal. Serious cases include fatal, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability, or congenital anomaly outcomes per ICH E2A.']
  signal_description varchar [note: 'Detailed narrative description of the safety signal including the nature of the concern, clinical context, patient population affected, and initial evidence summary. Supports signal triage and assessment documentation.']
  signal_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier assigned to the safety signal upon creation in Argus Safety / Oracle AERS. Used for cross-system referencing, regulatory correspondence, and PRAC rapporteur notifications.']
  signal_source_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the data source from which the safety signal was detected. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spontaneous_database|literature|clinical_trial|real_world_data|social_media|health_authority — promote to reference product]']
  signal_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the safety signal per GVP Module IX workflow: new (detected, not yet triaged), under_evaluation (active assessment in progress), validated (confirmed as a genuine safety concern), refuted (assessed and dismissed), closed (final disposition reached and documented).']
  signal_title varchar [note: 'Concise, human-readable title describing the safety signal, typically formatted as [Drug Name] and [Adverse Event Term]. Used in regulatory correspondence, PRAC submissions, and internal safety committee communications.']
  signal_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the signal as new (not previously known), strengthened (existing signal with increased evidence), weakened (existing signal with decreased evidence), or refuted (previously identified signal now dismissed).']
  source_reference_number varchar [note: 'Reference number or identifier from the originating data source (e.g., FAERS case number, EudraVigilance report ID, literature PubMed ID, clinical trial NCT number) that triggered or contributed to the signal detection.']
  triage_date date [note: 'Date on which the safety signal was formally triaged by the pharmacovigilance team to determine priority and assign for full assessment. Marks the transition from detection to active evaluation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the safety signal record. Supports audit trail requirements and tracks signal assessment progression through the lifecycle.']
  validation_date date [note: 'Date on which the safety signal was formally validated as a genuine safety concern following initial assessment. Triggers downstream regulatory notification and benefit-risk evaluation activities.']

  Note: 'Safety signal record representing a new or evolving safety concern identified through signal detection activities. Captures signal source (spontaneous database, literature, clinical trial, real-world data), detection method (disproportionality analysis, clinical review, machine learning), MedDRA-coded term, signal strength metrics (PRR, ROR, EBGM, IC), and signal status lifecycle (new, under evaluation, validated, refuted, closed). Includes formal assessment records: methodology, data sources reviewed, benefit-risk impact evaluation, proposed label change recommendation, regulatory action required, PRAC/PSUR referral status, and final disposition. Each signal supports multiple assessment iterations. Tracks the full signal management workflow from detection through triage, validation, prioritization, assessment, and closure or regulatory action per GVP Module IX. SLA-critical: PRAC rapporteur notification timelines.'
}

  indication varchar [note: 'Medical condition or disease for which the drug was prescribed or taken, coded using MedDRA terminology. Supports indication-stratified signal detection and benefit-risk assessment. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.7.r.2b.']

  is_blinded boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the drug identity is blinded (True) in the context of a clinical trial (e.g., randomized controlled trial where the patient or investigator does not know the assigned treatment). Affects SUSAR reporting and unblinding procedures.']
  is_company_product boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the drug is a product owned or marketed by the reporting company (True) or a competitor/third-party product (False). Determines regulatory reporting obligations and case ownership.']
  parent_drug_code varchar [note: 'WHO Drug Dictionary parent drug code representing the active moiety or parent compound, used to group drug products sharing the same active substance for aggregate signal detection and PSUR analyses.']
  rechallenge_result varchar [note: 'Outcome observed after the drug was reintroduced following dechallenge (rechallenge): whether the adverse event recurred. A positive rechallenge is strong evidence of causality. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.9.i.4.']
  record_created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this suspect or concomitant drug record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI.']
  record_updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this suspect or concomitant drug record was last modified in the pharmacovigilance system. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and GVP Module VI.']
  route_of_administration varchar [note: 'Route by which the drug was administered to the patient (e.g., oral, intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical). Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.10.2. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: oral|intravenous|subcutaneous|intramuscular|topical|inhalation|transdermal|intrathecal — promote to reference product]']
  source_system_drug_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of this drug record in the originating pharmacovigilance source system (e.g., Argus Safety case drug ID or Oracle AERS drug sequence identifier). Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit traceability between the lakehouse silver layer and the system of record.']
  start_date date [note: 'Date on which the patient started taking the drug. Used to calculate drug exposure duration and temporal relationship to adverse event onset. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.4.']
  stop_date date [note: 'Date on which the patient stopped taking the drug. Nullable if the drug was ongoing at the time of the report. Used to calculate exposure duration and assess dechallenge timing. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.4.r.5.']
  time_to_onset_days varchar [note: 'Number of days between the drug start date and the onset of the adverse event. A key temporal metric for causality assessment and signal detection algorithms (e.g., disproportionality analysis).']
  verbatim_drug_name varchar [note: 'Drug name exactly as reported by the reporter (patient, healthcare professional, or other source) before any coding or standardization. Preserved for traceability and audit. Maps to ICH E2B(R3) element G.k.2.2.']
  who_drug_code varchar [note: 'Unique alphanumeric code assigned by the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) to the coded medicinal product. Used for product-level case aggregation, line listing, and signal detection analytics.']
  who_drug_name varchar [note: 'Standardized drug name as coded against the WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD), representing the preferred term for the medicinal product. Enables cross-case aggregation and signal detection.']

  Note: 'Suspect and concomitant drug record within an ICSR. Captures drug name (verbatim and WHO Drug Dictionary coded), drug role (suspect, concomitant, interacting), dose, frequency, route, indication, start/stop dates, action taken (drug withdrawn, dose reduced, dose not changed, unknown), dechallenge result, rechallenge result, and batch/lot number. One ICSR may have multiple suspect and concomitant drugs. Enables product-level case aggregation for signal detection, line listing generation, and exposure-based analyses.'
}

  qualification varchar [note: 'Professional qualification of the reporter, particularly relevant for Healthcare Professional (HCP) reporters. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: physician|pharmacist|nurse|dentist|other_health_professional|consumer|unknown — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]']
  regulatory_authority_code varchar [note: 'Identifier of the regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA) when the reporter is a regulatory body. Used to route mandatory ICSR submissions and track authority-initiated follow-up requests.']
  reliability_score varchar [note: 'Internal PV team assessment of the reporter\'s historical reliability based on completeness and accuracy of prior submissions. Used to weight signal detection analysis and prioritize follow-up resources. Assigned by the PV case processor.']
  reporter_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of the reporter record within the PV system. Inactive or blocked reporters are excluded from new case assignments. Supports duplicate detection and data quality management.']
  reporter_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the reporter by their relationship to the adverse event. Drives regulatory reporting obligations and follow-up workflows. ICH E2B(R3) field A.2.1.1. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: healthcare_professional|patient_consumer|lawyer|regulatory_authority|literature|other — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]']
  source_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the original source through which the adverse event report was received. Determines regulatory handling requirements; e.g., literature-sourced reports require medical literature monitoring per GVP Module VI. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: spontaneous|literature|clinical_trial|regulatory_authority|solicited|other — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]']
  specialty varchar [note: 'Medical or clinical specialty of the HCP reporter (e.g., Oncology, Cardiology, Neurology). Supports signal detection analysis by therapeutic area and enables targeted follow-up by medically qualified personnel.']
  total_reports_submitted varchar [note: 'Cumulative count of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) submitted by this reporter. Used for duplicate detection, reporter profiling, and reliability assessment. Updated upon each new case linkage.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the reporter record. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR Article 30 record-keeping obligations.']

  Note: 'Reporter master data — the individual or organization who submitted an adverse event report. Captures reporter type (healthcare professional, patient/consumer, lawyer, regulatory authority, literature), qualification (physician, pharmacist, nurse, dentist, consumer), country, institution, anonymized reporter identifier (per GDPR/HIPAA), contact preference for follow-up, and reporter reliability assessment. Enables reporter-level case aggregation, duplicate detection, follow-up management, and compliance with ICH E2B reporter data requirements. Distinct from HCP master — this is the PV-specific reporter identity used solely for case processing.'

Table pharmacovigilance.rsi {
  rsi_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the Reference Safety Information record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.']
  previous_version_rsi_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding version of this RSI document for the same product and document type. Enables version chain traversal for historical listedness assessment and change impact analysis.']
  applicable_region varchar [note: 'Geographic region or regulatory jurisdiction for which this RSI document is authoritative (e.g., \'USA\', \'EU\', \'JPN\', \'GLOBAL\'). Determines which RSI version is used for listedness assessment in region-specific expedited reporting. Use ISO 3-letter country codes or \'GLOBAL\' for CCDS.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which this RSI version received internal company approval (e.g., sign-off by the Global Safety Officer or Medical Affairs). Distinct from effective_date; the document may be approved before it becomes effective for listedness assessment.']
  approved_by varchar [note: 'Name or employee identifier of the individual (typically Global Safety Officer, Medical Director, or Regulatory Affairs Lead) who provided final internal approval for this RSI version. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.']
  argus_rsi_code varchar [note: 'Native identifier of this RSI record in the Argus Safety / Oracle AERS pharmacovigilance system. Enables bidirectional traceability between the Databricks Silver Layer and the operational PV system for reconciliation and audit purposes.']
  atc_code varchar [note: 'WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code for the active substance, used to categorize the drug by therapeutic area and mechanism. Supports signal detection and aggregate safety analysis across product classes.']
  change_reason varchar [note: 'Categorized reason for issuing this new RSI version. Supports root cause analysis and regulatory inspection readiness. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: new_safety_signal|regulatory_request|periodic_review|label_update|clinical_data|spontaneous_reports|post_market_study|other — promote to reference product]']
  change_summary varchar [note: 'Narrative summary of the key changes introduced in this RSI version compared to the previous version (e.g., \'Added hepatotoxicity as listed reaction; updated frequency of nausea from common to very common\'). Supports impact assessment for ongoing ICSRs and SUSAR re-evaluation.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this RSI record was first created in the data platform. Supports audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and GDPR Article 5(2) accountability principle.']
  development_phase varchar [note: 'Stage of the product\'s development lifecycle at the time this RSI version was issued. Determines which document type is applicable (IB for clinical phases, SmPC/USPI for marketed). Relevant for SUSAR reporting obligations under IND/CTA.']
  document_language varchar [note: 'ISO 639-1 language code of the RSI document (e.g., \'en\', \'de\', \'fr\', \'ja\'). The English version is typically the master; translations may exist for regional submissions. Listedness assessment is performed against the language-appropriate version.']
  document_title varchar [note: 'Full official title of the reference safety document (e.g., \'Investigator\'s Brochure for Compound XYZ Edition 5\' or \'Summary of Product Characteristics for DrugName 10mg Tablets\'). Human-readable identity label for the document.']
  document_type varchar [note: 'Type of the reference safety document that defines the expected adverse reaction profile. IB = Investigator\'s Brochure (used in clinical trials), SmPC = Summary of Product Characteristics (EU marketed products), USPI = United States Prescribing Information (US marketed products), CCDS = Company Core Data Sheet (global company reference), PIL = Patient Information Leaflet. Drives which document is consulted for listedness assessment.']
  dosage_form varchar [note: 'Pharmaceutical dosage form of the drug product covered by this RSI (e.g., \'tablet\', \'injection\', \'capsule\', \'infusion\'). Relevant when a product has multiple formulations with different safety profiles requiring separate RSI documents.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which this version of the RSI document becomes the authoritative reference for listedness/expectedness assessment. Used in point-in-time queries to determine which RSI version was active at the time of an adverse event report.']
  emea_product_number varchar [note: 'EMA centralized procedure product number (EMEA/H/C/XXXXXX) associated with this RSI when document_type is \'SmPC\'. Links the RSI to the EU marketing authorization for EudraVigilance reporting and PSUR obligations.']
  ind_number varchar [note: 'FDA Investigational New Drug (IND) application number associated with this RSI, applicable when document_type is \'IB\'. Links the RSI to the specific IND under which clinical trials are conducted and SUSAR reporting obligations arise.']
  indication varchar [note: 'Primary approved or investigated clinical indication for which the product is used, as stated in this RSI version (e.g., \'Non-small cell lung cancer\', \'Rheumatoid arthritis\'). Contextualizes the expected safety profile for the intended patient population.']
  inn varchar [note: 'WHO-assigned International Nonproprietary Name (INN) for the active substance covered by this RSI. Provides a globally standardized, non-proprietary identifier for the drug substance, enabling cross-product and cross-company safety comparisons.']
  is_current_version boolean [note: 'Flag indicating whether this record represents the currently active version of the RSI for the given product, document type, and region. True = this is the version used for all new ICSR listedness assessments. Supports efficient querying without date-range filtering.']
  listed_reaction_count varchar [note: 'Total number of distinct adverse reactions enumerated as listed/expected in this RSI version, expressed as MedDRA Preferred Terms. Provides a quick summary metric for version comparison and completeness validation without querying the reaction detail table.']
  meddra_version varchar [note: 'Version of the MedDRA terminology used to encode the listed adverse reactions in this RSI (e.g., \'26.0\', \'26.1\'). Critical for consistent listedness assessment — MedDRA term changes between versions can affect whether a reaction is considered listed.']
  nda_bla_number varchar [note: 'FDA NDA or BLA application number associated with this RSI, applicable when document_type is \'USPI\' for approved marketed products. Links the RSI to the approved marketing authorization for expedited and periodic safety reporting.']
  product_name varchar [note: 'Proprietary or brand name of the medicinal product to which this RSI applies. May be a compound name (INN) for investigational products or a trade name for marketed products. Supports product-level filtering in ICSR listedness assessment.']
  psur_data_lock_point date [note: 'Data lock point date for the Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) cycle in which this RSI version was first used. Supports traceability of RSI changes across PSUR reporting periods.']
  regulatory_authority varchar [note: 'Primary regulatory authority to which this RSI document is submitted or under whose jurisdiction it is maintained. Drives authority-specific reporting obligations and listedness determination rules. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|HEALTH_CANADA|TGA|ANVISA|CDSCO — promote to reference product]']
  rmp_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or version of the Risk Management Plan (RMP) that was current when this RSI version was issued. The RMP\'s safety specification informs the listed reactions in the RSI and must be consistent with it.']
  route_of_administration varchar [note: 'Route by which the drug product is administered (e.g., \'oral\', \'intravenous\', \'subcutaneous\', \'intramuscular\', \'topical\'). Relevant for products with multiple administration routes that may have distinct safety profiles and separate RSI sections.']
  rsi_code varchar [note: 'Business-assigned unique code identifying this RSI document record, typically encoding product abbreviation, year, and sequence number. Used as the externally-known identifier across pharmacovigilance systems including Argus Safety.']
  rsi_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the RSI document version. \'draft\' = under preparation; \'approved\' = internally approved but not yet effective; \'active\' = currently in force for listedness assessment; \'superseded\' = replaced by a newer version; \'retired\' = no longer applicable; \'withdrawn\' = removed from use. Only one version per product/document type should be \'active\' at any time.']
  source_document_reference varchar [note: 'Document management system identifier (e.g., Veeva Vault document ID) for the source RSI document. Enables traceability from the RSI data record back to the controlled document in the eTMF or QualityDocs vault.']
  superseded_date date [note: 'Date on which this RSI version was superseded by a newer version and ceased to be the active reference. Null if this is the current active version. Together with effective_date, defines the validity interval for point-in-time listedness assessment.']
  susar_applicable boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this RSI is used for SUSAR determination in clinical trials. True when document_type is \'IB\' or \'CCDS\' and the product is under active clinical investigation. Drives the 7/15-day expedited reporting clock for unexpected serious reactions.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Primary therapeutic area or disease indication for which the product is developed or approved (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for domain-level safety reporting and signal management.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to this RSI record in the data platform. Together with created_timestamp, provides a complete audit trail for data governance and regulatory inspection readiness.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'Version or edition number of the RSI document (e.g., \'5.0\', \'2.1\', \'12\'). Critical for point-in-time listedness assessment — the version in effect at the time of an adverse event determines whether a reaction is listed or unlisted. Corresponds to the edition field in Argus Safety RSI configuration.']

  Note: 'Reference Safety Information record — the authoritative document defining the expected adverse reaction profile for listedness/expectedness assessment. Captures RSI document type (Investigator\'s Brochure for trials, SmPC for EU, USPI for US, CCDS as company core), version, effective date, product scope, and the enumerated list of expected adverse reactions by MedDRA preferred term. Used in every ICSR to determine whether a reaction is listed (expected) or unlisted (unexpected), directly driving expedited reporting obligations and SUSAR determination. Version-controlled with effective dating to support point-in-time listedness assessment.'
}

  Note: 'This association product represents the Coverage relationship between pv_agreement and pv_product. It captures the specific safety data exchange obligations, reporting timelines, and responsible party designations that apply when a particular product falls under a particular pharmacovigilance agreement. Each record links one pv_agreement to one pv_product with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship - the same agreement may have different exchange timelines or responsible parties for different products, and the same product may be governed by multiple agreements with different counterparties across different territories.. Existence Justification: In pharmacovigilance operations, a single PV agreement routinely covers multiple products (e.g., a CRO agreement covering an entire therapeutic portfolio), and a single product is frequently governed by multiple agreements simultaneously (e.g., different co-promotion agreements in different territories, or a manufacturing agreement plus a licensing agreement). The business actively manages this relationship through agreement negotiation, product scope amendments, and compliance monitoring - tracking which products are covered under which agreements, with what reporting timelines, and which party is responsible for what activities.'
}

Table pharmacovigilance.product_listedness {
  product_listedness_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the product-indication listedness record. Primary key.']
  indication_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the approved or investigational therapeutic indication']
  pv_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the pharmacovigilance product master record under safety surveillance']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the regulatory authority in this jurisdiction granted marketing authorization for this specific product-indication combination. Used to determine listedness status at the time of adverse event occurrence.']
  approval_jurisdiction varchar [note: 'ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or alpha-3 country/region code for the regulatory jurisdiction where this product-indication combination is approved. Critical for jurisdiction-specific listedness determination in ICSR processing.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this product-indication listedness record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system.']
  effective_date date [note: 'Date from which this listedness determination became effective for pharmacovigilance case processing. May differ from approval_date if label changes occurred post-approval.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which this listedness determination expires or was superseded (e.g., due to label update, withdrawal, or indication removal). NULL if currently active.']
  label_claim_text varchar [note: 'Verbatim text from the approved product label or SmPC describing this indication in this jurisdiction. Used by safety scientists for causality assessment and listedness verification during case processing.']
  listedness_determination varchar [note: 'Regulatory determination of whether the adverse event indication is listed in the approved product labeling for this jurisdiction. LISTED = indication appears in approved label; UNLISTED = indication not in label; NOT_APPLICABLE = investigational product. Drives SUSAR vs non-SUSAR classification per ICH E2A and EU GVP Module VI.']
  psur_inclusion_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether adverse events for this product-indication combination should be included in Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) / Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER) analysis for this jurisdiction.']
  rmp_section_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the specific section of the Risk Management Plan (RMP) that addresses this product-indication combination, if applicable. Used for safety specification and risk minimization activities.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this product-indication listedness record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail for regulatory compliance.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the regulatory listedness determination between a PV product and its approved therapeutic indications. It captures jurisdiction-specific approval metadata, label claim text, and listedness status used for SUSAR classification and causality assessment in pharmacovigilance case processing. Each record links one pv_product to one product_indication with regulatory approval attributes that exist only in the context of this specific product-indication pairing per jurisdiction.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical pharmacovigilance operations, a single PV product (e.g., ibuprofen 200mg tablet) has multiple approved therapeutic indications across different jurisdictions (pain relief, fever reduction, inflammation), and each indication can apply to multiple PV products (same API in different formulations or strengths). The business actively manages listedness determination records per product-indication-jurisdiction combination for SUSAR classification during adverse event case processing, with each record carrying jurisdiction-specific approval dates, label claim text, and regulatory metadata that belong to neither the product nor the indication alone.'
}

  Note: 'This association product represents the expert review relationship between Risk Management Plans (RMPs) and Healthcare Professionals (HCPs). It captures the formal review process where qualified HCPs (medical reviewers, therapeutic area specialists, external consultants) evaluate RMP documents for regulatory compliance, scientific accuracy, and clinical appropriateness. Each record links one RMP version to one reviewing HCP with attributes documenting the review scope, findings, and approval status required for regulatory audit trails and quality assurance.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical regulatory operations, Risk Management Plans (RMPs) undergo formal expert review by multiple qualified healthcare professionals serving in different roles (medical reviewers, therapeutic area specialists, external consultants). Each RMP version requires review by multiple HCPs with relevant expertise, and each HCP reviews multiple RMPs throughout their engagement with the organization. The review process generates relationship-specific data (review dates, reviewer roles, sections reviewed, comments, approval status) that belongs to neither the RMP nor the HCP alone, but to the specific review event.'
}

Table pharmacovigilance.signal_indication_assessment {
  signal_indication_assessment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for the signal-indication assessment record. Primary key for the association.']
  indication_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the product indication for which this signal is being assessed']
  safety_signal_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the safety signal being assessed for this specific indication']
  assessment_date date [note: 'Date on which the indication-specific signal assessment was completed by the pharmacovigilance team.']
  assessment_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow status of the indication-specific signal assessment. Values: draft, under_review, approved, submitted_to_authority.']
  assessor_name varchar [note: 'Name or identifier of the pharmacovigilance professional who performed the indication-specific signal assessment.']
  benefit_risk_impact varchar [note: 'Assessment of how this safety signal impacts the overall benefit-risk balance specifically for this indication. Values: favorable (signal does not change positive benefit-risk), acceptable (signal noted but benefit-risk remains positive), unfavorable (signal significantly impacts benefit-risk), requires_restriction (benefit-risk only acceptable with restrictions).']
  case_count_for_indication varchar [note: 'Number of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs) contributing to this safety signal that are specifically associated with this product indication. Subset of the total signal case count stratified by indication.']
  causality_assessment varchar [note: 'Formal causality assessment of the relationship between the safety signal (adverse event) and the product when used for this specific indication. Uses WHO-UMC causality categories: certain, probable, possible, unlikely, unrelated, unassessable.']
  contraindication_recommendation varchar [note: 'Specific recommendation for adding or modifying contraindications for this indication based on the signal assessment, including patient populations, comorbidities, or concomitant medications that should be contraindicated.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the signal-indication assessment record was first created in the pharmacovigilance system.']
  fatal_case_count_for_indication varchar [note: 'Number of fatal outcome cases among the indication-specific cases contributing to this signal assessment.']
  indication_restriction_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator of whether the signal assessment recommends restricting or narrowing the approved indication (e.g., limiting to specific patient subpopulations, adding biomarker requirements, restricting line of therapy).']
  label_change_recommendation varchar [note: 'Specific recommendation for product label modification for this indication, including proposed section (warnings, precautions, adverse reactions, dosage and administration) and verbatim text recommendation.']
  prac_notification_required_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean indicator of whether this indication-specific signal assessment requires notification to the PRAC rapporteur per EMA pharmacovigilance requirements.']
  prr_value_for_indication decimal(18,6) [note: 'Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR) calculated specifically for this signal-indication combination using indication-stratified case data.']
  regulatory_action_required varchar [note: 'Type of regulatory action recommended for this signal-indication combination. Values: none, label_update, indication_restriction, indication_withdrawal, prac_referral, urgent_safety_restriction.']
  ror_value_for_indication decimal(18,6) [note: 'Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) calculated specifically for this signal-indication combination using indication-stratified case data.']
  serious_case_count_for_indication varchar [note: 'Number of Serious Adverse Event (SAE) cases among the indication-specific cases contributing to this signal assessment.']
  signal_strength_for_indication varchar [note: 'Qualitative assessment of the signal strength specifically for this indication, based on indication-stratified disproportionality analysis, case characteristics, and clinical plausibility. Values: strong, moderate, weak, insufficient.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to the signal-indication assessment record. Supports audit trail and version control.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the indication-specific safety signal assessment between safety_signal and product_indication. It captures the stratified analysis of how a particular safety signal manifests differently across approved or investigational indications for the same medicinal product. Each record links one safety signal to one product indication with indication-specific signal strength metrics, case distribution, causality assessment, and regulatory action recommendations (label changes, restrictions, contraindications) required for GVP Module IX signal validation and PRAC reporting. Supports the pharmacovigilance requirement that signal validation must be performed with indication-level stratification, as the same adverse event may have different risk profiles, causality, and benefit-risk balance across different therapeutic uses of the product.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical pharmacovigilance operations, a single safety signal (e.g., hepatotoxicity) must be assessed separately for each approved or investigational indication of a medicinal product, because the same adverse event may have different risk profiles, causality, case distributions, and benefit-risk implications across different therapeutic uses. Conversely, each product indication accumulates multiple concurrent safety signals over its lifecycle that require ongoing monitoring and indication-specific regulatory action decisions. This is an operational M:N relationship mandated by GVP Module IX signal validation requirements.'
}

Each record links one safety signal to one HCP expert with consultation-specific attributes including expert opinion, causality assessment, risk evaluation contribution, meeting participation details, and compensation tracking required for regulatory documentation per GVP Module IX and transparency reporting requirements.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical safety signal management, a single safety signal is routinely evaluated by multiple HCP experts (KOLs, advisory board members, therapeutic area specialists) to obtain diverse clinical perspectives for regulatory validation per GVP Module IX requirements. Conversely, each HCP expert consultant evaluates multiple safety signals across different therapeutic areas and products throughout their engagement with the pharmaceutical company. The business actively manages these consultation engagements as discrete operational records with consultation dates, expert opinions, causality assessments, meeting types, and honorarium tracking required for regulatory submissions and transparency reporting.'
}

  Note: 'Master record for the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) or drug substance (DS) as defined in ICH Q7.   last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp when this pharmaceutical product record was last modified. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.']
  lifecycle_status varchar [note: 'The current lifecycle status of the pharmaceutical product in the regulatory and commercial context. Indicates whether the product is actively marketed or has been withdrawn.']
  marketing_authorization_holder varchar [note: 'The legal entity that holds the marketing authorization for the pharmaceutical product and is responsible for its quality, safety, and efficacy. Also known as the license holder or applicant.']
  pharmacopoeial_standard varchar [note: 'The pharmacopoeial monograph or standard that the pharmaceutical product complies with (e.g., USP, EP, JP, BP). Defines quality specifications and test methods.']
  phpid_code varchar [note: 'ISO 11616 compliant PhPID code uniquely identifying the administrable pharmaceutical product at the international level. Used for regulatory submissions and global product identification.']
  preparation_instructions varchar [note: 'Instructions for preparing the pharmaceutical product for administration, including reconstitution, dilution, or mixing requirements. Critical for products requiring preparation before administration.']
  preservative_free_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the administrable pharmaceutical product is formulated without preservatives. Critical for products intended for intrathecal, intraocular, or neonatal use.']
  product_name varchar [note: 'The full name of the administrable pharmaceutical product as it would be described in clinical and regulatory contexts. Includes strength and administrable dose form.']
  regulatory_approval_number varchar [note: 'The regulatory approval number assigned by the health authority for this pharmaceutical product (e.g., NDA number, BLA number, MAA number). Links to the regulatory submission and approval documentation.']
  rems_required_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy is required by FDA for this pharmaceutical product due to serious safety concerns. Impacts distribution and prescribing requirements.']
  route_of_administration varchar [note: 'The path by which the pharmaceutical product is administered to the patient (e.g., intravenous, oral, subcutaneous, intramuscular, topical, inhalation). Critical for clinical usage and safety.']
  shelf_life_after_preparation_hours varchar [note: 'The maximum time in hours that the pharmaceutical product remains stable and safe for administration after preparation (reconstitution, dilution, or opening). Critical for hospital pharmacy and clinical administration.']
  sterility_requirement varchar [note: 'Indicates the sterility requirement for the administrable pharmaceutical product. Sterile products are required for parenteral, ophthalmic, and certain other routes of administration.']
  storage_conditions varchar [note: 'The required storage conditions for the administrable pharmaceutical product to maintain stability and efficacy (e.g., store at 2-8°C, protect from light, store at controlled room temperature). Critical for supply chain and pharmacy operations.']
  target_patient_population varchar [note: 'Description of the intended patient population for this administrable pharmaceutical product, including age groups, disease stage, and any specific patient characteristics (e.g., adult patients with metastatic disease, pediatric patients 2 years and older).']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'The primary therapeutic area or disease category that this pharmaceutical product is indicated for (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Cardiovascular, Neurology, Rare Diseases).']
  total_volume_ml decimal(10,3) [note: 'The total volume of the administrable pharmaceutical product in milliliters, applicable to liquid dose forms. Used for dose calculation and administration instructions.']
  unit_of_presentation varchar [note: 'The discrete unit in which the pharmaceutical product is presented for administration (e.g., vial, syringe, tablet, capsule, ampoule, inhaler). Represents the smallest administrable unit.']

  Note: 'IDMP ISO 11616 entity representing the administrable pharmaceutical product form — the product as administered to the patient, distinct from the manufactured drug product. Captures administrable dose form, route of administration, unit of presentation, and reference to constituent active ingredients. Bridges drug_product (manufactured form) to clinical usage.'
}

Table product.specified_substance {
  specified_substance_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the specified substance record. Primary key for this entity representing an IDMP ISO 11238 substance with specified detail level.']
  formulation_ingredient_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the formulation ingredient that this specified substance represents. Links to the ingredient within a specific formulation context.']
  parent_specified_substance_id varchar [note: 'Self-referencing FK on specified_substance (parent_specified_substance_id)']
  primary_specified_drug_substance_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the global substance master record. Links this specified substance to the authoritative substance definition in the substance registry.']
  unit_of_measure_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to masterdata.unit_of_measure. Business justification: Specified substance strength UOM for substance specifications (IDMP), regulatory data exchange (substance strength representation). Replaces denormalized strength_unit with FK to UOM master for standa']
  change_control_number varchar [note: 'The change control or deviation number associated with the creation or modification of this specified substance record. Links to the formal change management process.']
  concentration_unit varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for concentration. Common units include mg/mL, g/L, % w/v, % w/w, molarity (M), or other pharmacopoeial concentration units.']
  concentration_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The concentration of the substance in solution or suspension formulations. Represents the amount of substance per unit volume or weight of formulation.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this specified substance record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for record creation tracking.']
  effective_date date [note: 'The date from which this specified substance definition becomes effective and valid for use in formulations and regulatory submissions.']
  expiry_date date [note: 'The date after which this specified substance definition is no longer valid or has been superseded by a newer version. Null if currently active.']
  grade varchar [note: 'The quality grade or compendial standard of the substance. Examples include USP, EP, JP, BP, or in-house specification grade. Indicates the purity and quality standard applied.']
  idmp_substance_code varchar [note: 'The globally unique IDMP substance identifier assigned per ISO 11238 standards. Used for international regulatory submissions and substance harmonization across health authorities.']
  is_active boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this specified substance record is currently active and available for use in formulations. True indicates active, False indicates inactive or archived.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this specified substance record was last modified. Audit trail field for change tracking and data lineage.']
  lifecycle_status varchar [note: 'The current lifecycle status of the specified substance record. Indicates whether the record is actively used, inactive, obsolete, or under review for changes.']
  manufacturer_substance_code varchar [note: 'The manufacturer-specific internal code or catalog number for this specified substance. Used for procurement, quality control, and supply chain traceability.']
  molecular_formula varchar [note: 'The chemical molecular formula of the specified substance. Represents the elemental composition including any salt, solvate, or hydrate components.']
  molecular_weight decimal(12,4) [note: 'The molecular weight of the specified substance in Daltons or g/mol. Includes the weight of any salt, solvate, or hydrate components.']
  optical_activity varchar [note: 'The stereochemical configuration or optical activity of the substance. Indicates whether the substance is a specific enantiomer, racemate, or other stereoisomeric form (e.g., R, S, (+), (-), racemic).']
  polymorphic_form varchar [note: 'The specific polymorphic or crystalline form of the substance. Polymorphism can significantly impact solubility, stability, and bioavailability. Examples include Form I, Form II, amorphous.']
  purity_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'The minimum purity percentage of the specified substance as defined in the specification. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 98.5 for 98.5% purity).']
  reference_strength_unit varchar [note: 'The unit of measure for the reference strength value. Typically represents the base or active moiety unit when different from the administered substance unit.']
  reference_strength_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The numeric quantity expressed as reference strength. Used when the active moiety differs from the administered form (e.g., salt vs base). Enables standardized strength comparison across different salt forms.']
  regulatory_status varchar [note: 'The current regulatory status of the specified substance in the context of its use in medicinal products. Indicates whether the substance is approved for commercial use, under investigation, or withdrawn.']
  salt_form varchar [note: 'The specific salt form of the substance if applicable. Examples include hydrochloride, sodium, sulfate, mesylate. Critical for bioavailability and stability considerations.']
  solvate_type varchar [note: 'The type of solvate if the substance exists as a solvate. Common examples include hydrate, ethanolate, or other solvent inclusion compounds.']
  specification_level varchar [note: 'The level of detail at which the substance is specified. Indicates whether the substance is defined at molecular, salt, solvate, hydrate, polymorphic form, or mixture level per IDMP hierarchy.']
  specification_reference varchar [note: 'Reference to the quality specification document that defines the acceptance criteria for this specified substance. Links to internal specification documents or compendial monographs.']
  stoichiometry varchar [note: 'The stoichiometric ratio of components in the specified substance. Relevant for salts, solvates, hydrates, and co-crystals (e.g., 1:1, 2:1, monohydrate, hemihydrate).']
  strength_value decimal(18,6) [note: 'The numeric quantity of the substance expressed as strength. Represents the amount of active moiety or substance per unit dose or per unit of measure.']
  substance_code varchar [note: 'The standardized code identifying the substance. May be an UNII code, CAS number, or other globally recognized substance identifier used for regulatory submissions.']
  substance_name varchar [note: 'The official name of the substance at the specified level. May be INN, USAN, chemical name, or other standardized nomenclature depending on regulatory context.']
  substance_role varchar [note: 'The functional role of the substance within the formulation. Indicates whether the substance is an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API), excipient, or other functional component per IDMP requirements.']
  version_number varchar [note: 'The version number of this specified substance definition. Incremented when specification details change, enabling change control and traceability.']

  Note: 'IDMP ISO 11238 entity representing a substance with a specified level of detail including strength, reference strength, and substance role (active, excipient). Links formulation_ingredient to the global substance reference and enables precise regulatory substance identification per IDMP requirements.'
}

Table product.prescription {
  prescription_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for this prescription record. Primary key for the prescription association.']
  master_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the healthcare provider who wrote this prescription. Used for prescriber network analysis and pharmacovigilance follow-up.']
  medicinal_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the medicinal product that was prescribed']
  patient_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the patient who received the prescription']
  adherence_score decimal [note: 'Calculated adherence metric for this prescription (e.g., proportion of days covered, medication possession ratio). Used for patient support program interventions and real-world evidence studies.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this prescription record was created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.']
  discontinuation_reason varchar [note: 'Reason why this prescription was discontinued or stopped. Critical for pharmacovigilance signal detection and real-world effectiveness analysis.']
  dosage_instructions varchar [note: 'Free-text or structured dosage instructions specific to this prescription (e.g., \'10mg twice daily with food\'). Varies by patient based on indication, weight, comorbidities.']
  prescription_date date [note: 'The date when the prescription was written by the prescribing physician. Critical for therapy timeline tracking and regulatory reporting.']
  prescription_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of this prescription. Used for patient support program workflow management and adherence intervention triggering.']
  prior_authorization_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether payer prior authorization was required for this prescription. Used for market access analytics and patient support program design.']
  refill_count varchar [note: 'Number of refills dispensed for this prescription. Used for adherence monitoring and patient support program engagement tracking.']
  specialty_pharmacy_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this prescription was dispensed through a specialty pharmacy channel. Relevant for high-cost biologics, oncology products, and products requiring special handling.']
  therapy_end_date date [note: 'The date when the patient stopped taking the medicinal product. Used to calculate treatment duration and time-to-discontinuation for real-world evidence studies.']
  therapy_start_date date [note: 'The date when the patient actually started taking the medicinal product. May differ from prescription_date due to prior authorization delays or patient decision timing.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this prescription record was last updated. Used for change data capture and incremental data pipeline processing.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the prescription event between a medicinal product and a patient. It captures the commercial/post-market relationship where a specific medicinal product is prescribed to a specific patient, including prescriber information, dosage instructions, therapy timeline, adherence tracking, and discontinuation details. Each record represents one prescription instance linking one medicinal product to one patient with attributes that exist only in the context of this prescribing relationship. Distinct from clinical trial exposure (protocol-driven) and represents real-world evidence for patient support programs, adherence monitoring, and pharmacovigilance.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical commercial operations, patients routinely receive multiple medicinal products simultaneously (polypharmacy for chronic conditions, combination therapies) or sequentially (treatment switches, dose escalations), and each medicinal product is prescribed to thousands of patients across diverse indications and patient populations. Patient support programs, specialty pharmacies, and real-world evidence teams actively manage prescription-level records as operational entities, tracking adherence metrics, refill patterns, discontinuation reasons, and therapy outcomes for each patient-product combination. This is distinct from clinical trial exposure (which is protocol-mandated) and represents the post-market commercial relationship where prescription records are created, monitored, and analyzed as core business data.'
}

Each record links one drug_product to one payer_account with attributes that exist only in the context of this payer-product coverage relationship.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical market access operations, each drug product is listed on multiple payer formularies (commercial plans, Medicare Part D, Medicaid, regional health plans), and each payer account maintains formularies covering hundreds to thousands of drug products. Market access teams actively manage these formulary listings as operational business entities, negotiating tier placement, rebate terms, and access restrictions for each drug-payer combination. The formulary listing is a recognized business concept with its own lifecycle, managed through P&T committee reviews, contract negotiations, and ongoing monitoring.'
}

Table product.approved_vendor {
  approved_vendor_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for the approved_vendor association']
  excipient_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the excipient master record being sourced']
  vendor_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the qualified vendor authorized to supply this excipient']
  active_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this vendor approval is currently active and available for procurement. Inactive approvals represent historical qualifications that are no longer valid.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date when this vendor was approved to supply this specific excipient following successful qualification activities including site audit, sample testing, and quality agreement execution.']
  gmp_compliance_status varchar [note: 'GMP compliance status specific to this vendor\'s manufacturing site for this excipient. A vendor may have different compliance statuses for different materials manufactured at different sites.']
  inactivation_date date [note: 'Date when this vendor approval was inactivated, if applicable. Inactivation may occur due to vendor disqualification, quality issues, business decisions, or vendor exit.']
  inactivation_reason varchar [note: 'Business reason for inactivating this vendor approval (e.g., Quality Issues, Vendor Exit, Cost, Strategic Sourcing Decision, Regulatory Non-Compliance).']
  last_audit_date date [note: 'Date of the most recent on-site or remote audit conducted specifically for this vendor\'s capability to supply this excipient. Audit scope is material-specific and site-specific.']
  lead_time_days varchar [note: 'Standard procurement lead time in days from purchase order issuance to material receipt for this excipient from this vendor. Lead time varies by vendor and material.']
  minimum_order_quantity decimal(15,3) [note: 'Minimum order quantity required by this vendor for this excipient, typically expressed in kilograms or the standard unit of measure for the material.']
  next_audit_due_date date [note: 'Scheduled date for the next audit of this vendor for this excipient. Audit frequency is risk-based and may vary by material criticality and vendor performance history.']
  preferred_vendor_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this vendor is the preferred source for this excipient based on quality, cost, reliability, and strategic relationship. Multiple vendors may be qualified but only one is typically preferred.']
  price_currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the unit price (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).']
  qualification_status varchar [note: 'Current qualification status of this specific vendor for this specific excipient. Status is excipient-vendor specific and may differ from the vendor\'s overall qualification status.']
  quality_agreement_reference varchar [note: 'Document control number or reference identifier for the Quality Agreement governing the supply of this excipient from this vendor. Each excipient-vendor combination typically has a specific quality agreement.']
  risk_classification varchar [note: 'Risk classification for this specific excipient-vendor combination based on material criticality, vendor performance, supply continuity, regulatory compliance, and alternative source availability.']
  standard_unit_price decimal(15,4) [note: 'Current standard unit price for this excipient from this vendor in the agreed currency. Price is vendor-specific and material-specific.']
  supplier_qualification_status varchar [note: 'Current qualification status of the excipient supplier based on quality audits, performance history, and GMP compliance. Determines procurement eligibility. [Moved from excipient: Qualification status is vendor-specific and excipient-specific, not a property of the excipient itself. The same excipient may have different qualification statuses with different vendors. This attribute belongs in the approved_vendor association as qualification_status.]']
  unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Standard unit of measure for ordering and pricing this excipient from this vendor (e.g., KG, MT, LB).']

  Note: 'This association product represents the qualification and approval relationship between an excipient and a vendor authorized to supply it. It captures vendor-specific qualification status, audit history, compliance verification, and supply agreement terms that exist only in the context of this specific excipient-vendor pairing. Each record represents one approved source for one excipient.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical manufacturing, excipients are routinely multi-sourced from multiple qualified vendors to ensure supply continuity, manage risk, and meet regulatory requirements for alternative sources. Each excipient-vendor pairing requires independent qualification activities including site audits, sample testing, quality agreement execution, and ongoing compliance monitoring. The approved vendor list is an operational business entity actively managed by procurement and quality teams, with vendor-specific and material-specific attributes including qualification status, audit dates, pricing terms, lead times, and risk classifications.'
}

It captures negotiated pricing terms, rebate structures, volume commitments, and contract periods that exist only in the context of this specific product-account relationship. Each record links one medicinal product to one contract account with pricing and terms that are unique to that combination. Supports contract pricing administration, rebate management, and institutional account management business processes.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical commercial operations, institutional contract accounts (GPOs, IDNs, hospital systems, specialty pharmacies) negotiate pricing agreements for multiple medicinal products, and each medicinal product has separate pricing contracts with multiple institutional accounts. The relationship represents a real operational business process: contract pricing administration and rebate management. Commercial teams actively create, negotiate, approve, and manage these contract pricing agreements as distinct business entities with product-account-specific terms.'
}

Table product.supply_allocation {
  supply_allocation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique identifier for the supply allocation record. Primary key for the association product.']
  plant_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the manufacturing or packaging plant providing supply. Part of the composite business key (sku_id, plant_id, effective_start_date).']
  sku_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the Stock Keeping Unit being supplied. Part of the composite business key (sku_id, plant_id, effective_start_date).']
  allocation_percentage decimal(5,2) [note: 'Percentage of total SKU demand allocated to this plant in the supply network. Used for demand planning and ATP calculations. Sum of allocation percentages across all plants for a given SKU should equal 100% for active allocations. Null if allocation is based on absolute capacity rather than percentage.']
  capacity_unit_of_measure varchar [note: 'Unit of measure for the maximum capacity metric (e.g., bottles, cartons, pallets, dosage units). Should align with SKU packaging configuration.']
  cost_per_unit decimal(18,4) [note: 'Standard manufacturing cost per unit for producing this SKU at this plant. Varies by plant due to labor costs, efficiency, scale, and local regulations. Used for supply network optimization and make-vs-buy decisions. Null if cost is managed at aggregate level.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when the supply allocation record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the cost per unit (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF). Required when cost_per_unit is populated.']
  effective_end_date date [note: 'Date when this supply allocation ceases to be effective. Null for currently active allocations. Used to track supply network changes due to plant shutdowns, capacity reallocation, regulatory events, or strategic manufacturing network optimization.']
  effective_start_date date [note: 'Date when this supply allocation becomes effective. Part of the composite business key enabling temporal tracking of supply network changes. Used for supply continuity planning and historical analysis of manufacturing network evolution.']
  is_active boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the supply allocation record is currently active in the system. False if the record has been logically deleted or superseded. Used for filtering current supply network configuration.']
  last_modified_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent update to the supply allocation record. Used for change tracking and data synchronization.']
  lead_time_days bigint [note: 'Standard lead time in days from order placement to product availability for this SKU from this specific plant. Varies by plant due to manufacturing batch cycles, packaging capacity, and logistics. Used for ATP calculations, order promising, and supply planning. Different from SKU-level lead time as it captures plant-specific manufacturing and logistics characteristics.']
  maximum_capacity_units decimal(18,2) [note: 'Maximum production or packaging capacity for this SKU at this plant, expressed in SKU units (e.g., bottles, cartons). Used for capacity planning, demand allocation, and ATP calculations. Null if capacity is managed at aggregate plant level rather than SKU level.']
  minimum_order_quantity decimal(18,2) [note: 'Minimum order quantity for this SKU from this plant, driven by batch size constraints, packaging line minimums, or economic order quantities. Null if no minimum applies. Used in supply planning and order consolidation logic.']
  modified_by_user varchar [note: 'User ID or name of the person who last modified the supply allocation record. Required for audit compliance and change management.']
  primary_supply_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this plant is designated as the primary supply source for this SKU. True for primary plant, false for secondary/backup plants. Only one plant should be marked as primary for a given SKU at any point in time. Used for supply chain routing and prioritization decisions.']
  regulatory_approval_status varchar [note: 'Regulatory approval status for manufacturing this SKU at this plant for the target market. Approved indicates regulatory authority has approved this plant-SKU combination. Pending indicates approval in process. Critical for ensuring only approved plants supply to regulated markets.']
  supply_priority bigint [note: 'Numeric priority ranking for this plant in the supply network for this SKU. Lower numbers indicate higher priority (1 = highest priority). Used during supply allocation decisions when demand exceeds capacity or when plants experience disruptions. Enables cascading supply logic in ATP and order promising systems.']
  supply_status varchar [note: 'Current operational status of this supply allocation. Active indicates currently supplying, Planned indicates future supply source, Suspended indicates temporary disruption (e.g., plant maintenance, regulatory hold), Discontinued indicates permanently ended. Used for supply availability checks and network planning.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the supply relationship between a Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) and a manufacturing/packaging plant. It captures the multi-sourcing strategy for each SKU across the pharmaceutical manufacturing network, including primary and secondary supply designations, allocation percentages, lead times, and supply priority. Each record links one SKU to one plant with attributes that exist only in the context of this supply relationship. Critical for supply chain planning, available-to-promise (ATP) calculations, demand allocation during capacity constraints, and supply continuity management during plant shutdowns or regulatory events.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical supply chain operations, SKUs are routinely sourced from multiple manufacturing and packaging plants to ensure supply continuity, balance capacity utilization, and comply with regulatory requirements for multi-site approval. Each plant can produce multiple SKUs across different therapeutic areas and dosage forms. The business actively manages these supply allocations with plant-specific data including allocation percentages, primary/secondary designations, lead times, supply priority rankings, and regulatory approval status for each plant-SKU combination.'
}

Table product.drug_product_assay_specification {

  specification_expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which this specification was superseded or retired. Null if currently active.']
  specification_limit varchar [note: 'The acceptance criteria or specification range for this assay when applied to this drug product (e.g., 95.0-105.0% of label claim, NMT 2.0% RSD). Product-specific and may differ from assay platform defaults.']
  specification_version varchar [note: 'Version identifier for this specification record, enabling change control and audit trail when acceptance criteria or testing frequency are revised.']
  test_frequency varchar [note: 'The cadence at which this assay must be performed on this drug product, driven by regulatory commitments, stability protocols, or risk-based testing strategies.']
  upper_specification_limit decimal(18,6) [note: 'Numeric upper bound of the acceptance range for computational validation and trending. Null if specification is qualitative or one-sided.']
  validation_protocol_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier for the validation protocol or report that qualifies this assay for use with this specific drug product.']
  validation_status varchar [note: 'The current validation state of this assay specifically for this drug product. An assay may be validated for one product but require transfer or revalidation for another.']
  created_by varchar [note: 'User or system identifier that created this specification record.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the quality control testing specification between a drug product and an assay. It captures the regulatory and operational requirements for testing each drug product using specific assays. Each record links one drug product to one assay with attributes that define the testing protocol, acceptance criteria, and regulatory commitments that exist only in the context of this specific product-assay combination.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical quality control operations, a single drug product requires multiple assays for comprehensive testing (potency, purity, dissolution, stability, impurities, content uniformity), and a single validated assay is reused across multiple drug products (platform assays, compendial methods like USP dissolution). The business actively manages these specifications as regulatory commitments with product-specific acceptance criteria, testing frequencies, and validation protocols that cannot reside on either the assay or drug product alone.'
}

Used for data lineage and reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EDC|LIMS|CENTRAL_LAB|MOLECULAR_DIAGNOSTICS|IMAGING_PACS|EHR|OTHER — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  delta_from_baseline_flag boolean [note: 'Boolean flag indicating whether this observation represents a change from baseline value. True if this is a delta calculation, False if this is an absolute measurement. Used for longitudinal analysis and safety monitoring.']
  endpoint_response varchar [note: 'Categorical response or outcome for clinical endpoint assessments (e.g., complete response (CR), partial response (PR), stable disease (SD), progressive disease (PD) for RECIST; remission, relapse for DAS28). Uses standardized response criteria.']
  gene_name varchar [note: 'Name of the gene analyzed in genomic or pharmacogenomic testing (e.g., EGFR, KRAS, BRCA1, TP53). Uses HGNC (HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee) standard gene symbols.']
  laboratory_identifier varchar [note: 'Unique identifier for the laboratory or assay vendor (e.g., CLIA number, CAP accreditation number, vendor assay catalog ID). Used for traceability and regulatory submissions.']
  laboratory_name varchar [note: 'Name of the laboratory, imaging center, or facility that performed the test or assessment. Used for quality control and result reconciliation.']
  mutation_detected varchar [note: 'Specific genetic mutation or variant detected (e.g., EGFR L858R, KRAS G12C, BRCA1 c.68_69delAG). Uses HGVS (Human Genome Variation Society) nomenclature for precision.']
  observation_category varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the clinical observation type. Aligns with CDISC findings-class domains (LB=laboratory, VS=vital signs, MB=microbiology/biomarker, TR=tumor response).']
  observation_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the observation record in the data lifecycle. Preliminary results may be updated; final results are locked for analysis. Amended indicates a correction was made post-finalization.']
  out_of_range_indicator varchar [note: 'Flag indicating whether the result is within, above, or below the reference range. Critical for safety monitoring and adverse event (AE) detection.']
  record_created_datetime timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this observation record was first created in the source system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking per Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.']
  record_updated_datetime timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this observation record was last modified in the source system. Used for audit trail and change tracking per Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and 21 CFR Part 11 requirements.']

  reference_range_upper decimal(18,6) [note: 'Upper bound of the normal reference range for this test. Used to determine if result is out of range (high). May vary by age, sex, and laboratory.']
  result_interpretation varchar [note: 'Clinical interpretation or assessment of the result by the investigator or central reviewer (e.g., clinically significant, not clinically significant, consistent with disease progression). Free-text field.']
  result_value_numeric decimal(18,6) [note: 'Numeric result value for quantitative observations (e.g., hemoglobin level, blood pressure, tumor size, biomarker concentration). Null for qualitative or categorical results.']
  result_value_text varchar [note: 'Text or categorical result value for qualitative observations (e.g., positive/negative, normal/abnormal, gene mutation detected). Used when result is not numeric.']
  specimen_type varchar [note: 'Type of biological specimen collected for laboratory or biomarker testing (e.g., blood, serum, plasma, urine, tissue, saliva, cerebrospinal fluid). Uses SNOMED CT or CDISC controlled terminology.']
  test_code varchar [note: 'Standardized code for the test or assessment. Typically LOINC code for laboratory tests, SNOMED CT for clinical findings, or proprietary assay identifier for genomic tests.']
  test_code_system varchar [note: 'The coding system or terminology used for the test_code field. Identifies the standard vocabulary (LOINC, SNOMED CT, CDISC controlled terminology, or proprietary assay catalog).']
  test_name varchar [note: 'The name of the laboratory test, vital sign measurement, biomarker assay, or clinical assessment performed. Free-text or standardized name from LOINC or assay catalog.']
  toxicity_grade varchar [note: 'Severity grade for laboratory abnormalities using CTCAE grading scale (Grade 0=none, Grade 1=mild, Grade 2=moderate, Grade 3=severe, Grade 4=life-threatening, Grade 5=death). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: GRADE_0|GRADE_1|GRADE_2|GRADE_3|GRADE_4|GRADE_5|NOT_APPLICABLE — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']

  Note: 'Consolidated clinical findings and measurements collected from participants across all observation categories. Covers laboratory results (LOINC-coded tests, specimen type, toxicity grade), vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, weight, BMI, respiratory rate, SpO2), biomarker/genomic results (CDx, TMB, PD-L1, MSI, PGx panels, gene mutations), and clinical endpoint assessments (RECIST 1.1, iRECIST, DAS28, ECOG PS, Karnofsky). Table patient.patient_enrollment2 {
  patient_enrollment2_id varchar [pk, note: 'Primary key for patient_enrollment2']
  patient_id varchar [note: 'Auto-generated FK linking siloed enrollment to patient']

  Note: 'This association product represents the enrollment relationship between a patient and a patient support program (PSP). It captures the complete lifecycle of a patient\'s participation in a specific support program, including enrollment dates, eligibility verification, benefit tracking, and disenrollment. Each record links one patient to one support program with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific enrollment relationship. This is the operational record that enables tracking of copay assistance utilization, adherence monitoring participation, and program-specific patient outcomes.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical patient services operations, patients routinely enroll in multiple patient support programs simultaneously (e.g., copay assistance for one brand, adherence monitoring for another, nurse educator support for a third therapeutic area). Conversely, each support program serves thousands of patients concurrently. The enrollment relationship is a recognized operational business entity with its own lifecycle, managed actively by patient services teams, hub vendors, and specialty pharmacies.'
}

  data_collection_frequency varchar [note: 'Frequency at which data is collected for this specific product within the registry context.
