  medicinal_product_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the drug product (Drug Product / Finished Dosage Form) for which the marketing authorization was obtained and which forms the basis of the extension application. Links the extension to the commercial product in the master data.']
  patent_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the underlying base patent record in the IP portfolio for which this term extension or SPC is being sought. Links the extension to the specific patent being extended.']
  regulatory_inspection_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_inspection. Business justification: PTE applications are verified during regulatory inspections. Inspectors validate regulatory review period calculations and marketing authorization dates. Essential for inspection response and complian']
  responsible_employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical regulatory affairs assigns employees to manage PTE applications for FDA/EMA submission coordination, regulatory review period calculation, and opposition response. Critical for lifecycl']
  adjusted_expiry_date date [note: 'The new patent expiry date after application of the granted term extension or SPC. Calculated as base_patent_expiry_date plus granted_extension_days. This is the Loss of Exclusivity (LOE) date for the product in this jurisdiction and is the primary output used in lifecycle management and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategies.']
  applicant_delay_days varchar [note: 'Number of days deducted from the regulatory review period due to delays attributable to the applicant (e.g., failure to respond to FDA requests within the prescribed period). Reduces the calculated extension duration under 35 U.S.C. § 156(c)(1). Tracked for audit and dispute resolution purposes.']
  application_number varchar [note: 'The official application number assigned by the granting authority (e.g., USPTO, EPO, UKIPO, JPO) when the patent term extension or SPC application was filed. Serves as the primary external business identifier for tracking the application through the regulatory process.']
  approval_phase_start_date date [note: 'For US PTE calculations: the date on which the regulatory approval phase began, typically the date of NDA/BLA submission to the FDA. Used to calculate the approval phase component of the regulatory review period under 35 U.S.C. § 156(g)(1)(B).']
  atc_code varchar [note: 'The WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) classification code assigned to the active substance covered by the extension. Provides standardized classification for cross-portfolio analytics, competitive intelligence, and regulatory reporting.']
  base_patent_expiry_date date [note: 'The original expiry date of the underlying base patent before any term extension or adjustment is applied. Used as the baseline for calculating the adjusted expiry date and the duration of the extension period.']
  base_patent_number varchar [note: 'The official patent number of the underlying patent for which the term extension or SPC is sought (e.g., US10,123,456 or EP1234567). For SPC purposes, this is the \'basic patent\' as defined under Article 1(c) of EU Regulation 469/2009. Retained as a denormalized field for direct reference without joining to the patent table.']
  calculated_extension_days varchar [note: 'The number of days of patent term extension calculated based on the regulatory review period formula. For US PTE: one-half of the testing phase plus the approval phase, capped at 5 years with remaining patent life not exceeding 14 years post-approval. For EU SPC: period between IND filing and MA grant minus 5 years, capped at 5 years.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this patent term extension record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.']
  data_exclusivity_expiry_date date [note: 'The date on which regulatory data exclusivity (also known as data protection) expires for the product in this jurisdiction. In the EU, this is 8+2+1 years from first authorization; in the US, 5 years for NCEs or 12 years for biologics. Tracked alongside PTE/SPC to determine the complete exclusivity landscape.']
  decision_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the patent term extension or SPC application. Tracks the application from initial drafting through filing, examination, and final decision by the granting authority. Critical for LOE (Loss of Exclusivity) date calculation and portfolio management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|under_review|granted|refused|withdrawn|appealed|lapsed|invalidated — promote to reference product]']
  external_counsel_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or name of the external patent law firm or legal counsel managing this patent term extension or SPC application. Used for coordination of legal strategy, correspondence tracking, and matter management. Marked confidential as it reflects privileged legal relationships.']
  filing_date date [note: 'The date on which the patent term extension or SPC application was formally filed with the granting authority. For US PTE, must be filed within 60 days of first marketing approval. For EU SPC, must be filed within 6 months of marketing authorization grant. Critical for determining application validity.']
  grant_date date [note: 'The date on which the granting authority officially granted the patent term extension or SPC. Null if the application has not yet been decided or was refused/withdrawn. Used to confirm the effective start of the extended protection period.']
  granted_extension_days varchar [note: 'The actual number of days of patent term extension officially granted by the granting authority. May differ from the calculated extension if the authority applies different determinations of the regulatory review period or applicant delay deductions. Null until the extension is formally granted.']
  granting_authority varchar [note: 'Name of the national or regional intellectual property office responsible for examining and granting the patent term extension or SPC (e.g., USPTO, EPO, UKIPO, JPO, CIPO, IP Australia). Determines procedural rules and timelines.']
  loe_date date [note: 'The effective Loss of Exclusivity (LOE) date for the product in this jurisdiction, accounting for all applicable exclusivity mechanisms (PTE/SPC, pediatric extension, orphan drug exclusivity, data exclusivity). This is the single most critical date for commercial planning, generic/biosimilar entry defense, and lifecycle management strategy. Represents the date after which generic or biosimilar competition may legally enter the market.']
  marketing_authorization_date date [note: 'The date on which the first marketing authorization for the product was granted in the relevant jurisdiction. This date is critical for calculating the regulatory review period and the permissible extension duration under Hatch-Waxman PTE and EU SPC frameworks.']
  marketing_authorization_number varchar [note: 'The official marketing authorization number (NDA number, BLA number, EU MA number, or national equivalent) that forms the regulatory basis for the extension application. For EU SPC, this is the first authorization to place the product on the market in the Community per Article 3(b) of Regulation 469/2009.']
  mechanism_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the patent term extension mechanism. PTE = US Hatch-Waxman Patent Term Extension under 35 U.S.C. § 156; SPC = EU/UK Supplementary Protection Certificate under EC Regulation 469/2009; national_equivalent = country-specific analogous mechanisms (e.g., Japan, Canada, Australia); pediatric_extension = additional 6-month pediatric exclusivity; data_exclusivity = regulatory data protection period. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PTE|SPC|national_equivalent|pediatric_extension|data_exclusivity|regulatory_data_protection — promote to reference product]']
  notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for capturing additional context, legal strategy notes, authority correspondence summaries, or other relevant information pertaining to this patent term extension or SPC record that is not captured in structured fields. Used by IP counsel and regulatory affairs teams.']
  opposition_date date [note: 'The date on which a third-party opposition, invalidity action, or equivalent challenge was filed against this patent term extension or SPC. Null if no opposition has been filed. Used to track litigation timelines and coordinate with legal counsel.']
  opposition_filed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a third party (e.g., generic manufacturer, biosimilar applicant) has filed an opposition, invalidity action, or equivalent challenge against this patent term extension or SPC. True triggers escalation to the legal team for litigation management and LOE date reassessment.']
  orphan_drug_exclusivity boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the product covered by this extension also benefits from orphan drug exclusivity (7 years in the US under the Orphan Drug Act, 10 years in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 141/2000). Used in conjunction with PTE/SPC to determine the effective exclusivity cliff date.']
  pediatric_extension_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this patent term extension or SPC is eligible for an additional 6-month pediatric extension under the US Best Pharmaceuticals for Children Act (BPCA) or EU Paediatric Regulation (EC) No 1901/2006. True if a Written Request (US) or Paediatric Investigation Plan (EU) has been completed and accepted.']
  pediatric_extension_granted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the additional 6-month pediatric extension has been formally granted on top of the base PTE or SPC. Distinct from eligibility — this flag confirms the authority has approved the pediatric supplement. When True, the adjusted_expiry_date should reflect the additional 6 months.']
  regulatory_review_period_days varchar [note: 'The total number of days of the regulatory review period as determined by the granting authority. For US PTE, this is the period from IND filing to NDA/BLA approval, reduced by any applicant-caused delays. Directly determines the maximum permissible extension duration under 35 U.S.C. § 156.']
  spc_product_definition varchar [note: 'For EU/UK SPC applications only: the definition of the \'product\' as per Article 1(b) of EU Regulation 469/2009, specifying the active ingredient or combination of active ingredients of a medicinal product. This definition determines the scope of SPC protection and is critical for freedom-to-operate analyses and generic entry defense.']
  testing_phase_start_date date [note: 'For US PTE calculations: the date on which the regulatory review testing phase began, typically the date of IND (Investigational New Drug) application submission. Used to calculate the testing phase component of the regulatory review period under 35 U.S.C. § 156(g)(1).']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'The therapeutic area or disease indication for which the drug product covered by the extension is approved (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular, Neurology). Used for portfolio analytics, lifecycle management planning, and commercial strategy alignment.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this patent term extension record was most recently modified. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking for IP portfolio management and regulatory compliance.']
  veeva_vault_document_reference varchar [note: 'The document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM (Regulatory Information Management) where the official extension application documents, correspondence with the granting authority, and supporting regulatory dossier are stored. Enables direct navigation from this record to the source regulatory documents.']

  Note: 'Records all patent term extension and supplementary protection mechanisms across global jurisdictions that compensate for regulatory review time lost during drug approval. Covers US Hatch-Waxman Patent Term Extension (PTE), EU/UK Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPC), Japanese patent term extension, and equivalent national mechanisms. Captures application number, mechanism type (PTE, SPC, national equivalent), filing date, patent reference, product reference, marketing authorization reference, regulatory review period, calculated/granted extension duration, adjusted expiry date, granting authority, decision status, SPC-specific fields (basic patent, product definition per Article 1(b)), and pediatric extension eligibility. Single source of truth for all patent term adjustments — critical for accurate LOE date calculation across all markets.'
}

Table intellectual.ip_watch {
  ip_watch_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique system-generated identifier for each IP watch record tracking a third-party IP activity that may threaten the company\'s portfolio.']
  country_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to masterdata.country. Business justification: Competitive intelligence is jurisdiction-specific; required for paragraph IV response planning, biosimilar monitoring, and market-specific threat assessment.']
  lead_patent_counsel_employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical competitive intelligence assigns internal IP counsel to watch items for threat assessment, paragraph IV response coordination, and litigation decision-making. Replaces text field lead_p']
  patent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to intellectual.patent. Business justification: IP watch records track competitive intelligence on third-party patents that may threaten the company\'s freedom to operate. The patent_number (STRING) should be replaced with a FK to patent.patent_id t']
  risk_register_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_risk_register. Business justification: IP watch activities (competitor filings, Paragraph IV notices, biosimilar applications) identify compliance risks (exclusivity loss, revenue at risk, litigation exposure) that populate risk registers ']
  affected_ndc varchar [note: 'The National Drug Code (NDC) of the specific drug product formulation or SKU threatened by the competitor\'s filing. Enables precise linkage to the commercial product portfolio and Orange Book listings.']
  affected_product_name varchar [note: 'The proprietary or International Nonproprietary Name (INN) of the company\'s drug product that is potentially threatened by the competitor\'s IP activity. Supports linkage to commercial and lifecycle management decisions.']
  authority_name varchar [note: 'The name of the regulatory or intellectual property authority with which the competitor\'s filing was made, such as FDA, EMA, USPTO, EPO, PMDA, or NMPA. Provides context for applicable rules and timelines.']
  biosimilar_interchangeability boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the competitor\'s aBLA biosimilar application seeks an interchangeability designation with the company\'s reference biologic product. Interchangeable biosimilars may be substituted at the pharmacy level without prescriber intervention, representing a higher commercial threat.']
  closed_date date [note: 'The date on which the IP watch record was formally closed, indicating that the threat has been resolved, the litigation concluded, the competitor\'s application was withdrawn or rejected, or the matter is no longer actively monitored.']
  commercial_revenue_at_risk decimal(18,2) [note: 'Estimated annual revenue (in USD) of the affected product that is at risk of erosion if the competitor\'s generic or biosimilar entry is successful. Used to prioritize IP defense investment and inform lifecycle management decisions.']
  competitor_country varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country of incorporation or principal operations of the competitor entity filing the IP activity.']
  competitor_name varchar [note: 'Name of the third-party company or entity that filed the competing patent, ANDA, aBLA, or patent challenge being monitored. Critical for competitive intelligence and IP defense strategy.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp at which this IP watch record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and compliance with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements.']
  detected_date date [note: 'The date on which the company\'s IP watch function first identified or was notified of the competitor\'s filing or IP activity. Used to measure response time and early warning effectiveness.']
  estimated_generic_entry_date date [note: 'The estimated date on which the competitor\'s generic drug or biosimilar product could enter the market, based on patent expiry, exclusivity expiry, regulatory approval timelines, and litigation outcomes. Critical for lifecycle management and revenue forecasting.']
  exclusivity_at_risk varchar [note: 'The type of regulatory exclusivity period that may be threatened or circumvented by the competitor\'s filing, such as orphan drug exclusivity, data exclusivity, pediatric exclusivity, New Chemical Entity (NCE) exclusivity, New Biological Entity (NBE) exclusivity, or Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) protection.']
  filing_date date [note: 'The date on which the competitor filed the patent application, ANDA, aBLA, or patent challenge with the relevant regulatory or IP authority. This is the principal real-world event date for the watch record.']
  filing_reference_number varchar [note: 'The official reference number assigned by the regulatory or IP authority to the competitor\'s filing, such as an ANDA application number, aBLA application number, USPTO patent application number, or IPR petition number. Enables direct cross-referencing with public databases.']
  fto_analysis_required boolean [note: 'Indicates whether a Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis is required in response to the competitor\'s patent filing or IP activity, to assess whether the company\'s products or processes may infringe the competitor\'s claims.']
  fto_analysis_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the Freedom-to-Operate (FTO) analysis associated with this IP watch record, tracking whether the analysis has been initiated, is in progress, or has been completed.']
  lawsuit_filed boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the company has filed a patent infringement lawsuit in response to the competitor\'s Paragraph IV certification or other IP challenge. Triggers the 30-month stay of FDA approval under Hatch-Waxman.']
  lawsuit_filing_date date [note: 'The date on which the company filed the patent infringement lawsuit in response to the IP threat. Must be within 45 days of receiving the Paragraph IV notice letter to trigger the 30-month stay.']
  outside_counsel_firm varchar [note: 'Name of the external law firm engaged to represent the company in litigation or IP proceedings related to this watch record. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.']
  paragraph_iv_certification boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the competitor\'s ANDA or 505(b)(2) submission includes a Paragraph IV certification asserting that the company\'s listed patent is invalid or will not be infringed. Triggers the 30-month stay provision under the Hatch-Waxman Act.']
  paragraph_iv_notice_date date [note: 'The date on which the company received the formal Paragraph IV notice letter from the ANDA or 505(b)(2) applicant, as required under the Hatch-Waxman Act. The 45-day window to file suit and trigger the 30-month stay begins from this date.']
  recommended_response varchar [note: 'The recommended strategic or legal response to the identified IP threat, such as filing a patent infringement lawsuit, filing an IPR petition, seeking a preliminary injunction, entering licensing negotiations, or monitoring without action. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.']
  resolution_outcome varchar [note: 'The final outcome of the IP dispute or watch activity upon closure, indicating whether the matter was settled (e.g., licensing agreement), won by the company, lost (competitor entry permitted), withdrawn by the competitor, dismissed by the authority, or remains ongoing.']
  response_deadline date [note: 'The statutory or internally-set deadline by which the company must initiate a legal or regulatory response to the IP threat (e.g., 45-day deadline to file suit following Paragraph IV notice, IPR petition deadline of 1 year from service of infringement complaint).']
  risk_assessment_summary varchar [note: 'Narrative summary of the risk assessment conducted by the IP and legal team, describing the basis for the risk level assignment, key vulnerabilities, and potential commercial exposure. Classified as confidential due to legal strategy sensitivity.']
  risk_level varchar [note: 'Assessed risk level of the IP threat to the company\'s portfolio, reflecting the likelihood of successful generic or biosimilar entry and the commercial impact. Drives prioritization of legal and IP defense resources.']
  technology_area varchar [note: 'The scientific or technical domain of the IP activity, such as small molecule chemistry, biologics, formulation technology, manufacturing process, delivery device, or specific therapeutic mechanism. Aligns with internal R&D and IP portfolio taxonomy.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'The disease or clinical indication area relevant to the IP activity, such as oncology, immunology, rare diseases, cardiovascular, or neurology. Used to prioritize IP defense resources by commercial importance.']
  thirty_month_stay_expiry date [note: 'The date on which the 30-month stay of FDA approval expires following a Paragraph IV certification and timely patent infringement lawsuit. Null if no Paragraph IV certification was filed. Critical for generic entry timeline planning.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The timestamp at which this IP watch record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.']
  watch_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for additional context, observations, or legal strategy notes related to the IP watch record, entered by the IP analyst or legal counsel. Classified as confidential due to potential legal strategy content.']
  watch_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier assigned to this IP watch record, used for cross-referencing with legal counsel, RIMS, and Veeva Vault RIM module. Typically follows a structured format such as IPW-YYYY-NNNNNN.']
  watch_source varchar [note: 'The source or monitoring service through which the IP activity was identified, such as FDA Orange Book, FDA ANDA database, USPTO patent database, EPO database, EMA biosimilar register, Derwent Innovation, Clarivate IP watch service, or internal monitoring. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fda_orange_book|fda_anda_database|uspto_database|epo_database|ema_register|derwent_innovation|clarivate_watch|internal_monitoring|third_party_service — promote to reference product]']
  watch_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the IP watch record, indicating whether the threat is newly identified (open), being assessed (under_review), escalated to legal or senior management, actively monitored (monitoring), or resolved (closed).']
  watch_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the third-party IP activity being monitored. Covers competitor patent filings, Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) submissions, 505(b)(2) submissions, abbreviated Biologics License Application (aBLA) biosimilar filings, patent challenges (e.g., IPR, PGR, inter partes review), and trademark oppositions.']

  Note: 'Competitive intelligence records tracking third-party IP activities that may threaten the company\'s portfolio. Monitors competitor patent filings, ANDA/505(b)(2) submissions, biosimilar applications (aBLA), and patent challenges. Captures watch type, competitor, filing date, reference number, technology area, affected products, risk assessment, and recommended response. Supports proactive IP defense and early warning for generic/biosimilar entry.'
}

Table intellectual.ip_valuation {
  ip_valuation_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each IP valuation record in the pharmaceutical IP portfolio. Primary key for the ip_valuation data product.']
  fixed_asset_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.fixed_asset. Business justification: IP valuations determine carrying value of capitalized patents/trademarks in fixed asset register. Finance links valuation reports to asset records for purchase price allocation (M&A), impairment testi']
  lead_valuator_employee_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Pharmaceutical finance requires tracking which employee conducted IP valuations for SOX compliance, transfer pricing documentation, and impairment testing. Replaces text field lead_valuator_name with ']
  medicinal_product_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to product.medicinal_product. Business justification: IP valuations driven by product commercial forecasts. Essential for M&A, impairment testing, transfer pricing, and portfolio prioritization. Removes denormalized inn and nda_bla_number.']
  patent_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the patent record in the intellectual.patent product that is the subject of this valuation. Enables linkage to patent expiry, exclusivity periods, and prosecution status for lifecycle management decisions.']
  rd_capitalization_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.rd_capitalization. Business justification: IP valuations determine fair value of capitalized R&D for purchase price allocation, impairment testing, and transfer pricing studies. Finance links valuation reports to capitalized R&D records for ca']
  amortization_method varchar [note: 'Accounting method used to systematically allocate the cost of the intangible IP asset over its useful economic life.   annual_amortization_charge decimal(20,4) [note: 'Annual amortization expense amount for the IP asset in the valuation currency, calculated based on the carrying value and amortization method. Used for P&L reporting, R&D capitalization decisions, and COGS allocation in pharmaceutical financial statements.']
  approval_date date [note: 'Date on which the valuation was formally approved by the authorized internal reviewer. Marks the transition of valuation_status from in_review to approved and establishes the effective date for financial reporting use.']

  carrying_value decimal(20,4) [note: 'Net book value of the IP asset on the balance sheet as of the valuation date, after accumulated amortization and any impairment charges. Compared against fair market value to determine whether an impairment loss must be recognized under IAS 36.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this IP valuation record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit trail creation marker required for SOX-compliant internal controls and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.']

  discount_rate_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'Risk-adjusted discount rate (expressed as a percentage, e.g., 12.50 for 12.5%) applied in the income approach or DCF valuation to convert projected future cash flows to present value. Reflects the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) or IP-specific risk premium. Critical input for sensitivity analysis and impairment testing.']
  exclusivity_expiry_date date [note: 'Date on which the most commercially significant regulatory exclusivity period (data exclusivity, orphan drug exclusivity, or pediatric exclusivity) expires for the IP asset. Represents the effective end of market protection and is a critical input to the DCF projection horizon and generic/biosimilar entry defense strategy.']
  fair_market_value decimal(20,4) [note: 'Estimated fair market value of the IP asset as of the valuation date, expressed in the valuation currency. Represents the price at which the asset would change hands between a willing buyer and willing seller, neither being under compulsion. Used for IAS 38 intangible asset recognition and balance sheet reporting.']
  impairment_indicator_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether one or more impairment indicators (as defined under IAS 36) were identified for this IP asset at the valuation date. Triggers a formal impairment test when True. Indicators include clinical trial failure, regulatory rejection, loss of market exclusivity, or significant decline in projected revenues.']
  impairment_loss_amount decimal(20,4) [note: 'Amount by which the carrying value exceeds the recoverable amount of the IP asset, recognized as an impairment loss in the income statement.   ip_asset_type varchar [note: 'Classification of the IP asset being valued. Determines applicable valuation methodology and accounting treatment under IAS 38. Patents cover NCE/NBE/formulation/process IP; trademarks cover brand assets; trade secrets and know-how cover undisclosed proprietary information; exclusivity types cover regulatory-granted market protections. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: patent|trademark|trade_secret|know_how|data_exclusivity|orphan_drug_exclusivity|dmf|rems — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]']
  litigation_support_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this valuation was prepared in connection with patent infringement litigation, inter partes review (IPR), or other IP dispute proceedings. When True, the valuation is subject to legal privilege considerations and must be coordinated with external patent litigation counsel.']
  next_review_date date [note: 'Date by which this valuation must be reviewed or refreshed. Supports proactive impairment monitoring.']
  peak_sales_forecast decimal(20,4) [note: 'Projected peak annual net sales attributable to the IP asset, expressed in valuation currency.   probability_of_success_pct decimal(6,4) [note: 'Risk-adjusted probability (expressed as a percentage, e.g., 65.00 for 65%) that the IP asset will achieve full commercial realization, accounting for clinical development risk, regulatory approval probability, and market access uncertainty. Applied as a risk adjustment factor in rNPV (risk-adjusted Net Present Value) income approach valuations.']
  rd_capitalization_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the IP asset meets the IAS 38 criteria for capitalization of development costs (technical feasibility, intention to complete, ability to use/sell, probable future economic benefits, adequate resources, ability to measure expenditure). When True, associated development costs are capitalized rather than expensed.']
  report_issue_date date [note: 'Date on which the formal valuation report was issued by the valuation firm or internal team. May differ from valuation_date when retrospective valuations are performed for M&A due diligence or tax transfer pricing purposes.']
  risk_adjusted_npv decimal(20,4) [note: 'Risk-adjusted net present value of the IP asset, calculated by applying the probability_of_success_pct to the DCF-derived NPV. Standard valuation metric in pharmaceutical IP for assets still in clinical development. Expressed in valuation currency.']
  royalty_rate_pct decimal(8,4) [note: 'Notional or actual royalty rate (expressed as a percentage of net sales) used in the relief-from-royalty valuation method or as the basis for intercompany licensing transfer pricing. Derived from comparable uncontrolled transactions or industry benchmarks for the relevant therapeutic area and IP type.']
  sap_asset_number varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA Fixed Asset (FI-AA module) asset number assigned to the intangible IP asset on the balance sheet. Enables reconciliation between the IP valuation record and the SAP general ledger intangible asset register for IAS 38 balance sheet reporting and amortization posting.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Therapeutic area classification of the drug or biologic associated with the IP asset (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio segmentation, royalty rate benchmarking, and comparable transaction analysis in market approach valuations.']
  transfer_pricing_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this valuation was prepared specifically to support intercompany IP licensing transfer pricing documentation under OECD guidelines. When True, the valuation must comply with OECD BEPS Action 8-10 arm\'s length principle requirements and be included in the transfer pricing master file.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp of the most recent modification to this IP valuation record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Required for SOX audit trail, data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer, and change detection in downstream financial reporting pipelines.']
  useful_economic_life_years decimal(6,2) [note: 'Estimated remaining useful economic life of the IP asset in years as of the valuation date. For patents, typically aligned with remaining patent term or commercial exclusivity period. Drives amortization schedule and DCF projection horizon under IAS 38.']
  valuation_currency varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the valuation amounts (fair market value, carrying value, royalty rate base) are expressed. Enables multi-currency consolidation for global pharmaceutical IP portfolios.']
  valuation_date date [note: 'The reference date as of which the IP asset fair market value is determined. This is the principal business event date for the valuation — distinct from the date the report was issued or approved. Required for IAS 38 impairment testing and balance sheet reporting.']
  valuation_firm_name varchar [note: 'Name of the external valuation firm or internal team that performed the IP valuation. Required for SOX audit trail and independence assessment.   valuation_notes varchar [note: 'Free-text field for material assumptions, key value drivers, sensitivity analysis commentary, or qualifications noted by the valuator.   valuation_reference_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known unique alphanumeric reference number assigned to this valuation engagement, typically issued by the valuation firm or internal finance team. Used for cross-referencing with audit files, board papers, and external valuation reports.']
  valuation_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle state of the valuation record. Draft indicates work-in-progress; in_review indicates submission to finance/legal for approval; approved indicates SOX-compliant sign-off; superseded indicates replaced by a newer valuation; withdrawn indicates cancelled prior to approval.']

  payment_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the annuity fee payment obligation. \'paid\' indicates the fee has been successfully remitted; \'overdue\' indicates the due date has passed without payment; \'waived\' indicates the fee has been formally waived (e.g., small entity, micro-entity); \'lapsed\' indicates the patent has lapsed due to non-payment; \'pending\' indicates payment is in process; \'scheduled\' indicates payment is queued for future processing.']
  reinstatement_eligible boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the lapsed patent is eligible for reinstatement or restoration under the applicable jurisdiction\'s rules (e.g., USPTO petition for revival, EPO re-establishment of rights). Relevant only when payment_status is \'lapsed\'.']

  reminder_sent_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether an automated or manual payment reminder notification has been sent to the responsible IP manager or paying agent ahead of the annuity fee due date. Supports proactive portfolio maintenance workflows.']
  sap_payment_document_number varchar [note: 'The SAP S/4HANA FI payment document number generated when the annuity fee payment is posted in the financial system, enabling end-to-end reconciliation between IP management records and the general ledger.']
  surcharge_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'Additional surcharge amount applied when the annuity fee is paid during the grace period after the original due date. Zero or null if payment was made on time.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'The therapeutic area or disease indication associated with the patent being maintained (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Cardiovascular). Used for portfolio cost allocation and strategic IP investment analysis.']
  total_payment_amount decimal(18,4) [note: 'The total amount actually paid, comprising the base annuity fee amount plus any applicable surcharges, agent service fees, or adjustments. Represents the net cash outflow for this annuity obligation.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when this annuity fee record was last modified in the system, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Used for change tracking, audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing.']
  veeva_vault_doc_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier for the annuity fee payment confirmation, receipt document, or related correspondence stored in Veeva Vault RIM, enabling document traceability and audit compliance.']
  waiver_reason varchar [note: 'Documented business justification for waiving an annuity fee payment, applicable when payment_status is \'waived\'. Examples include strategic portfolio pruning, patent no longer commercially relevant, or covered product discontinued. Null if not waived.']

  Note: 'Tracks patent annuity (maintenance fee) payment obligations and payment history across all jurisdictions for the patent portfolio. Captures patent reference, jurisdiction, fee year, due date, fee amount, currency, payment date, payment status (paid, overdue, waived, lapsed), paying agent, and confirmation receipt number. Failure to pay annuities results in patent lapse, making this a critical operational record for portfolio maintenance.'
}

  licensing_agreement_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the parent licensing, co-development, or collaboration agreement under which this milestone is defined. Links to the intellectual.licensing_agreement product.']
  milestone_payment_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to finance.milestone_payment. Business justification: IP agreement milestones (contractual triggers) link to milestone payment records (financial transactions) for contract compliance verification, revenue/expense recognition per ASC 606, and audit trail']
  achieved_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the milestone trigger event was confirmed as achieved. Null if the milestone has not yet been achieved. Used for revenue recognition timing and partner notification.']
  clinical_phase varchar [note: 'Clinical development phase associated with a clinical milestone trigger event (Phase I, Phase II, Phase III, Phase IV). Applicable when milestone_type is \'clinical\'. Aligns with ICH E8 and FDA clinical trial phase definitions.']
  cost_center_code varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA CO cost center code associated with the business unit or function responsible for managing this milestone. Supports internal cost allocation and P&L reporting.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this milestone record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX.']
  currency_code varchar [note: 'Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the milestone payment amount (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, GBP). Determines the denomination of the contractual payment obligation.']
  dispute_reason varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the reason for a milestone or payment dispute, applicable when milestone_status is \'disputed\' or payment_status is \'disputed\'. Captures the nature of the disagreement for legal and deal management review.']
  due_date date [note: 'Contractually agreed date by which the milestone trigger event must occur or the milestone payment must be made, as specified in the agreement schedule. Used for deal management and partner relationship tracking.']
  exchange_rate decimal(18,6) [note: 'Foreign exchange rate applied to convert the milestone payment amount from the agreement currency to the functional currency at the time of recognition or payment. Sourced from SAP FI exchange rate tables.']
  functional_currency_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Milestone payment amount converted to the company\'s functional reporting currency (typically USD) using the exchange rate at the time of recognition. Supports consolidated financial reporting and SOX compliance.']
  gl_account_code varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA General Ledger account code to which the milestone payment revenue or expense is posted. Supports financial reporting, revenue recognition, and SOX audit trails.']
  legal_counsel_reference varchar [note: 'Reference identifier or name of the internal or external legal counsel responsible for advising on this milestone, including patent litigation or dispute resolution matters. Supports coordination with legal on milestone disputes.']
  licensed_product_name varchar [note: 'Name of the drug product, drug substance, or technology to which this milestone applies, as defined in the agreement. May reference the International Nonproprietary Name (INN), USAN, or internal compound code.']
  milestone_description varchar [note: 'Free-text description of the milestone event as defined in the agreement schedule, including specific conditions, indications, territories, or product formulations that must be met for the milestone to be triggered.']
  milestone_number varchar [note: 'Externally-known business identifier for this milestone, typically assigned during deal negotiation and referenced in the agreement schedule (e.g., MS-00012). Used in partner communications, SAP contract management, and Veeva Vault deal documents.']
  milestone_payment_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Gross contractual payment amount due upon achievement of this milestone, expressed in the agreement currency. Represents the base monetary obligation before any withholding tax or adjustments.']
  milestone_status varchar [note: 'Current lifecycle status of the milestone. Pending: not yet achieved; Achieved: trigger event confirmed and milestone met; Waived: contractually waived by mutual agreement; Disputed: counterparty disputes whether trigger conditions were met; Cancelled: milestone removed from agreement via amendment.']
  milestone_subtype varchar [note: 'Granular classification within the milestone type. Examples include: IND Submission, Phase I Completion, Phase II Completion, Phase III Completion, NDA Submission, NDA Approval, BLA Submission, BLA Approval, MAA Submission, MAA Approval, First Commercial Sale, Annual Net Sales Threshold, Orphan Drug Designation, Pediatric Exclusivity Grant. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND_submission|phase_I_completion|phase_II_completion|phase_III_completion|NDA_submission|NDA_approval|BLA_submission|BLA_approval|MAA_submission|MAA_approval|first_commercial_sale|net_sales_threshold|orphan_drug_designation|pediatric_exclusivity — promote to reference product]']
  milestone_type varchar [note: 'High-level classification of the milestone category. Regulatory milestones include IND/NDA/BLA/MAA submissions and approvals; clinical milestones cover Phase I/II/III completion; commercial milestones include first commercial sale and net sales thresholds; technical milestones cover manufacturing or formulation achievements; financial milestones cover upfront or equity events; legal milestones cover patent grants or litigation outcomes.']
  notification_date date [note: 'Date on which the achieving party formally notified the counterparty of milestone achievement, as required by the agreement. Relevant for triggering payment obligation timelines and dispute windows.']
  payment_direction varchar [note: 'Indicates whether the milestone payment is inbound (receivable — counterparty pays the company upon milestone achievement) or outbound (payable — the company pays the counterparty). Determines accounting treatment in SAP FI.']
  payment_due_date date [note: 'Date by which the milestone payment must be received, typically calculated as a fixed number of days after the notification date or achieved date per the agreement terms. Drives accounts receivable or payable scheduling in SAP FI.']
  payment_received_date date [note: 'Actual date on which the milestone payment was received or disbursed, as confirmed in the bank or SAP FI ledger. Null if payment has not yet been made.']
  payment_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the milestone payment obligation. Unpaid: milestone achieved but payment not yet invoiced; Invoiced: invoice raised in SAP FI; Paid: payment confirmed received or disbursed; Overdue: payment past due date; Disputed: payment amount or obligation under dispute.']
  regulatory_agency varchar [note: 'Regulatory authority whose action (e.g., IND acceptance, NDA/BLA/MAA approval) constitutes the trigger event for regulatory milestones. Applicable only to regulatory milestone types. Values include FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, NMPA, WHO, or other. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|EMA|MHRA|PMDA|NMPA|WHO|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  responsible_party varchar [note: 'Name of the party (licensor, licensee, or co-development partner) contractually responsible for achieving the milestone trigger event or making the milestone payment. Supports partner relationship management and deal accountability tracking.']
  revenue_recognition_flag boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the milestone payment has been recognized as revenue in the financial statements under ASC 606 / IFRS 15. True = revenue recognized; False = not yet recognized or deferred. Supports finance and SOX compliance reporting.']
  sales_threshold_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Annual or cumulative net sales threshold that must be reached to trigger a commercial sales-based milestone payment, expressed in the agreement currency. Applicable only to commercial milestone types with net sales triggers.']
  sap_invoice_number varchar [note: 'SAP S/4HANA FI invoice or billing document number generated upon milestone achievement and payment invoicing. Enables reconciliation between the IP milestone record and the financial accounting system.']
  sequence_number varchar [note: 'Ordinal sequence number of this milestone within the agreement, as defined in the agreement schedule (e.g., 1 = first milestone, 2 = second milestone). Supports ordered reporting and deal progress tracking.']
  submission_type varchar [note: 'Type of regulatory submission associated with a regulatory milestone trigger event. Applicable when milestone_type is \'regulatory\'. Values: IND (Investigational New Drug), NDA (New Drug Application), BLA (Biologics License Application), MAA (Marketing Authorization Application), sNDA (supplemental NDA), sBLA (supplemental BLA), or other. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: IND|NDA|BLA|MAA|sNDA|sBLA|other — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]']
  territory varchar [note: 'Geographic territory or jurisdiction in which the milestone trigger event must occur for the milestone to be payable (e.g., USA, EU, JPN, Worldwide). Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or named multi-country regions as defined in the agreement.']
  therapeutic_area varchar [note: 'Therapeutic area or disease indication to which the licensed product and this milestone apply (e.g., Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, Neuroscience). Supports portfolio analytics and deal management reporting.']
  trigger_event varchar [note: 'Specific contractual event or condition that triggers this milestone obligation, as defined in the agreement (e.g., \'Receipt of written FDA approval of NDA for Product X in the United States\', \'First patient dosed in Phase I clinical trial\'). Supports legal review and milestone verification.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this milestone record was last modified in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and change tracking requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and SOX.']
  veeva_vault_doc_reference varchar [note: 'Document identifier in Veeva Vault RIM or QualityDocs referencing the agreement schedule, milestone amendment, or supporting evidence document for this milestone. Enables traceability to the source controlled document.']
  withholding_tax_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Amount of withholding tax deducted from the milestone payment, as applicable under the governing tax treaty between the licensor and licensee jurisdictions. Recorded in SAP FI for tax compliance reporting.']

  Note: 'Tracks milestone events and payment obligations under licensing, co-development, and collaboration agreements tied to IP assets. Captures milestone type (regulatory filing, IND submission, Phase I completion, NDA approval, first commercial sale, sales threshold), milestone description, trigger event, due date, achieved date, milestone payment amount, currency, payment status, and responsible party. Supports deal management, revenue recognition, and partner relationship management.'

Table intellectual.patent_license {
  patent_license_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each patent-licensing agreement pairing. Primary key for the association.']
  licensing_agreement_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the licensing agreement under which this patent is licensed']
  patent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the patent being licensed under this agreement']
  diligence_obligations varchar [note: 'Narrative description of commercially reasonable efforts or best efforts diligence obligations specific to this patent (e.g., \'Licensee must file IND for Patent A compound within 18 months\'). May differ from agreement-level diligence if certain patents have accelerated or deferred development timelines.']
  enforcement_rights varchar [note: 'Identifies which party has the right to enforce this patent against third-party infringers during the license term. Licensor: licensor retains enforcement rights. Licensee: licensee has enforcement rights (common in exclusive licenses). Joint: both parties must agree. Licensee-First-Right: licensee has first right to enforce; licensor may enforce if licensee declines. May vary by patent within the same agreement.']
  exclusion_date date [note: 'Date on which this patent was removed from the licensing agreement, if applicable. May occur due to patent expiry, invalidation, amendment, or strategic decision to narrow the licensed portfolio. Null if the patent remains actively licensed.']
  exclusivity_type varchar [note: 'Scope of exclusivity granted for this specific patent within the agreement. Exclusive: licensee is the sole licensee globally or in the specified territory. Co-Exclusive: licensor may grant rights to a limited number of additional licensees. Non-Exclusive: licensor retains the right to license to others. Sole: licensee is the only licensee, but licensor retains rights to practice the patent. May vary by patent within the same agreement.']
  field_of_use varchar [note: 'Specific therapeutic area, indication, or application domain within which this patent is licensed under the agreement. May be narrower than the agreement-level field_of_use if certain patents are restricted to specific indications (e.g., Patent A for oncology only, Patent B for all indications). Stored as free text or controlled vocabulary (e.g., \'Oncology - NSCLC\', \'Immunology - Rheumatoid Arthritis\').']
  inclusion_date date [note: 'Date on which this patent was added to the licensing agreement. May be the agreement effective_date for patents included at execution, or a later date if patents were added via amendment or automatic inclusion clauses (e.g., all patents filed during the term are automatically included).']
  license_scope varchar [note: 'Defines the breadth of rights granted for this specific patent within the agreement. Full grants all rights; Limited restricts to specific claims or applications; Research-Only excludes commercial use; Commercial-Only excludes research use; Diagnostic-Only restricts to diagnostic applications. Scope may vary by patent within the same agreement.']
  license_status varchar [note: 'Current status of the license for this specific patent within the agreement. Active: license is in force. Suspended: temporarily paused due to breach, non-payment, or force majeure. Terminated: license ended prior to agreement expiry. Expired: license ended due to patent expiry or agreement expiry. Status may vary by patent within the same agreement.']
  maintenance_fee_responsibility varchar [note: 'Identifies which party is responsible for paying patent maintenance fees (annuities) for this specific patent during the license term. Licensor: licensor pays. Licensee: licensee reimburses or pays directly. Shared: costs split per agreement terms. May vary by patent within the same agreement.']
  patent_specific_milestone_value decimal(18,2) [note: 'Aggregate value of milestone payments specifically tied to this patent (e.g., regulatory approval milestone triggered only if this patent covers the approved product). Null if no patent-specific milestones exist. Complements agreement-level milestone tracking.']
  patent_specific_upfront_payment decimal(18,2) [note: 'One-time upfront payment allocated to this specific patent, if the agreement structure assigns value to individual patents (common in patent portfolio acquisitions or carve-out deals). Null if upfront payment is agreement-level only.']
  prosecution_control varchar [note: 'Identifies which party controls patent prosecution (filing, amendments, responses to office actions) for this specific patent during the license term. Licensor: licensor retains control. Licensee: licensee assumes control (common in exclusive licenses). Joint: both parties must agree. May vary by patent within the same agreement.']
  royalty_rate decimal(10,6) [note: 'Patent-specific royalty rate expressed as a decimal fraction of net sales (e.g., 0.035 for 3.5%). May differ from the agreement-level royalty_rate when certain patents command premium rates (e.g., composition-of-matter patents vs. formulation patents) or when royalty stacking applies. Null if this patent does not trigger royalty obligations.']
  sublicensing_permitted boolean [note: 'Indicates whether the licensee has the contractual right to sublicense this specific patent to third parties. May differ from the agreement-level sublicensing_permitted if certain high-value patents (e.g., composition-of-matter) are excluded from sublicensing rights while others are permitted.']
  territory varchar [note: 'Geographic territory or jurisdiction(s) in which this specific patent is licensed under the agreement. May be narrower than the agreement-level territory if certain patents are restricted to specific regions (e.g., US-only for composition patents, EU for formulation patents). Stored as ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes or region codes (e.g., \'USA\', \'EU\', \'APAC\', \'Global\').']

  Note: 'This association product represents the licensing relationship between a patent and a licensing agreement. It captures the specific terms, scope, and financial arrangements under which each patent is licensed within a broader agreement. Each record links one patent to one licensing agreement with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific patent-agreement pairing, such as territory-specific exclusivity, field-of-use restrictions, and patent-specific royalty rates that may differ from the agreement-level defaults.. Existence Justification: Patent licensing in pharmaceuticals is operationally many-to-many. A single patent (e.g., a composition-of-matter patent covering a blockbuster compound) is routinely licensed through multiple agreements—an exclusive license to Partner A for oncology indications in North America, a co-exclusive license to Partner B for autoimmune indications in Europe, and a non-exclusive license to Partner C for diagnostic use globally. Conversely, a single licensing agreement typically bundles multiple patents—composition patents, formulation patents, method-of-use patents, and process patents—to provide comprehensive IP coverage for a product or platform. Business development teams actively manage these patent-agreement pairings, negotiating patent-specific terms (territory, exclusivity, royalty rates, field-of-use restrictions) that vary within the same agreement.'
}

Table intellectual.blocking_patent_assessment {
  blocking_patent_assessment_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each blocking patent assessment record.']
  fto_analysis_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the FTO analysis in which this patent was identified and assessed.']
  patent_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to the third-party patent being assessed as a potential blocking patent in this FTO analysis.']
  assessing_attorney varchar [note: 'Name of the patent attorney or IP counsel who conducted the assessment of this specific patent within the FTO analysis. May differ from the overall conducting attorney if multiple attorneys divided the patent review workload.']
  assessment_date date [note: 'Date on which this specific patent was assessed within the FTO analysis. May differ from the overall FTO analysis date if patents were evaluated in phases or if the assessment was updated.']
  blocking_patent_count varchar [note: 'Total number of third-party patents identified during the FTO analysis as potentially blocking or relevant to the commercialization of the assessed product or technology. Key metric for risk quantification. [Moved from fto_analysis: This is an aggregate count that should be derived from the blocking_patent_assessment association table via COUNT() rather than stored redundantly in fto_analysis. Moving it eliminates data synchronization risk.]']
  blocking_patent_numbers varchar [note: 'Comma-separated list of patent publication or grant numbers (e.g., US10123456B2, EP3456789A1) identified as potentially blocking in the FTO analysis. Enables direct cross-referencing with patent databases and IP watch systems. [Moved from fto_analysis: This comma-separated list is a denormalized representation of the M:N relationship. The patent numbers should be retrieved via JOIN to the blocking_patent_assessment association and then to the patent table, eliminating redundancy and ensuring data consistency.]']
  claim_mapping varchar [note: 'Detailed mapping of specific patent claims (e.g., claims 1, 3, 7-12) to the company\'s product features, formulation elements, or process steps that may infringe. This is relationship-specific because it describes how THIS patent\'s claims read on THIS product/technology under analysis.']
  created_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this blocking patent assessment record was first created in the system.']
  design_around_strategy varchar [note: 'Narrative description of the proposed design-around approach to avoid infringement of this specific patent, such as alternative formulation, different synthesis route, modified dosing regimen, or alternative excipients. This is relationship-specific because the design-around is tailored to both the patent claims and the product under analysis.']
  invalidity_assessment varchar [note: 'IP counsel\'s assessment of potential grounds for challenging the validity of this patent (e.g., prior art references, obviousness arguments, enablement deficiencies). This is relationship-specific because invalidity strategy is developed in the context of the specific FTO analysis and product development timeline.']
  licensing_recommendation varchar [note: 'IP counsel\'s recommendation on whether a license should be pursued for this patent in the context of this FTO analysis. Values: required (license necessary to proceed), recommended (license advisable to mitigate risk), optional (license could reduce risk but not essential), not_required (no license needed). This is relationship-specific because licensing need depends on both the patent scope and the specific product/technology.']
  non_infringement_rationale varchar [note: 'Legal rationale explaining why the company\'s product or technology does not infringe this patent, citing specific claim limitations, product specifications, or process differences. This is relationship-specific because the non-infringement argument is tailored to both the patent claims and the product under analysis.']
  risk_level_per_patent varchar [note: 'IP infringement risk level assigned specifically to this patent within the context of this FTO analysis. Values: critical (immediate blocking threat), high (significant infringement risk), medium (moderate risk requiring monitoring), low (minimal risk), negligible (no material risk). This is relationship-specific because the same patent may pose different risk levels to different products or technologies.']
  updated_timestamp timestamp [note: 'Timestamp when this blocking patent assessment record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail and change tracking.']

  Note: 'This association product represents the evaluation of third-party patents that may block commercialization of company products or technologies. Each record links one third-party patent to one FTO analysis, capturing the IP counsel\'s assessment of infringement risk, claim mapping, design-around strategies, and licensing recommendations specific to that patent-analysis combination. This is a core operational entity in pharmaceutical IP risk management, actively created and maintained by patent attorneys during FTO assessments.. Existence Justification: In pharmaceutical IP risk management, FTO analyses routinely evaluate multiple third-party patents that may block commercialization, and each third-party patent may be assessed across multiple FTO analyses for different products or technologies. IP counsel creates blocking patent assessment records that capture patent-specific risk levels, claim mappings, design-around strategies, and licensing recommendations that exist only in the context of a specific patent-analysis combination. This is a recognized operational entity actively managed by patent attorneys.'
}

  tax_code varchar [note: 'SAP tax code associated with the GL account for VAT/GST and withholding tax determination. Relevant for pharmaceutical entities operating across multiple tax jurisdictions. Supports indirect tax reporting and compliance.']
  trading_partner varchar [note: 'Company code of the intercompany trading partner for balances involving intercompany transactions. Used to identify and eliminate intercompany balances during group consolidation. Populated only when intercompany_flag is True.']

  Note: 'Central repository for all financial accounting entries across the enterprise, representing the authoritative chart of accounts, account balances, and period-end ledger positions. Captures account master data (account number, account type, account group, currency), period balances (opening, debit totals, credit totals, closing balance by period), company code, profit center allocations, cost center references, and currency translations as sourced from SAP FI module. Serves as SSOT for trial balance, balance sheet, income statement, and SOX-compliant period-end close processes across all legal entities in the pharmaceutical group. Supports consolidation eliminations, multi-GAAP reporting (US GAAP and IFRS), and financial close status tracking. Does NOT own individual postings (owned by journal_entry) — owns aggregate balances and account structure.'
}

Table finance.journal_entry {
  journal_entry_id varchar [pk, note: 'Unique surrogate identifier for each journal entry record in the general ledger. Primary key for the journal_entry data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.']

  goods_receipt_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to procurement.goods_receipt. Essential for pharmaceutical inventory accounting, en']

  amount_transaction_currency decimal(18,2) [note: 'Gross monetary amount of the journal entry in the original transaction currency. For debit entries this is positive; for credit entries this is negative (SAP sign convention). Core monetary fact for the posting.']
  assignment_field varchar [note: 'SAP assignment field (ZUONR) used for sorting and matching open items in accounts payable, accounts receivable, and bank reconciliation. Typically populated with invoice number, payment reference, or contract number for automated clearing.']

  debit_credit_indicator varchar [note: 'SAP indicator specifying whether the line item is a debit (S=Soll/Debit) or credit (H=Haben/Credit) posting. Fundamental double-entry bookkeeping attribute required for GL balance validation and trial balance generation.']

  entry_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The exact date and time when the journal entry record was created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.']
  exchange_rate decimal(12,6) [note: 'Foreign currency exchange rate applied to translate the transaction currency amount to local currency at the time of posting. Sourced from SAP exchange rate tables per the applicable rate type (e.g., M=standard, B=bank buying rate).']
  fiscal_period varchar [note: 'The fiscal period (month 01–12, plus special periods 13–16 for year-end adjustments) within the fiscal year. Drives period-end close processes, P&L reporting by period, and financial close calendar management.']
  fiscal_year varchar [note: 'The fiscal year to which the journal entry belongs, as defined in the SAP fiscal year variant. Used for annual financial reporting, R&D capitalization tracking, and SOX compliance period assignment.']
  functional_area varchar [note: 'SAP functional area classifying the business function of the posting (e.g., R&D, Manufacturing, Sales & Distribution, General & Administrative). Supports cost-of-goods-sold (COGS) analysis and functional P&L reporting per IFRS.   gl_account varchar [note: 'SAP GL account number to which the journal entry line is posted. Determines the financial statement line item (P&L or balance sheet). Supports COGS by product, R&D capitalization, and therapeutic area P&L analysis.']
  header_text varchar [note: 'Free-text description at the journal entry header level explaining the business purpose of the posting (e.g., \'Q3 R&D accrual – Oncology Phase III\', \'API procurement – CMO settlement\'). Supports audit review and financial close documentation.']
  is_reversal boolean [note: 'Indicates whether this journal entry is itself a reversal of a prior posting (True) or an original entry (False). Used to filter reversals from net financial reporting and to identify accrual reversal patterns in period-end close.']
  last_changed_timestamp timestamp [note: 'The date and time when the journal entry was last modified or reversed. Supports change audit trail requirements under SOX Section 404 and 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records integrity.']
  line_item_number varchar [note: 'Sequential line item number within the journal entry document (e.g., 001, 002). Uniquely identifies each debit/credit line within the document for reconciliation, audit, and subledger matching.']
  line_item_text varchar [note: 'Free-text description at the individual line item level providing context for the specific debit or credit posting (e.g., \'API batch #XYZ123 – COGS\', \'Phase III trial accrual – CRO milestone\'). Supports granular audit review.']
  local_currency varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the company code\'s local (functional) currency. Used for statutory reporting in the country of the legal entity.']
  posting_date date [note: 'The date on which the journal entry is posted to the general ledger. Determines the fiscal period and year to which the transaction is assigned. Critical for period-end close and financial reporting.']
  posting_status varchar [note: 'Current workflow state of the journal entry in the general ledger lifecycle. \'posted\' = fully committed to GL; \'parked\' = saved but not posted; \'held\' = incomplete draft; \'reversed\' = offset entry created; \'cleared\' = matched against open items; \'blocked\' = pending approval.']
  profit_center varchar [note: 'SAP CO profit center representing the business unit or product line responsible for the financial result. Enables P&L reporting by therapeutic area (oncology, immunology, rare diseases), brand, and geography.']
  reference_document_number varchar [note: 'External reference number from the source document (e.g., vendor invoice number, purchase order number, contract reference, or regulatory submission reference). Enables cross-system reconciliation and audit traceability.']
  reversal_document_number varchar [note: 'Document number of the reversing journal entry if this posting has been reversed. Populated only for reversed entries; null otherwise. Supports audit trail completeness and period-end close validation.']
  subledger_type varchar [note: 'Identifies the subledger from which the journal entry originates: AP (Accounts Payable), AR (Accounts Receivable), asset accounting, tax accounting, material ledger, or none (direct GL posting). Enables subledger-to-GL reconciliation.']
  tax_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The calculated tax amount (VAT, GST, sales tax) in local currency for the journal entry line. Supports indirect tax return filing, tax provision calculations, and multi-jurisdiction tax compliance reporting.']
  tax_base_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'The taxable base amount in local currency on which the tax is calculated. Required for indirect tax return preparation and multi-jurisdiction VAT/GST compliance reporting.']
  tax_code varchar [note: 'SAP tax code identifying the applicable tax rate and type (e.g., VAT, sales tax, withholding tax) for the posting. Drives automatic tax calculation and links to tax jurisdiction for multi-jurisdiction indirect tax compliance.']
  tax_jurisdiction_code varchar [note: 'Code identifying the tax jurisdiction (country, state, county, city) applicable to the transaction for multi-jurisdiction indirect tax reporting. Required for US sales tax (Vertex/Avalara integration) and international VAT compliance.']
  tax_return_period varchar [note: 'The reporting period (YYYY-MM) to which this tax posting belongs for indirect tax return filing purposes. May differ from the accounting fiscal period; used for VAT/GST return preparation across multiple tax jurisdictions.']
  transaction_currency varchar [note: 'ISO 4217 three-letter currency code of the original transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY, GBP). The currency in which the business transaction was originally denominated, before conversion to local or group currency.']
  vat_classification varchar [note: 'Classification of the tax posting type for indirect tax reporting: input VAT (recoverable on purchases), output VAT (collected on sales), deferred VAT (timing difference), exempt, zero-rated, or not applicable. Supports multi-jurisdiction VAT compliance.']
  withholding_tax_amount decimal(18,2) [note: 'Amount of withholding tax (WHT) deducted at source for cross-border payments to vendors, royalty recipients, or service providers. Relevant for pharmaceutical royalty accounting, CRO/CMO payments, and international tax treaty compliance.']

  Note: 'Individual accounting transactions posted to the general ledger with full header and line-item detail, including tax-specific postings. Header captures posting date, document type, reference number, fiscal year/period, currency, and posting user. Line items capture GL account, cost center, profit center, debit/credit amounts in transaction and local currency, tax code, tax jurisdiction, taxable base amount, tax amount, withholding tax, assignment field, and line item text. Encompasses all subledger postings (AP, AR, asset, tax) and manual adjustments. Tax postings carry additional attributes: tax jurisdiction, tax return reference, VAT/sales tax/deferred tax classification, and indirect tax reporting period for multi-jurisdiction compliance. Supports audit trails required under SOX and 21 CFR Part 11, financial close processes, and granular P&L analysis by therapeutic area, brand, and geography.'
}

Existing created_by_user is username string; FK enables proper authorization controls, Gx']
  plant_id varchar [note: 'Reference to the manufacturing plant or facility associated with this internal order. Relevant for CAPEX orders tied to facility investments or manufacturing overhead orders. Corresponds to WERKS in SAP AUFK.']

  supply_contract_id varchar [note: 'Foreign key linking to procurement.supply_contract. Business justification: R&D and clinical trial internal orders frequently reference master supply agreements for CMO/CRO services and materials procurement. Essential for cost tracking against contracted rates, budget vs. ac']

Represents the authorized spending limit for the R&D program, capital project, or overhead activity. Used for budget vs. actual variance analysis and availability control.']

Typically set to True for Phase 3 clinical development orders meeting the six IAS 38 criteria. Drives R&D capitalization tracking and CAPEX lifecycle governance.']

Represents future obligated spend. Sourced from SAP CO commitment management (COOI table). Critical for total exposure reporting.']
